items.statement: Management aims for consistent double-digit revenue growth in the medium term
items.quote: Our endeavor in the medium term is, you know, as I'd indicated to some other participant was that we want to get to a consistent double-digit revenue growth.

items.statement: ERP implementation went live on April 1 with zero business disruption
items.quote: In fact, kudos to the team. There has been zero disruption on that front.

items.statement: Floats reached almost mid-single-digit contribution with 16,000 pairs average weekly sales
items.quote: Floats continues to power at a very high level, and now it's reached almost mid-single-digit contribution, almost doubling for the quarter. 16,000 pairs average weekly sales

items.statement: Gross margin protected reasonably well despite tough trading conditions
items.quote: The last chart on margins, gross margin was protected reasonably well, I would say during this quarter, despite the tough trading conditions

items.statement: No price increases for almost five to six quarters since mid-second half of FY22-23
items.quote: We have refrained from price increases now for the almost five quarters or a little more, maybe six quarters now. So middle of, let's say, second half of '22, '23.

items.statement: Demand improved from January to March but sustainability unclear; optimistic medium term
items.quote: we did see an improvement during the quarter from a Jan which was actually much worse, but to March which was a little better, but still not giving us complete clarity

items.statement: Premium brands (Hush Puppies, Power, Nordstar, Comfit) contribute ~40% of turnover; premium defined as >Rs2,000 MRP
items.quote: They will cumulatively account for almost something like 40% of our turnover.

items.statement: Mass segment below Rs700 MRP remains sensitive; distribution business still a drag on growth
items.quote: the mass segment, which is an MRP, which is below INR700, consumers are extremely sensitive to it. And that did create its own, how do you say, struggle from a consumption point of view

items.statement: Marketing spend at ~260 bps for FY24; H2 run rate to continue in FY25 with potential increase
items.quote: The second half run rate. Yes, broadly ballpark, yes, we will run with that run rate. And in fact, we might want to invest a little more.

items.statement: Franchise store additions to dominate at 80-20 ratio vs COCO; target 40 doors per quarter run rate
items.quote: We will have predominant franchise store additions, which is in the ratio of 80-20. Does that answer your question?

items.statement: Industry growth estimated at GDP plus inflation (~low double-digits); aim to edge ahead of industry
items.quote: The industry growth estimates based on various inputs that we get, but I mean, nominally speaking, it should be GDP growth plus the inflation, minimal, and that works out to almost low-double digits in those lines.

items.statement: Global sugar consumption growth for 2023-24 revised up to 1.2% from 0.9%; 2024-25 balance revised to 278,000 MT deficit from small surplus
items.quote: Annual growth of global sugar consumption for 2023-24 season is now estimated at 1.2% compared with earlier estimate of 0.9%. For 2024-25 season, the sugar supply and demand balance has been revised downwards from an initial estimate of small surplus of 27,000 metric tons to 278,000 metric tons of deficits.

items.statement: India sugar production estimated at 323 LMT for 2023-24 season; closing stock ~90 LMT by Sep 2024 vs 2.5 months consumption norm
items.quote: Hence, the final net sugar production is estimated to be 323 LMT for sugar season '23-'24. Taking into account an opening stock of approximately 56 LMT, as on 1st October 2023, and a forecasted domestic consumption of 285 LMT, the closing stock is estimated to be approximately 90 LMT by September '24.

items.statement: No volume or revenue guidance given; FY25 cane planting dipped in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka okay, AP marginal dip
items.quote: We don't sort of give guidance on any of our volumes or revenues, but this is the broader picture for you.

items.statement: Distillery EBITDA margin FY24 ~12% vs 9% FY23; would have been 16-17% without policy change; aspire to 20%
items.quote: So this impacted our overall distillery EBITDA margin on a full year basis, probably at around 12%. Wh ile this has improved from FY'23 of 9%, if there was perhaps no change in the policy framework, the EBITDA margins would have been closer to 16% and perhaps on track to move closer to 20

items.statement: Refinery spread improved ~$10 PMT, cost reduced $3 PMT; posted cash profit INR12 cr in FY24
items.quote: Refinery business volume has grown by 16% and the spread also has improved about $10 PMT and cost reduced by $3 PMT and this has resulted in the refinery posting a cash profit of INR12 crores.

items.statement: Consumer business targets late single-digit EBITDA margin over 5 years; value-added products target gross margin >35%
items.quote: At steady state, and I think we're some years away from that if you look at this business as a P&L, we need to be in the late single-digit EBITDA on an ideal basis.

items.statement: Distillery expansion 165 KLPD at Haliyal and Nellikuppam to operate full stream by Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the year, expansion in distillery of 165 KLPD in Haliyal and Nellikuppam had reached greater degree of completion and will operate in full stream by Q1 of FY25.

items.statement: Distillery price realization Q4 INR64.49/litre vs INR62.56/litre YoY
items.quote: As far as price realization is concerned, the price realization in Q4 is INR64.49 per litre against pr evious year realization of INR62.56 per litre

items.statement: Sugar MSP at INR31/kg unchanged while FRP rising; management urges MSP relook
items.quote: The MSP has stayed at INR31 a kilo, while the FRP has moved up on a year-on-year basis for a number of years. So, I think it would be really positive for all stakeholders if the MSP is relooked at.

items.statement: Standalone debt ~INR1,000 cr (INR300 cr long-term for projects, INR750 cr short-term for inventory); expected to reduce by Sep 2024
items.quote: out of INR1000 crores, INR300 crores is long-term in nature, which is for the projects which are underway and is getting commercialized in a quarter. So, as far as the short-term is concerned, it is about INR750 crores or so, and this majorly is on account of inventory increase, compared to the 31st March 2023. So, the debt is stretched around INR1000 crores, but gradually it will come down by Sep

items.statement: Retail branded sugar sales crossed INR500 cr; value-added (Amrit, jaggery) 4% of retail volume; aim to grow value-added share aggressively
items.quote: Retail overall this year was about 28% of our sale in terms of volume, the value-added portion of that, we will aspire to grow aggressively because it's a sterilization of retail over the coming year.

items.statement: Nutraceuticals under strategic review; open to alliances for value creation; no news currently
items.quote: As I said, nutra is under strategic review and we're always going to be open to looking at alliances which are going to create value for the business. So, I think that's kind of where we are right now.

items.statement: Refinery strategic partner search ongoing; open to alliances; no news to discuss
items.quote: We are always open to alliances for value creation and if we have any news at all we'll make appropriate intimations, but there's no news to discuss at this point in time.

items.statement: Global sugar prices fallen to late teens cents/lb from ~27 cents 6-9 months ago; export viability challenged even if policy allows
items.quote: Six to nine months ago, they were probably closer to [£0.27 cents per pound]. I think they're well into the late teens right now on account of surpluses in the global sugar balance. So, I think we must take note of that.

items.statement: Cogen power generation Q4 1,741 lakh units vs 2,034 lakh units YoY; exports 903 vs 1,060 lakh units; avg tariff INR4.84 vs INR5.11/unit
items.quote: As far as the cogen is concerned, we generated power in Q4 of about INR1741 lakhs units against the previous year of INR2,034 lakhs units. As far as the power exports is concerned, we did around INR903 lakhs units against the previous year, which was INR1,060 lakhs units. Average power tariff has come at INR4.84 paisa per unit as against the previous year of INR5.11 paisa per unit.

items.statement: Nutraceuticals standalone loss in FY24 due to Europe certification issues; expected to resolve near future
items.quote: The standalone Nutraceuticals Division had registered loss during the year on account of certification issues in Europe. However, such certification issues are expected to be resolved in the near future.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 is 525-560 bps above FY24 level
items.quote: we're looking at a margin outlook for fiscal 25 guiding in the range of 525 north to 550, 560. And on that, if you look at the overall EBITDA margin, we're expecting a jump in EBITDA margin from the full year of fiscal 24.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY25 is 5-10%
items.quote: I believe our guidance going forward between 5% and 10% growth is at the back of gradually exiting but largely focusing on good quality customers going deeper but keeping our focus on EBITDA growth from where we are at this time.

items.statement: Targeting 10% operating margin over next couple of years
items.quote: Our goal is to reach about 10% operating margin, and we are clearly focused over the next couple of years to get there.

items.statement: Total order backlog is $470 million as of March 2024, down from $490 million in December 2023
items.quote: Just to highlight, on an order backlog across our various solutions and services and projects is US $470 million as on March 24 as against an order backlog of US $490 million as in December 23.

items.statement: Pipeline is close to $2 billion, strong in networking and data center solutions
items.quote: And our pipeline, of course is very strong, specifically in our networking and our data center solutions business. It's close to $2 billion at this time.

items.statement: Data center capacity expected to nearly double from 17 GW to 35 GW over next 5-7 years
items.quote: The current requirement for a data center over the next several years, 5-7 years, is for the current capacity of data center will increase from the current 17 gigawatts to about 35 gigawatts.

items.statement: Actively working with three of five major hyperscalers on data center projects
items.quote: Currently, we are working on active projects with three out of the five major hyperscalers.

items.statement: Pivoting away from long-tail customers (90% revenue from top 50) to focus on top 250-300 accounts
items.quote: We are reorganizing ourselves to be able to serve large logos, Fortune 500 customers across enterprise and across hyperscalers, data center market and so on and so forth. Now, the larger customers have a little longer lead time to work on.

items.statement: Data center revenue grew from ~$15-20M three years ago to $110-115M in FY24 (~20% YoY growth)
items.quote: About three years ago, our revenue from the data center was about $15 million or $20 million. And in fiscal '22, we did about $70 -odd million. In fiscal 23, we did about $90 -odd million. The year that we exited, we've done about $110 million-$115 million in that range.

items.statement: TPS business contributes 12-13% of revenue, expected to remain in that range
items.quote: So, the TPS business contributes currently about between 12% and 13%. We expect the contribution to remain in that range going forward.

items.statement: Center of Excellence in Bangalore matured after 2 years of investment, driving productivity gains
items.quote: The second of course, our ability now to have our Center of Excellence in India support us because it's mature now we put the investment for the last 2 years time. So, we are able to get better productivity from our Center of Excellence in India that allows us to have better margin.

items.statement: Higher US interest costs caused slight miss on FY24 profitability target
items.quote: Our strong operating performance has led to increased profitability despite higher interest costs due to the interest rate environment in US. However, these high interest costs which we have incurred in fiscal year have caused us to slightly miss our profitability target and t he guidance for

items.statement: Customer decision-making delays affected short-term revenue growth and order bookings
items.quote: There was some shrinkage when compared to December 23 order backlog due to slow decision making on project orders and consistent execution of projects at our end on a quarter -on-quarter basis led to lower than anticipated order bookings.

items.statement: No active inorganic pipeline but will pursue accretive opportunities for market depth or portfolio expansion
items.quote: We will continue to look at inorganic opportunities, but we want to be economically accretive for us and not be emotional about that. So currently, we do not have an active pipeline, but as I said, we will continue to look at if it makes sense.

items.statement: India revenue contribution expected to stay at 6-7% while exploring data center and large infrastructure opportunities
items.quote: From a percentage perspective as we grow, I do not see a massive change in terms of contribution of revenue of 6%, 7% as we scale up. But clearly, we see growth as well in that market, most specifically exploring data center or supporting other large-scale infrastructure that is getting built.

items.statement: Expect 50% to 60% growth on pharma side in current year
items.quote: we're looking at, at the moment, 50% to 60% growth on the pharma side in the current year as well.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve year-on-year over next two to three years
items.quote: yes, we expect margins to go up and in the next two to three years, you will see margins year-on-year improving

items.statement: No substantial capex planned for FY25; focus on improving utilization
items.quote: We are not looking at any substantial capex as of now as we speak. There will be some small capexes which we will be doing. But our focus is going to be on improving utilization level

items.statement: Additional capex of $15-20 million over next 6-7 years to scale from 25-30M to 60-70M devices
items.quote: I think the additional capex in the range of, I would say, somewhere in the range of between $15 and $20 million will be -- is what we're looking at additional capex

items.statement: Confirmed orders from three customers in Q4 FY24: two for Semaglutide, one for Lanreotide
items.quote: In the Healthcare division, we have received confirmed business orders from three customers, two for Semaglutide and one for Lanreotide in the last quarter.

items.statement: Total ongoing projects across all molecules: 20 to 23
items.quote: Sanjay Shah: Yes, I'd say about 20 to 23.

items.statement: Auto injector projects: 4; balance are pen injectors
items.quote: So auto injectors, we have a total of four projects and balance are on pen injectors.

items.statement: Proprietary devices share increased from 10% to 30-40% of volumes over 3 years
items.quote: contract manufacturing, for example, is 3 years ago, contract manufacturing was 90% and proprietary devices were 10%. I'd say today, the split would be somewhere 70%-30% or 60%-40%.

items.statement: Expect US/EU approvals for injection pen platforms in current financial year before end of calendar year
items.quote: We're very confident that these approvals will come in, in the current financial year before the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Commercial supplies for Teriparatide (Axiom pen) started; Liraglutide commercial supplies expected in current year
items.quote: we started commercial supplies for Teriparatide, which is our Axiom pen. And we're starting -- we are looking at starting some commercial supplies of our Liraglutide pen as well in the current year

items.statement: Semaglutide RoW market launches targeted for calendar 2026 (FY27)
items.quote: most of our customers would be targeting '26, which is basically FY'27, but calendar '26 launch in these markets.

items.statement: Pen/device volumes: 11-12 million in FY24; expect 17-18 million in FY25 (15-16% growth)
items.quote: We're looking at -- like I said, we're looking at about 15%, 16% growth. So, I anticipate somewhere around to 17 million to 18 million pens in the clinical devices in the current year.

items.statement: No significantly adverse USFDA comments received on device-related queries
items.quote: Have we have received any significantly adverse comments? No. We have not yet received any significantly adverse comments that I'm aware of.

items.statement: GLP-1 pens give higher margins than insulin; not 3-4x difference
items.quote: GLP-1 will certainly give you higher margins than insulin. I don't think it's going to be 3, 4x.

items.statement: Carbon Steel business near EBITDA breakeven; expect breakeven in current year
items.quote: EBITDA level, I would say we have not broken even, but we are at a very borderline thing, and we should be able to breakeven in the current year.

items.statement: Expects better situation in second half of FY25 if anti-dumping duty comes into play by 1st October
items.quote: We are doing our best and in case the duty comes into play by 1st of October, which is what we are expecting, the situation in second half could be better from that perspective.

items.statement: Planning to spend over INR100 crores in FY25 on balancing equipment, captive solar-wind hybrid, and furnace rebuild preparation
items.quote: See, this year, we are planning to spend over INR100 crores in capex and this is for balancing equipment, which is required now because the type of glass, which is being demanded by the customers in order to make that to manufacture that we need to spend this capex.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR1,100-plus crores for capacity expansion put on hold pending duty structure visibility
items.quote: So we decided purposely to wait for right duty structure to be in place before we can move into this large project of say INR1,100-plus crores.

items.statement: Filing draft letter of offer to SEBI for rights issue; Board approved raising up to INR750 crores via equity, convertible securities, warrants, QIP, or preferential issue
items.quote: Finally, the company is filing around to file the draft letter of offer to SEBI to raise funds by a rights issue of equity shares. The proceeds will be utilized mainly to reduce the debt for the Indian operations as well as at the operating subsidiaries. The Board has also approved further raising of funds through the issuance of instruments of security, including equity shares or any other securi

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin declined to 12.1% from 25.7% in FY23 due to dumping and price erosion
items.quote: Consequently, the EBITDA during financial year 2024 was INR18.93 crores, corresponding to a margin of 12.1%, which was a steep decline compared to an EBITDA margin of 25.7% in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Average selling price fell 20.2% to INR109 per mm per sqm in FY24; Q4 FY24 price fell 25.6% YoY to INR98.8 per mm per sqm
items.value: INR109 per millimeter per square meter
items.quote: Average selling prices during the year were about INR109 per millimeter per square meter, a serious decline of 20.2% as compared to INR136.5 per millimeter per square meter during the previous year.

items.statement: Import freight rates from China to India rose from $700 to $3,200, improving landed cost of imports and domestic realizations
items.quote: The import freight rate into India from China has gone up from about $700 to about $3,200. And therefore, this may have a positive impact on our selling prices.

items.statement: Indian solar installations grew to 15 GW in FY24 from 12.8 GW; ALMM implementation from 1 April 2024 driving domestic module manufacturing and glass demand
items.quote: Firstly, solar installations in India last year were 15 gigawatts, an impressive growth over the previous year's insta llations of 12.8 gigawatts. Secondly, after some hesitant steps, the government has firmly implemented the ALMM mechanism on 1st April 2024, which mandates use of only ALMM -certified modules in the projects being installed in India

items.statement: 2mm glass now 20-25% of portfolio, expected to reach 60-65% by end of FY25; large-format glass now 90% of module manufacturer requirements
items.quote: This 2-millimeter glass is now almost 20% - 25% of our portfolio and which will soon become almost 60%- 65% by end of this year. So this is very much the requirement now. And also, the other thing, what we have done is to come up quickly is the large-format glass because there's a demand for larger module which started to become very popular. We have been abl e to introduce the large size of glass

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty applications accepted by DGTR; investigation ongoing, decisions expected in 5-6 months; customs duty exemption extended to 30 September 2024
items.quote: Our applications for DGTR in this regard have been prima facie accepted and already taken up for investigation. The government is now fully seized of the matter, and satisfactory decisions are expected to follow, perhaps in the next 5, 6 months.

items.statement: German subsidiary GMV resumed full production from mid-March 2024 after order cancellations in H2 FY24; export inquiries improving
items.quote: As informed in the last call, the company had temporarily slowed down production due to paucity of orders. Meanwhile, GMV has made inroads in other export markets to fill the gap created by a low domestic demand and has been able to resume full production from the middle of March this year.

items.statement: Negotiating additional solar-wind hybrid captive power plant with expected commissioning in H1 FY26
items.quote: We are negotiating an additional color placement hybrid drop at with expected commissioning during first half of financial year 2025, '26. This will not only save cost for us but will also enable us to meet a major portion of our demand for electricity from captive sources of renewable energy.

items.statement: GMV in Germany restarted second production line in late March 2024 and continues to receive enough export and domestic orders to run both lines fully
items.quote: Sometime in the last week of March, we got enough orders to start the second production line. And fortunately, we are continuing to get orders, export orders, domestic orders enough to continue to use both production lines fully.

items.statement: US demand starting in small way, expected to ramp up later in 2024 as plants start volume production, raising export demand from India
items.quote: Demand in the U.S.A. has started in a small way. We expect this to go up in the later part of this year as some of plants start volume production and ramp up operations. This will raise export demand from India.

items.statement: Company has batch house ready for 2,000 tons/day and electrical infrastructure in place, enabling faster furnace commissioning (14-24 months) if expansion approved
items.quote: We have a batch house. It's a very expensive component of the entire solar glass manufacturing plant, which is up and ready already for 2,000 tons. So if we set up another furnace, we do not need to spend any money on the batch house. We'll be saving money on the capital. The second thing, the entire electrical installation is already ready with us.

items.statement: Expect capacity utilization around 75% on 100,000-ton capacity in FY25, could reach 80% if market improves
items.quote: Yes, in the region of 75%, more like 75%. It could go to 80% if the market picks up a little bit. But at this moment, I'll probably say 75%.

items.statement: TACC anode project capex INR1,600-1,800 crores over next 18 months
items.quote: So for the anode, so at least the overall capex for the project that we are envisaging is between INR1,600 crores and INR1,800 crores depending on the final selection of technology, et cetera, how much power we need to take, how much -- we are still kind of contemplating between 48-kilometer 250 kVA line or whether we can make do with a 133 kVA line, that changes the entire dynamics. But between I

items.quote: We hope to see marginal improvement in steel production towards second half of 2024, which should result in increase in demand of electrodes. The positive for our industry is that the decarbonization has now become an irreversible process with more and more electric arc furnaces being announced every month. Till date, as per our information, more than 90 million tons of greenfield capacities have

items.quote: only that reduction in the selling price quarter-on-quarter basis. Nothing more than that. Pradeep Rawat: Yes. And what's the reason driving the reduction in selling price? Manish Gulati: There is no -- that is the degrowth of steel production between '22 and '23, which is, I mean, resulting in slowdown of demand and all the -- ou r peer group not being fully utilized. So that is why -- I mean, al

items.statement: Revenue split roughly 70-75% UHP grade electrodes, balance HP/non-UHP
items.quote: See, if you -- in the portion of our business, it's roughly, I would say, 70% to 75% of UHP and balance of HP grade electrodes -- I mean, non-UHP electrodes.

items.statement: Next 2-3 quarters may see margins under pressure; demand recovery hoped for H2 2024 onwards
items.quote: The next 2, 3 quarters may see margins remaining under some pressure but we are hoping that the demand will come back sometime in second half of 2024 onwards and we're now fully equipped to take advantage of our expanded capacity.

items.statement: TACC capex funded by INR750 crores cash in Greentech, INR80 crores already invested, INR250-300 crores Bhilwara Energy dividends, balance INR400-500 crores debt
items.quote: So like we mentioned earlier, around 700 -- arou nd INR80 crores of it has already been funded by HEG in terms of the land and the basic civil work that have started. There's around INR750 crores, which will be left in the balance sheet of the HEG Greentech company, which will be used for funding this. We will have a dividend in Bhilwara Energy of easily close to around INR200 crores or INR300 cro

items.statement: Bhilwara Energy hydro valuation INR3,000 crores (51% stake = INR1,500 crores); HEG's 49% share = INR750 crores; TACC valued at INR292 crores for INR80 crores invested
items.quote: So TACC value will be around INR292 crores, as Puneet said. Puneet Anand: Riju Jhunjhunwala: For INR80 crores of money that HEG has put in today. It's a 100% subsidiary of HEG. And the new Greentech company will own 100% of TACC. It will not be 29%, it will 100% of TACC, the new Greentech company

items.statement: Needle coke prices corrected in line with electrode prices; no inventory overhang; no NRV hits taken unlike peers
items.quote: No. See, currently, there is no shortage. There's no problem at all. As the electrode prices have dropped in the last 6, 7 quarters, so have been needle coke prices dropped. So if you are talking about the margin being the difference of the selling price of electrode versus the buying price of needle coke, it hasn't changed much. It has kept pace with the drop in the electrode prices. And this is

items.statement: Global graphite electrode demand expected to grow 150,000-200,000 tons by 2030 (ex-China) from current 500,000-550,000 tons; no new Western capacity announced
items.quote: As we have said in our earlier calls, we expect graphite demand to increase gradually by around 150,000 to 200,000 tons by 2033 -- 2030, which is a significant increase over current demand of about 500,000 to 550,000 tons, excluding China. Other than HEG, no new capacity has yet been announced in the Western world. It takes at least 4 to 5 years to build a new greenfield capacity and about 2 to 3

items.statement: HEG Graphite to retain 20MW Tawa hydro power and cash for dividend, expansion leftovers, safety capital; Greentech gets BEL 49%, TACC 100%, RePlus
items.quote: One will be the HEG Graphite company, which will have the HEG Limited, which is 100,000 tons graphite plant and the captive 20-megawatt power – Tawa hydroelectric power units and enough cash in its balance sheet to fund dividend for this year and the leftovers from the expansion and some kind of safety capital as we might call it. And the leftover company would be renamed to, let's say, HEG Greent

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 18-23% excluding smart meters; smart meter revenue expected INR400-500 crore if orders materialize
items.quote: Excluding the smart meters, we expect to grow anywhere between 18% and 23% in the coming year. Smart meter business sales will be over and above that.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin target of 10.5-11% excluding smart meters, up ~100 bps from current level
items.quote: EBITDA margins, we have improved to around 70 basis points this year compared to last year. So we expect this to go up by another 1 percentage point in the coming year.

items.statement: Industrial Switchgear expected to grow 22-23%, Wire & Cable 18-20%, Building Products ~40% in FY25
items.quote: industry switched gear business should be growing at around 22%- 23% this year. Copper wire and cable business should be growing b etween 18% and 20%. A building segment, we are expecting that it will grow by around 40

items.statement: FY25 capex limited to maintenance INR17-20 crore; smart meter plant capex ~INR40 crore mostly done in FY24
items.quote: I think there's no major capex because we have done our smart meter capex almost 70% this year. So the balance will be done next year. Other than this, there is no major capex, and we will be doing the maintenance capex of approximately INR17 crores-INR20 crores.

items.statement: Smart meter facility 80% installed, trial production started, commercial production expected June-July; capacity 40 lakh meters/year, may double to 80 lakh with additional INR40 crore capex
items.quote: Right now t he factory installation of the factory is almost 80% complete, and we are running trial production starting June. And we are in discussion with various customers and we are submitting samples to the customers

items.statement: Smart meter order pipeline unclear; initial orders may range 10,000 to 10 lakh meters depending on customer readiness
items.quote: It can start anywhere between 10,000 and it can go up to 1 lakh or 10 lakhs, depending on how our customers are capable of buying and installing.

items.statement: Smart meter EBITDA margin expected 12-15% in first year, targeting ~15% at steady state
items.quote: But I'm optimistic, if we are able to do this first year, and the EBITDA margin is not 15 %, I think definitely, it will be between 12% and 15% for the first year.

items.statement: EV charger business targets 18-20% EBITDA margin if technology and demand materialize
items.quote: We actually projected an EBITDA margin close to 18% to 20% if everything goes well in the charger business.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on global demand; mega shift to clean energy and India infrastructure/digitalization driving growth
items.quote: We are witnessing a mega shift towards clean energy on a global scale, which is posting significant investments in renewable energy projects across the world.

items.statement: Smart meter facility BIS certified for single-phase; three-phase certification by end-June; backward integrated with existing Coimbatore factories
items.quote: We successfully developed smart meters and the smart meter facility and received BIS certification for our single phase smart energy meter.

items.statement: EV charger failed ARAI communication test due to DIN vs ISO standard mismatch; software fix underway, hardware unchanged
items.quote: The DIN standards are working fine, but the ISO standards are not working properly because the standard that the charger was developed is for Europe. Unfortunately, it is not complementing the Indian standards.

items.statement: Smart meter sales to AMISPs with DISCOM orders; also hold AMISP license to bid directly for DISCOM tenders
items.quote: Right now, I think our focus is to manufacture meters sell to the AMISPs, those who have already taken orders from DISCOM.

items.statement: Export share ~27% in Q4, ~25% for FY24; targeting Russia as large new market, also Australia, New Zealand, Middle East

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 11.1%, down from FY23 due to elevated raw material prices
items.quote: EBITDA for FY24 declined by 16.4% to Rs. 70.6 crores compared to Rs. 84.4 crores in FY23 impacted on account of elevated raw material prices. EBITDA margin stood at 11.1%.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin similar to Q1 FY24 level in near term
items.quote: So in my opinion, more or less the margin would be in the line of what we had in the Q1.

items.statement: Historical 15-16% EBITDA margin not achievable currently
items.quote: I don't see any chances, because the cost increase has been very high, its price reduction has not yet happened that is one thing and second is the prices at what we were operating earlier and the prices now what we are operating there is a huge difference that is number two.

items.statement: Value-added products contributed 15% of revenue in FY24
items.quote: In FY24, value-added products contributed 15% of revenue and we aim for 25% in FY25

items.statement: FY25 maintenance capex Rs. 8-10 crores; Wada plant may need Rs. 50-60 crores extra if land cleared
items.value: Rs. 8 crores to Rs. 10 crores and other than that , I think if that Wada things goes through, then there may be Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores extra
items.quote: Normal would be Rs. 8 crores to Rs. 10 crores and other than that , I think if that Wada things goes through, then there may be Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores extra.

items.statement: Wada plant commissioning in FY26, Odisha plant in FY27
items.quote: As we said earlier, we stand on the same only , Wada would be in FY26 and Odisha will be in FY27.

items.statement: FY24 capacity utilization 72% vs 68% in FY23
items.quote: Our capacity utilization for FY24 stood at 72% compared to 68% in FY23.

items.statement: FY24 price increase ~5%, volume growth ~2%
items.quote: The total volume is 6% to 7% and price increase is 5%.

items.statement: Raw material prices stabilized; not yet back to previous low levels
items.quote: As I said, the prices are stabilized, it is not increasing number one. It has not gone back to that level, that level is still far.

items.statement: Forex increased 3% last year; may offset raw material savings
items.quote: if you see last year , the FOREX has increased by 3%. if that is also going up, whatever the reduction is happening on account of the raw material prices will again go back to the forex increase.

items.statement: Value-added products are non-asbestos tiles, planks, water repellent products sold through same dealers
items.quote: Value-added product is the non -asbestos product, where we s ell lot of tiles, planks, and water repellent product

items.statement: No known competitor capacity expansions announced
items.quote: I don't have any knowledge of anybody has announced any capacity expansion so far.

items.statement: Asbestos sheets ~60% cheaper than metal sheets per meter
items.quote: See the prices for raw material is around Rs. 200 to Rs. 220 per meter, compared to that the metal sheet is around Rs. 500 to Rs. 520. So that is what the difference, so I think 60% cheaper comparatively.

items.statement: Total debt Rs. 116 crores, now Rs. 67 crores; average interest rate 8.5%
items.quote: Total debt we have in the books is Rs. 116 crores, which is now Rs. 67 crores and average rate of interest would be 8.5%.

items.statement: Started term loan repayment in Q1 FY25; ICRA reaffirmed A-/A2+ ratings
items.quote: We also started making repayment of term loan during the first quarter of FY25. ICRA has also reaffirmed the long-term rating A- and short-term rating A2+.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs. 1 per share (face value Rs. 10) for FY24
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs.1 per equity share of the face value of Rs. 10 for the financial year ending 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Margin recovery depends on demand improvement, price hikes, and forex stability
items.quote: There would be definitely improvement in the EBITDA margin, but side by side we have to see how the FOREX is working because if you see last year , the FOREX has increased by 3%.

name: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Ltd

items.statement: Expects calendar year 2024 CV production to be flat, FY25 single-digit growth, company to outperform OE by ~10%, exports to grow 15-20%, aftermarket low double-digit growth
items.quote: Current year, if you look at the calendar year, we expect our projection is about minus 3% versus last year a very good production. We expect after the election because in the last 2 to 3 months the demand was subdued somewhat for various reasons.

items.statement: Export of compressors expected to grow from INR 250 crores to INR 500 crores in next 2-3 years based on clear pipeline and orders
items.quote: So, this, from a level of INR 250 crores last year, we expect this to go to INR 500 crores in a matter of next two to three years. We have a clear pipeline, these are all based on specific orders and with a clear execution plan.

items.statement: Export of actuators and brake chambers expected to grow from INR 400 crores to INR 450 crores next year
items.quote: From about INR 400 crores here, we expect the volume to increase to INR 450 Crores next year. This is the second product line.

items.statement: Export of air supply units for BMW expected to grow from INR 250 crores to INR 300 crores
items.quote: Again, from INR 250 crores, we expect that to grow to INR 300 crores. So, all areas we are only looking at growth.

items.statement: Need to invest about INR 120 crores before March 2025 to meet PLI commitments, subject to customer nominations for advanced technologies
items.quote: In order to meet that commitment, we need to invest about another INR 120 crores before March 2025. We are working on many projects. We are trying to comply with that subject to customers giving nomination, etc., for some of the advanced technologies.

items.statement: Export order book supports 15% growth in FY25 exports
items.quote: Yes, I see at least 15% growth based on the order inflow that is there with us. Yes, it takes about 15% growth.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin at 19.4%, PBT at 16% of product sales
items.quote: Our EBITDA for this quarter is 19.4% and for FY 2023-24 is at 19.4%.

items.statement: Content per vehicle currently ~INR 45,000, expected to at least double in 2-3 years with ESC, EBS, ADAS, e-mobility adoption
items.quote: Current content, Jaya raj is in the range of about INR 45,000 as a total combining all that including trailers and everything put together. The next 2 to 3 years, if you look in India the advanced technologies are yet to fully get adopted.

items.statement: ESC delta content ~INR 30,000 per bus; e-compressor ~INR 85,000-100,000 per electric bus; EBS similar range to ESC
items.quote: The delta content, you may take probably in the range of INR 30,000.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 CV production (>6T) de-grew 7.2% due to OEM inventory reduction; company OE sales grew 0.8% outperforming market by 8%
items.quote: In Q4, the production of CVs (>6T) de -grew by 7.2% due to the inventory reduction measures by OEMs, and our company grew by 0.8%, outperforming the market by 8%.

items.statement: FY24 CV production (>6T) grew 6.5%; company OE sales grew 16% outperforming market by 9.5%
items.quote: In FY 2023 -24, against 6.5% growth i n OE vehicle production (>6T)) the company recorded OE sales growth of 16% thus outperforming the market by 9.5%.

items.statement: Headwinds from geopolitical tensions, Red Sea disruptions, extreme weather events pose risks to outlook; election-related delays in mining and construction projects impacted Q4
items.quote: Headwinds from geopolitical tensions, volatility in international financial markets, geoeconomic fragmentation, rising Red Sea disruptions, and extreme weather events, however, pose risks to the outlook.

items.statement: Wholly-owned subsidiary ZF CV Control Systems Manufacturing India commenced commercial production March 2023, sales INR 34.8 crores, PAT INR 1.7 crores, eligible for 15% tax rate
items.quote: ZF C V Control Systems Manufacturing India Pvt. Ltd., a wholly -owned subsidiary of the company, commenced its commercial production in March 2023. The WoS recorded sales of 34.8 Crores and PAT of 1.7 crores.

items.statement: Export lead times increased from 6 weeks to 8/9 weeks due to Red Sea disruptions causing Q4 export degrowth of 15.5%
items.quote: This degrowth is due to a sales drop in Q4 caused by inventory reductions and delays in sea shipments as lead time increased from 6 weeks to 8/9 weeks.

items.statement: Targets 15%+ volume growth and EBITDA margin above 40% for FY25
items.quote: So with all this, we should be in a position to cross 10% to 12% -- reach 10% to 12% growth in Paint this year.

items.statement: Targets INR 20 crore pharma revenue in FY25, doubling in FY26
items.quote: And the full year, we have kept the target close to INR20 crores for this current year. And next year, it can easily double because all these clients will be going in a smooth way and supplies will be just happening without any hinderance and new clients will be added.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 70 crore for FY25, down from INR 140 crore in FY24
items.quote: As of today, we are looking at about INR70 crores investment possibility in this current year.

items.statement: Mahad plant for Aditya Birla Group to be ready by October-November 2024
items.quote: And the third plant will be getting ready by October, November. That is at Mahad.

items.statement: Panipat thin wall facility expected to start production by July-August 2024
items.quote: With the addition of Panipat thin wall facility getting into production by August, probably we thought of June, July, but probably it'll go into July, August.

items.statement: Pharma plant capacity utilization target of 70-80% by Q3 FY25
items.quote: So hopefully, by third quarter of this financial year, we will be running our pharma to a reasonably good extent, capacity utilization, something around 70% to 80%.

items.statement: Aditya Birla Group plants at Panipat and Cheyyar in commercial production; Mahad plant by Oct-Nov
items.quote: So we are still confident we will be in the region of 3,000 to 4,000 tons at least 3,000 tons for sure is what I'm expecting from ABG, which is almost 8% to 9% of our total volume.

items.statement: Qpack sales grew 80% in FY24; expects 30-50% growth in current year
items.quote: And today, we have seen 80% growth in Qpack sales in the current financial year. And even the trend during the first few months is still better. We still see a growth of high -- very high -- I mean maybe at least 30% to 50% rise in Qpack numbers even in this current year.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA/kg improved to INR 39 from INR 35-36 average due to Qpack mix and raw material discounts
items.quote: The improvement is mainly because of increase in sale of Qpack, which contributed around INR43 to INR45 per kg compared to Paint packs, which are below our average, it's somewhere around INR30 to INR35.

items.statement: Full year FY24 EBITDA margin was 37.7%; targets >40% in FY25
items.quote: We are hopeful that the EBITDA should cross 40% again in this current financial year, up from 37.7%, which we could achieve last year.

items.statement: Food & FMCG volume growth dipped to single digits in FY24 due to early monsoon impacting ice cream and delayed Kissan/Horlicks projects
items.quote: So the ice cream consumption picks up from middle of March and peaks in April and May. So last year, if you all remember, there were a lot of rains and early set of monsoon, which has impacted ice cream industry by more than 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Pharma packaging seeing strong traction with EV tubes crossing 5 lakh units in May; canisters and bottles under stability tests with top pharma companies
items.quote: And actually, now the commercial sales are happening in a reasonably a good manner in EV tubes, even in the month of April and May, and in the month of May at least I can comment, we crossed 5 lakhs EV tube sales and things can improve further because ther e are so many other products under

items.statement: Consciously shifting capacity from low-margin paints to higher-margin Qpacks and pharma
items.quote: And purposefully, we are using those capacities for our Qpacks, where we have better value addition. So that is one of the conscious decisions where we have taken a hit in the Paint segment.

items.statement: Pharma portfolio includes canisters with laser marking, EV tubes with IML, and bottles/caps - all three from single source
items.quote: We have come out with 3 product range that is canisters, EV tubes that is effervescent tablet tubes and tablet containers and caps. So all these 3 range is giving us a very good advantage when our marketing people approach a client because they had generally buy these 3 products from 3 different sources.

items.statement: Asian Paints contributes ~12,000 tons (1/3 of sales); lost some volumes as competitors now make thin-wall containers
items.quote: Contribution from Asian Paints is fungible. They continue to be our major client, almost 12,000 tons, I guess, it would be from them. That is almost 1/3 of our sales.

items.statement: Added new paint client in Hyderabad who shifted completely to IML packaging
items.quote: In fact, very recently, we added 1 client in Hyderabad itself, who has shifted completely his product range into IML.

items.statement: Stopped competitors copying Qpack designs via Delhi High Court IP enforcement
items.quote: and our ability to push our IP rights in the High Court of Delhi and subsequently stopping some of the competitors, who are copying our designs wi thout consent and using them that also helped in establishing our products better in the market

items.statement: First in India to offer IML on EV tubes; competitors lack quality IML capabilities
items.quote: we are first people to break the ice in IML EV tubes and that is going to give us an edge, I'm sure, to an Indian market, but also exports that are available

items.statement: Working capital utilization at INR 69-70 crore against drawing power of ~INR 100 crore; QIP funds parked in WC to save interest
items.quote: But today, even at that level, our -- what you call drawing power, is close to INR100 crores, but our utilization is hardly INR69 crores, INR70 crores. So there's still a big gap of unutilized working capital.

items.statement: Borrowed only INR 40 crore against INR 140 crore capex in FY24; balance funded via QIP and internal accruals
items.quote: If you look at what we borrowed is only INR40 crores. But what we invested is INR140 crores, okay?

items.statement: IML share of revenue stable at ~64% in FY24
items.quote: The IML overall is stagnating around 64% for the last year and this year also.

items.statement: FY24 segment volume growth: Paints -9% Q4, -6.7% full year; Lubricants flat Q4, +3.4% full year; Food & FMCG -10% Q4, +6.9% full year; Qpack +75% Q4, +88% full year
items.quote: Full year -- and for the full year Paints are down by 6.7%, Lubes are up by 3.4%, Food & FMCG 6.9%, Qpacks by 88%. Overall growth is 4.85%.

items.statement: FY24 segment revenue growth: Paints -15%; Lubricants -5.6%; Food & FMCG -0.17%; Qpack +70%; Total -4% due to raw material price pass-through
items.quote: In revenue terms, it's all because of the raw material, but anyway, for Paints it is down by 15% for the full year. In Lubricants also down by 5.6%. Food & FMCG down by 0.17%. Qpacks up by 70%. Total minus 4% because basically, when the raw material prices fell considerably from INR110 to INR95, our -- we passed on the pricing advantage to the whatever raw material price to consumer -- I mean our

items.statement: Pharma capacity expansion decision to be reviewed at Q3 FY25 based on demand traction
items.quote: And looking at the kind of demand and traction we could create, probably during the period at the Q3, Q4, we have to take a decision about expanding our capacity. But however, I'll keep that to be reviewed during the Q3 time, in the time of Q3.

items.statement: Consolidating Unit 2, Unit 6 (printing) and Unit 4 into Sultanpur and Annaram; printing integration by July-August 2024
items.quote: And now that at Sultanpur central unit, we are going to set up all the printing machinery, including die cutting, storage and distribution. It's all going to be under 1 roof. It is a 3 storeyed building where you have from top to down, there's a logistically controlled way of manufacturing the IML labels, which is going to save enormous, it's not enormous, sizable amount of wastage reduction cost

items.statement: Volume growth guided at around 8% for FY25; revenue growth not guided due to market pricing uncertainty
items.quote: You know, I can tell you about the volume growth. It will be around 8%, but revenue is totally driven by market pricing. So, it is really difficult because if the market further goes down, there is a less selling price. Then the revenue will be less than 8%.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% long-term
items.quote: I would still maintain 14% to 15% is sustainable margins.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected at 80-90 crore, may increase by 10-20 crore for iron making; two-year cumulative 170-200 crore
items.quote: Absolutely. And then, subsequently, I said it may go up because we wanted to put some thrust on iron making area. It may go up maybe by 10-20 crore more.

items.statement: Recovered 11,200 tons and ~8 million euros order from Dalmia Cement starting April
items.quote: And for this year, we already got 11,200 tons of volume and about 8 million euros order. So, we recovered this. So, this will add on to our growth story of volumes.

items.statement: Acquired Dalmia (RHI M-IR) EBITDA margin improved from 6.9% to 11.4% within a year
items.quote: When we acquired this was 6.9% EBITDA of Dalmia Group with one timer even. So, from 6.9%, we have reached almost 12%, 11.4% or so now.

items.statement: Export demand weak globally; China overcapacity, Europe steel production down 30-35%; no near-term revival expected
items.quote: You know, the market is really bad. If we talk about export, hardly any country is producing, I would say. China is reducing their steel production. They have an overcapacity of refractory. Europe is almost 30%, 35% lower steel production.

items.statement: Flow control ~25% of sales, lining ~75%; acquired assets more commodity brick/mix, not flow control
items.quote: Share, normally, historically flow control is about 25% and 75% is a lining in there.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis extending container transit from 25 to 60+ days; shipments stuck at Colombo, Singapore impacting Q4 invoicing
items.quote: Earlier, the container from China to India was about 25 days. Now it is more than 60 days. It is shipments at Colombo, at Singapore, at many places. So, it also is hitting us.

items.statement: One PSU customer credit risk remains; limiting exposure despite secured payments
items.quote: Still, we have one PSU plant which is not doing well. Though the payments are secured because it is a government plant, they are in not a really good shape. So, we are very cautious when it comes to shipping the material.

items.statement: Target 40% India market share in 5 years with global board support; shifting production from global plants to India for local-for-local
items.quote: Actually, our intention is to go to 40% market share in next five years' time. That is what our global CEO also, when he was in India, talked about in his TV interview.

items.statement: Export target 20-25% of revenue if geopolitical situation normalizes; currently ~10.5-11% of revenue
items.quote: You know, if marketing improve, I think 20%, 25% is not a very difficult task to reach. But it all depends on the market geographical situation.

items.statement: Working capital target 25-26% long-term; realistic sustainable 28-30% in 2-3 years
items.quote: 30. 28% to 30% should be realistically sustainable, but I would like to keep it to 25, 26 if all goes well in the next two-three years' time.

items.statement: FY24 capex ~80 crore (60% maintenance, 40% modernization); similar run-rate going forward
items.quote: So, basically this 80 crores CAPEX is not on modernization and upgrading of systems. It is maybe 60% is maintenance regular CAPEX to run these plants. And we spend about say 35 crores or so on some equipment.

items.statement: Goodwill impairment of Rs 326 crore on DOCL acquisition due to changed export assumptions; one-time non-cash charge
items.quote: In the financial systems, the value of the goodwill on acquisition of DOCL has been reduced by Rs. 326 crores against the amount initially recorded on the balance sheet, which has resulted in a non-cash charge to P&L.

items.statement: Domestic steel/cement growth attractive; iron making, DRI, pellet identified as growth areas
items.quote: We are now exceptionally positioned to enjoy the understood growth in the steel and cement sector. We will enhance this growth by leveraging synergies from our acquired acquisition and entering into the targeted area where we are underrepresented like iron making, DRI, pellets, etc.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Post demerger, ABFRL will raise fresh capital of INR2,500 crores to strengthen its balance sheet and support growth needs of its constituent businesses.
items.quote: Post demerger, ABFRL will raise fresh capital of INR2,500 crores to strengthen its balance sheet and support the growth needs of its constituent businesses.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 estimated in range of INR600 crores to INR650 crores for both entities put together.
items.quote: FY '25, my own estimate is that capex should be in a range of around INR600 crores to INR650 crores in both the entities put together.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 300 basis points to 11.1% in Q4 FY24 versus 8% last year.
items.quote: The company achieved a consolidated EBITDA of INR377 crores with margin expansion of 300 basis points to reach 11.1% versus 8% last year.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.2%, standalone margin expanded 60 basis points.
items.quote: EBITDA for FY '24 was INR1,703 crores with margin of 12.2%. Here too, EBITDA for standalone business led by profitability enhancement initiatives grew 10% with margin expansion expanding by 60 basis points.

items.statement: Lifestyle brands FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 300 basis points to 19.6%, highest ever EBITDA at INR1,284 crores.
items.quote: Despite this, led by all the profitability measures as explained before, Lifestyle brands posted highest ever EBITDA at INR1,284 crores, growing 17% Y-o-Y. Margin expanded by 300 basis points to reach 19.6% this fiscal.

items.statement: Pantaloons Q4 EBITDA margin grew 270 basis points to 10.4%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the business grew by 270 basis points to reach 10.4%.

items.statement: Market conditions remained largely unchanged with continued sluggishness in discretionary spending; January and February particularly affected by reduction in weddings and delayed winter onset.
items.quote: The market conditions remained largely unchanged from previous quarters with continued sluggishness in discretionary spending. The months of January and February were particularly affected primarily due to a reduction in the number of weddings and a delay in the onset of winter.

items.statement: Contribution from businesses other than Lifestyle and Pantaloons increased from ~16% to ~25% of overall sales in FY24.
items.quote: Specifically, the contribution to overall sales from businesses other than Lifestyle and Pantaloons increased from approximately 16% last year to around 25% this year.

items.statement: Pantaloons private label mix improved by 140 basis points in FY24 led by design aesthetics and addition of labels and categories.
items.quote: This fiscal, private label mix improved by 140 basis points led by significant improvement in design aesthetics and addition to labels and categories.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio annual revenue run rate INR2,000 crores plus, growing rapidly led by network expansion, same store sales growth and category extensions.
items.quote: This portfolio now has an annual revenue run rate of INR2,000 crores plus and continue to grow rapidly, led by network expansion, same store sales growth and category extensions.

items.statement: Reebok on path to double revenue in next 3-4 years led by rapid distribution expansion across channels.
items.quote: The brand is on a path to double its revenue in the next 3, 4 years, led by rapid expansion of distribution across channels.

items.statement: StyleUp format economically viable; accelerated expansion expected in H2 FY25 and even faster next year.
items.quote: You will see a more accelerated expansion in this format as we are beginning to get more and more comfortable with the format and its viability. The second half of this year, we'll see more accelerated expansion and perhaps an even faster one next year.

items.statement: Demerger expected to complete by end of Q3 or Q4 FY25; TCNS merger to complete in ~3 months after court AGM on June 5.
items.quote: On demerger, it may be, as you know, we are progressing as per our timeline. We plan to complete this exercise by end of fiscal -- end of Q3 or in last quarter of FY '25.

items.statement: Lifestyle brands ROC without goodwill historically 35-60%, expected to remain at that level.
items.quote: We do believe this business over a long period of time has operated at ROC without goodwill, anything between 35%, 40% to 60%, depending on the year. And we expect that trajectory to remain at that level.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at around 10%, in line with market growth
items.quote: I have always maintained that our revenue growth will be in line with the market growth. We will be at par with around 10% is what our revenue growth looks like for the coming financial year, and largely driven from even the domestic market.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin and EBITDA margin guided at current FY24 levels
items.quote: In terms of gross margins, we maintain we will be within the range of both the gross margin as wel l as EBITDA as to what we are currently. So, I think that is what we will as a guidance I would like to give you

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at Rs 600-700 crore including US CDMO facility
items.quote: It will be to the tune of 600 to 700 crores.

items.statement: US CDMO facility capex around Rs 400 crore; maintenance capex Rs 80-100 crore annually
items.quote: For US facility, that's new facility we will have a CAPEX around 400 crores. For the maintenance CAPEX of existing plant, it will be in the range of 80-100 crores.

items.statement: R&D spend guided at 4.5-5% of revenue for FY25 vs 4.1% in FY24
items.quote: if you see this year, we have been at around 4.1%, but then we would like to keep it at 4.5% to 5%, that's something that has been our trend on the R&D side and that includes some of the clinical trials that we do for some of our biosimilar portfolio as well.

items.statement: Domestic growth FY25 driven by volume (70% non-NLEM portfolio) and 3% price, 1-2% new launches
items.quote: So, we have 3% growth that comes out of price that we take. There are 1% or 2% growth that we attribute to the new launches that we do dur ing the year and balance we should have the volume -led

items.statement: Anti-infective growth pegged at 7-8% for FY25 after weak FY24
items.quote: So, I would peg it at somewhere within the range of 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Enzene US CDMO order book building; customers ready to work once plant operational
items.quote: We have already started building our order book in US. I can't share the numbers like how much orders we have already booked, but we already have customers who are ready to work with us.

items.statement: Chronic portfolio contribution 17-18% of domestic sales, expected to cross 20% near-to-mid term
items.quote: today we have around 17% to 18% business, that comes out of chronic and I expect it to cross 20% in the near-term-to-mid-term.

items.statement: Trade generics stable at 20-21% of domestic business, growing in line with Rx business
items.quote: we are within the range of 20% to 21%.

items.statement: US CDMO facility for biosimilars expected operational by end of FY25 (Q4/Q1 FY26)
items.quote: that will become operational by the end of this financial year most likely

items.statement: Field force headcount ~12,000 medical representatives; no major expansion planned FY25
items.quote: So, today put together we have around 12,000 number that we have overall on our field force.

items.statement: Domestic chronic productivity Rs 3.5 lakh per MR; overall group productivity Rs 4.5 lakh per MR in FY24
items.quote: for F Y'24 we have an overall group level productivity at around 4.5 lakhs, from chronic it's around 3.5 lakhs already that we have got

items.statement: US business FY25 new launches ~6-7 (including 1 relaunch) contributing 7-8% growth; Debigatran in Q2
items.quote: In FY'25 overall we are looking at around six to seven launches I would say and one of those will be a relaunch. So, looking at around 7% to 8% growth contributed by the new product launches in the US market

items.statement: Baddi site received 10 US FDA observations; no data integrity issues; responses submitted
items.quote: since we had few observations to which we have responded to the US FDA and we are pretty sure that none of these observations were very significant or such that there were no data integrity issues, etc., that we got as an observation.

items.statement: Service level penalties Rs 120 crore for FY24 (Rs 30 crore in Q4) due to US supply chain issues; expected to normalize FY25
items.quote: Only one-off was service level penalties which we have incurred. So, in our U.S. business we face some supply chain issues and because of that we have incurred some amount of service level penalties. So, that was the only one-off.

items.statement: Net cash position ~Rs 3,550 crore; generated ~Rs 1,400 crore cash in FY24
items.quote: we have generated approximately 1,400 crores in cash, which reinforces our balance sheet to establish a substantial net cash position of around Rs.3,550 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guided at 13-15% for FY25-26; rising to ~25% from FY27 as tax benefits expire
items.quote: For next two years we see our tax rate in the range of 13% to 15%. For FY'27 the second tax benefit will be over. So, our tax rate will definitely increase and it will be in the range of say 25% from there on.

items.statement: Actively seeking value-accretive acquisitions, priority chronic therapy; open to medical devices inorganic opportunities
items.quote: We are building what just for acquisitions, I would say we are very hungry, we are looking for right opportunity in the market, but of course at the right price. So, we are very open to acquiring any asset which will be synergistic to us of strategic value to us and comes at the right price.

items.statement: Dividend payout to continue within historical range
items.quote: dividend payout, we have always been within the range of a particular range and we are continuing to be within that range as far as our dividend payout is concerned.

items.statement: Penicillin G price decline expected but not yet materialized; would benefit margins if it occurs
items.quote: there are certain elements which will play out in the market over a period of time and that will decide on some of our key products like PenG, where everybody is ex pecting the price to come down. So, far we haven't seen it getting played
