We will discuss about the Kolkata part. LOGOS deal as I explained in the last conferenc

items.statement: Reaffirmed long-term revenue CAGR guidance of 25% over next 3-5 years, with gradual trajectory
items.quote: we stand with our revenue guidance of 25% CAGR over the next three to five years. But again, one should see that this is going to be more of a gradual trajectory towards moving towards the 25% CAGR growth.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA and PAT expected to grow faster than revenue driven by operational efficiencies and capacity utilization
items.quote: We also anticipate that our EBITDA and PAT will grow at a faster rate than revenue, driven by operational efficiencies and increased utilization across our units.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 230 bps to 42.8%, PAT margin expanded 220 bps to 30.3%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for FY '24 stood at 42.8% as compared to 40.5%, an increase of 230 bps. Our PAT margins for FY '24 stood at 30.3% as compared to 28.1%, an increase of 220 bps.

items.statement: Margin expansion to continue but delta will diminish at higher utilization levels; injectable facility may slightly offset FY25 expansion
items.quote: Beyond a certain number, the delta would be there but it would be lower compared to what you would have seen when the capacity utilization was, say, at 10% or 15%.

items.statement: Major capex completed; only maintenance capex of ~INR 25 crores annually going forward
items.quote: Now we would have some bit of maintenance capex only which will be to the tune of INR25 crores or so. As, now as mentioned earlier also that this year as well as the coming year is more about how we optimally utilize the capacities that we have put in place.

items.statement: Limbasi facility utilization at 35.12% in FY24 vs 31.81% in FY23; injectable plant commercial production expected early H2 FY25
items.quote: Limbasi facility is working at around 35.12% in this financial year. It was 31.81% in the last financial year.

items.statement: Injectable facility commissioning delayed to early Q3 FY25 from late Q1 due to validation and regulatory approvals
items.quote: we're expecting it to be somewhere in the early half of Q3.

items.statement: Added 95 new customers in FY24; top 10 customer concentration reduced from 44.3% to 42%
items.quote: In FY'24, we acquired 95 new customers and introduced new products to existing customers. As a result, the contribution from our top 10 customers decreased from 44.3% in FY'23 to 42% in FY'24

items.statement: Immunosuppressant share reduced by ~4% YoY; oncology and anti-infectives growing faster
items.quote: compared to last year, the immunosuppressants have come down by around 4%, the weightage on immunosuppressants.

items.statement: Added 2 new fermentation API products (total 30) and 21 formulation products (total 98) in FY24; pipeline of 10+ products
items.quote: We are pleased to announce the addition of two new products in the fermentation API space, bringing our total products count to 30. We also have a robust pipeline of over 10 products to be introduced in the coming years

items.statement: API revenue growth of 9% YoY in FY24 impacted by customer site relocations requiring regulatory approvals; normalization expected in FY25
items.quote: The growth was partially impacted on account of a couple of customers relocating their manufacturing bases, necessitating compliances with regulatory authorities and approval processes to procure materials from Concord in the new location, which has been completed in March of '24. Hence, we anticipate revenue normalization in FY'25.

items.statement: Formulation revenue grew 106% YoY in FY24 to INR 189 crores; domestic business grew 24%
items.quote: Our formulations revenue grew by 37% in Q4FY'24 and 106% for the full year FY'24 on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Limbasi facility received USFDA EIR with zero 483 observations; EU-GMP, ANVISA Brazil, Saudi FDA, Kenya, Tanzania approvals completed
items.quote: The USFDA authorities conducted an inspection of our Limbasi facility in June '23. I am pleased to announce that the inspection concluded successfully with zero 483 observations. We now have an EIR for this inspection.

items.statement: Two key API customers relocated manufacturing bases causing ~6-7% revenue impact in Q4; approvals received in March, supply resumed from April
items.quote: this was close to around -- probably around 6% to 7% or so.

items.statement: API revenue INR 828 crores (9% YoY), Formulation revenue INR 189 crores (106% YoY), Domestic revenue grew 24%, Export revenue grew 15%
items.quote: revenue from API business grew by 14% in this quarter and 9% for the full financial year 2024. It stood at INR 265 crores for this quarter and INR 828 crores for the financial year 2024

items.statement: FY24 revenue crossed INR 1,000 crores at INR 1,107 crores (19% YoY); EBITDA INR 435 crores (26% YoY); PAT INR 308 crores (28% YoY)
items.quote: Revenue from operations for the financial year 2024 crossed INR 1,000 crores and stood at INR1,107 crores against INR 853 crores in financial year 2023, representing growth of 19% as compared to the last year.

items.statement: Actively exploring CDMO opportunities with innovators and major generic players; submitting RFQs; not included in guidance
items.quote: We are in discussion with various innovators and major generic players, submitting RFQs and positioning Concord as a reliable partner.

items.statement: Quarterly lumpiness in API sales due to customer procurement patterns; management recommends annual evaluation
items.quote: Revenue growth can be impacted on account of customers' procurement patterns, leading to lumpiness in sales in a particular quarter, causing fluctuations in sales.

items.statement: No significant raw material cost increases; some raw material costs reduced; no API pricing pressure seen
items.quote: we do not see any challenges either on the pricing front or any raw material or anything which has actually increased substantially in terms of the pricing. As a matter of fact we have been able to bring down, in certain cases, the cost of the raw materials which we were currently procuring.

items.statement: International revenue grew 15% YoY in FY24; new regulatory approvals opening emerging markets
items.quote: Our revenue from the international business grew by 14% in this quarter and 15% for the full fiscal year 2024.

items.statement: Expanded doctor reach by 1,000+ in FY24 across nephrology, oncology, rheumatology
items.quote: In FY'24 alone, we established touchpoints with over 1,000 doctors in critical care, nephrology and rheumatology, among others.

items.statement: Aspires mid-teens revenue growth in FY25 backed by new store openings and subject to industry demand recovery; targets profitability improvement via cost efficiency
items.quote: To summarise, going ahead for FY '25 , the company aspires to achieve mid -teens revenue growth backed by new store openings in new and existing geographies and subject to recovery in the overall industry demand for premium and mid-premium brands.

items.statement: Intends to spend around 5% of revenues on branding and advertising going forward
items.quote: Going ahead, we will spend on around 5% of revenues on branding and advertising.

items.statement: Capex of INR35 crores each in FY23 and FY24 includes new store additions and renovation of old stores; warehouse capex of INR13-14 crores was incurred last year
items.quote: So, it is both the capex for new stores as well as renovation of the old stores. That keeps on happening every year. Some stores keep on getting renovating. Every year.

items.statement: Added 52 EBO stores in FY24; plans to add 30-40 new EBO stores in FY25; total EBO count at 425 as of March 2024
items.quote: During the year, we have added 52 EBO stores and we plan to add another 30 to 40 new stores in FY '25.

items.statement: Premium and mid-premium apparel demand softened due to inflation curtailing discretionary spend and delayed winter onset shortening fresh season sales period in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The market for premium and mid -premium branded appar el continued to experience softened demand due to consumer behaviour influenced by an inflationary environment that curtailed discretionary expenditures while concurrently witnessing a surge in consumer spend towards travel and other essential purchases.

items.quote: We should be in that range.

items.statement: MBO channel revenue degrew ~2% for FY24; Q4 degrowth appearance due to higher voluntary return provision of 25% vs 14.4% prior year
items.quote: MBO channel for the year has degrown by around 2%.

items.quote: There has been an increase in advertisement expenses related to brand building and store openings and these upfront investments will strengthen the brand in the coming years. items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 3.9% YoY in Q4 FY24 and 0.6% YoY for full year FY24
items.quote: Our SSSG for the year stood at 0.6% year -on-year.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR0.50 per share on face value of INR2 each
items.quote: The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of INR0.50 per share on face value of INR2 each of the company.

items.statement: Voluntarily increased expected goods return provision to 25% in Q4 FY24 from 14.4% in Q4 FY23, creating ~INR21 crores excess provision impacting gross profit, EBITDA, PBT by ~INR11.8 crores and PAT by ~INR9 crores
items.quote: In Q4 FY '23 , this provision was at 14.4% of sales whereas in Q4 FY '24 it has been voluntarily taken at 25% instead of 14.4% considering the increased returns due to the current market scenario. This has led to an excess provision of approximately INR 21 crores which has an approximate INR 11.8 crores impact on gross profit, EBITDA and PBT and an impact of INR9 crores on PAT.

items.statement: Market conditions remain volatile; April was good but May demand dwindled; difficult to predict immediate recovery; moderated growth ambitions to protect profitability

Hence, we have moderated our growth ambitions but we certainly want to improve our profitability and our working capital days, etc. by the end of this year.

items.statement: Brand positioned between denim-lead and casual-lead universes in mid-premium to premium segment; balanced top-wear and bottom-wear offering (~50:50) enabling larger wallet share
items.quote: We are one of the brands that has a very very strong, balanced offering in terms of bottom-wear and top-wear. And that is visible in our sales, which is almost half and half.

items.quote: As of 31st March 2024, we are present in 599 cities having over 1800 retail touch points. We have presence through 425 EBOs, 77 large format stores and 1,332 plus MBOs.

items.statement: Franchise deposits held as liability on balance sheet; interest paid on deposits; no material debt concerns mentioned
items.quote: So franchises give us deposits as advances towards the goods that we supply to them, but we don't reduce that from receivables. We park it separately in the balance sheet as a liability and pay interest on that to the franchises.

items.statement: One-time bonus of ~INR1.7 crores paid to all employees for 25th anniversary in FY24; increased outsourced manpower for larger warehouse and MBO shop-in-shop staff
items.quote: Some of this, what you see is on account of a one time thing that we did because last year was our 25th anniversary. So, there was a bonus paid to all our employees for the silver jubilee at around INR 1.7 odd crores.

items.statement: Subsidiary (former sampling unit) has no business activity; sampling brought in-house; subsidiary to be closed shortly
items.quote: There is no business being transacted in that subsidiary. Rasik Mittal: So earlier it was a sampling unit for us. See because we are a brand , we create samples. items.quote: So in terms of FY24 yes Kerala market was not -- so that's happened for the last 2-3 years, but in terms of all primary indicators that we've been speaking to banks, financial institutions and other related like real estate, etc we're hoping for a recovery from this year and going forward.

items.quote: Ather, if I look at it in two wheelers, Ather, there's been a change of model and also because of the FAME in terms of uncertainty the numbers in April and May are far lower than what the numbers were in Jan, Feb, March. items.statement: FY24 debt/equity 0.7x, net debt/equity 0.6x, net debt/EBITDA 1.3x, interest coverage 2x
items.quote: The interest coverage ratio is two times. Debt to equity ratio is 0.7x. Net debt to equity is 0.6x and net debt to EBITDA is 1.3x.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR0.50 per share (face value INR2) for FY24
items.quote: We are pleased to inform that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR0.50 paisa per equity share of face value of 2 which is subject to approval at the ensuing AGM.

items.statement: Subsidiaries Popular Auto Works (JLR) and Vision Motors (Honda) received Great Place to Work certification for 5th consecutive year
items.quote: Last but not least, it has been our great pride I want to share that for the fifth consecutive year the company's owned subsidiary, fully owned subsidiary that is Popular Auto works that is the JLR dealership and Vision Motors which is the Honda dealership received the Great Place to Work certification.

items.statement: FY24: PV revenue +9.7% to INR3,300 cr; CV revenue +24% to INR1,900 cr; EV revenue +51% to INR85 cr; Service revenue +21% to INR865 cr; Spares distribution +14% to INR263 cr

items.statement: Regular & Others EBITDA grew 22% YoY in FY24; expect further growth in FY25 from price hikes and lower raw material costs
items.quote: We expect further growth because we have got price increases in Rajasthan as well as the -- as was being discussed earlier on this call with softening raw material prices, that impacts profitability in our consumer business as well.

items.statement: Ethanol production shifting to maize: over 2/3 of ethanol output from maize in FY25 vs negligible in FY24
items.quote: In this financial year, for ethanol, we expect over 2/3 of our ethanol production to come from maize?

items.statement: Prestige & Above distribution expanding from 6 to 8 states in FY25; 3 of first 5 states showing strategy benefits
items.quote: We are also going to be expanding our distribution presence, which currently stands at 6 states to another 2 states during the coming quarters.

items.statement: Regular & Others entry into UP planned for Q2-Q3 FY25
items.quote: I think Q2, Q3 is when you will have the launch of Regular & Others, sometime towards the end of Q2, maybe beginning of Q3.

items.statement: Differentiation via innovation in liquid and packaging; later entrant advantage allows sharper offerings
items.quote: We also have certain advantages for being later entrant because we have the advantage of being more innovative. We have the advantage of giving better offerings than what are existing in the marketplace.

items.statement: Income tax demand of INR40.93 crores received; INR255.11 crores deposited under protest; no provision deemed necessary
items.quote: Subsequent to the year-end, the company has received assessment orders of income tax. The amount of tax demand is INR40.93 crores out of which INR5.3 crores was deposited in Q3. For the balance amount, the company has deposited INR255.11 crores in protest and has gone for appeal.

items.statement: Net debt (net of cash) INR241 crores at end FY24 vs INR194 crores end FY23; increase due to new units and geographies
items.quote: Our net debt of cash -- net of cash and cash equivalents at the end of FY'25 stands at INR241 crores, a slight increase versus FY'23, which stood at INR194 crores.

items.statement: Bulk alcohol Q4 production 64.8 million liters; sales 48.7 million liters; power & fuel cost FY24 INR245 crores
items.quote: The production in Q4 has been 64.8 million liters. Our power and fuel cost for the entire year has been INR245 crores.

items.statement: Raw material policy change (FCI rice stoppage) caused unprecedented Q4 margin collapse; maize transition underway to eliminate volatility
items.quote: In Q4 FY'24, we saw unprecedented low margin due to a change in the raw material mix as FCI discontinued rice supplies for manufacturing of bulk alcohol.

items.statement: No brewery investment planned until beer volumes reach 1-2 million cases per annum; will stay contract brewed for couple of years
items.quote: So I don't foresee an investment in a brewery in a hurry. When we get to a certain scale, and I believe that scale is somewhere around 1 million to 2 million cases per annum of beer. That is when a brewery investment starts making sense.

items.statement: Management guides minimum 15% loan growth for FY25, aims to better it.
items.quote: And of course, as usual, we would give a guidance of 15% minimum guidance of growth in this year also. Last year, we gave a guidance of 15%, but we were able to achieve almost 20%.

items.statement: Targets non-gold loan subsidiaries to contribute 18-20% of loan assets in five years.
items.quote: We embark financial year '25 on a positive note and shall continue our vision to grow the share of gold loan subsidiary -- non-gold loan subsidiaries to 18% to 20% in the next five years.

items.statement: Plans to add 150-200 branches annually.
items.quote: I think we have -- last year, we have grown about -- last quarter, we have grown about 225 branches. So going forward, we will go -- we will grow our branches maybe 150, 200 every year, yes.

items.statement: Overall borrowing costs expected to move towards 9% in coming quarters.
items.quote: I think that cost of borrowings would be somewhere around 8.65%. The incremental cost of borrowing is almost around 8.8% to 9%. So I think in the coming quarters, I think the overall borrowing costs will move towards 9%.

items.statement: 25-30 bps increase in borrowing costs can be absorbed or passed on to customers.
items.quote: And 25, 30 basis points increase. And our return on assets can easily absorb. If we want, we can pass on to the customers also.

items.statement: May pass on incremental borrowing costs to borrowers if rates rise.
items.quote: But given the fact we have a wide -- larger return on assets, the impact on the impact because of such increa sed 25, 30 basis points is not material, we can always decide to pass on this incremental cost to the borrowers also

items.statement: Sees good growth in micro finance, home loan, and personal loan sectors.
items.quote: But we see good growth in these probably, as you said, in the micro finance. In the home loan sector, I think we have a new set of team there. They will definitely grow well home loan sector and also in the personal loan sector also.

items.statement: Regulatory cash disbursal limit has no significant impact on business volumes.
items.quote: I think the regulation about the INR20,000 cash limit is applicable to all, and it has not had any significant effect on any of these disburses and we see quite good traction even in this year even in this quarter.

items.statement: Sees good growth in April and May despite cash limit regulation.
items.quote: And we have seen -- even after this in April, May, we have seen a good growth in these months also.

items.statement: Vehicle loan business prospects muted due to crowded sector.
items.quote: The vehicle loan business, probably if you ask me personally, we don't see a very big prospect because the because the sector is very crowded and we don't have much stren gth their. Of course, it will be there, but it will be

items.statement: Average LTV on gold loans is around 63%.
items.quote: Even today also, the average LTV on the gold loans is around 63%.

items.statement: Ticket size breakup: <1L 35%, 1-3L 37%, >3L 29%.
items.quote: Less than INR1 lakh is 35%; INR1 lakh to INR3 lakh is 37%; and above INR3 lakh is 29%.

items.statement: Accrued interest increased to INR2,180 crores in March 2024 from INR1,853 crores in March 2023.
items.quote: In terms of accrued interest for March '24, the total interest accrued is INR2,180 crores; March '23 interest accrued is INR1,853 crores, I think Shubhranshu asked for that interest accrued details.

items.statement: ECL provision: Stage 1 INR620 crores, Stage 2 INR28 crores, Stage 3 INR288 crores.
items.value: INR620 crores; INR28 crores; INR288 crores
items.quote: ECL provision of Stage 1, the ECL provision is INR620 crores. Stage 2 is INR28 crores and sales 3, it is INR288 crores.

items.statement: Auction amount for quarter INR162 crores, total INR892 crores.
items.quote: It's INR162 crores. Total INR892 crores.

items.statement: Raised INR480 crores through public issue of secured NCDs.
items.quote: During the year, we raised INR480 crores to the 33rd public issue of secured renewable nonconvertible debentures.

items.statement: Expects 8x to 10x loan book growth over next three years with healthy PAT and EPS increase
items.quote: As far as the book size is concerned we are expecting 8 to 10x growth in the next 3 years and we should have a very healthy increase in the PAT and the EPS in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Targets 100-120 corporate partnerships for EVA by end of FY25
items.quote: We plan to increase it to 100 this thing by end of this year. 100 to 120, you know, whatever maximum we can go.

items.statement: Expects EVA disbursements to scale 7x-8x by end of FY25 from current ~INR1 crore/month
items.quote: We are clocking close to 1 crore in disbursement in this month. And we expect to scale it to almost 7x to 8x by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin will go up driven by high-return EVA product
items.quote: Yes definitely EBITDA margin will go up.

items.statement: EVA product yields ~36% IRR with zero delinquency in last six months
items.quote: We are almost ending at 2.5% to 3% per month. IRA is roughly around 36%. And in the past six months, we have been doing on the single trial basis, there's a 0% delinquency in that.

items.statement: Plans to open offices in Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore for EVA corporate sourcing
items.quote: We are planning to open an office in Delhi, Bangalore and maybe later going to say Bombay. For sourcing more corporates for the EVA product.

items.statement: Mauritius Fund invested INR10 crores via warrants; INR2.5 crores received, balance INR7.5 crores by H1 FY25
items.quote: Mauritius Fund has invested about INR10 crores in our share of the warrants issue, INR2.5 crores they already put in. And I think then, say, before the end of the next, this thing, half year closing, they put the balance of INR7.5 crores.

items.statement: Main challenge is corporate onboarding taking ~1.5 months and low product awareness
items.quote: That is a major challenge. That is what onboarding an employer takes about one and a half months with currently with us.

items.statement: EVA charges 2-2.5% upfront processing fee; business loans at 17-18%
items.quote: We charge about 2%, or 2.5% processing fees is deducted upfront.

items.statement: SBI sanctioned INR15 crore limit at 10.95%; debt-to-equity target 2:1
items.quote: Last year we were sanctioned limit by State Bank of India. And they have sanctioned a INR15 crore limit. Out of that, we have just placed only INR6 crores.

items.statement: Announcing one or two new business lines in 7-10 days
items.quote: I think we should be able to tell the exchange in the next 7-10 days.

items.statement: Management maintains ~20% revenue growth guidance for FY25 including some contribution from particle board plant
items.quote: So on the guidance, I think we still are maintaining about a 20% revenue growth with some value of revenue coming in from the particle board plant.

items.statement: Laminate volume growth expected in double digits over next few years
items.quote: And on the outlook, we think we should grow in double digits in volume over the next few years.

items.statement: Particle board plant capex of INR250-275 crore in FY25 plus INR50 crore maintenance capex; routine maintenance capex ~INR50 crore annually thereafter
items.quote: So this year, since the particle board unit is under implementation, so we expect around INR250 crores, INR275 crores in this year and another around INR50 crores of maintenance capex in this year. Going forward, the -- after the particle board unit put into place, so then you can expect around INR50 crores of capex -- maintenance capex on a routine basis.

items.statement: Peak net debt expected at INR925-950 crore in FY25
items.quote: We expect it to be in the range of around INR925 crores to INR950 crores in this year. That will be the peak debt -- peak net debt, which we are hoping.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 12.8% in FY24; expected to stay in this range or improve as new categories stabilize
items.quote: The blended margin this year is at 12.8%, and we believe that this should be in this range, or it will go up as and when the new product category, which we are into, may stabilize and start contributing more in terms of the margin.

items.statement: Particle board segment targeting 20-24% EBITDA margin by year 4 of operations
items.quote: We are expecting this to happen, the 20%, 25% -- 20%, 24% within fourth year of operation.

items.statement: Domestic demand slow across building material categories; export market share gains continuing despite Red Sea disruptions
items.quote: being a bit slow in terms of demand and all that stuff, as we've been hearing from our partners and teams and I'm sure you all have also heard that commentary from other building material industries. items.statement: No price hikes planned for laminates and veneers; price hikes planned for plywood business
items.quote: So no price hikes have been planned for Lam and Allied and Veneer Allied. Price hikes have been planned for plywood business.

items.statement: Laminate Q4 FY24 production 5.21 million sheets, sales 5.23 million sheets; FY24 production 19.85 million, sales 18.97 million sheets
items.quote: Production volumes were the highest at 5.21 million sheets and at a utilization level of 85% on the enhanced capacity of 24.52 million. Sales volume for the quarter also was highest and stood at 5.23 million sheets.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 60 days in Q4 FY24 from 72 days in Q3 FY24; net debt INR834 crore as of March 31
items.quote: In the current quarter, working capital cycle improved by 12 days to 60 days as compared to 72 days in the quarter 3 of this year. Net debt as on March 31 stood at INR834 crores as against INR847 crores in -- on December 31.

items.statement: Uttar Pradesh land acquired; approvals process underway; no concrete expansion plan yet
items.quote: So we're in the process of getting all the approvals in place, et cetera, but that's the stage we're at on the Uttar Pradesh plant.

items.statement: Board declared final dividend of INR1.65 per share (face value INR1) for FY24
items.quote: Board has declared a final dividend of INR1.65 per share of a face value of INR1.

items.statement: Revenue growth to be volume-led, better than market growth rate.
items.quote: So, look, our revenue growth in last few years is primarily driven by two-third by volume growth and will continue the same trend going forward, it will be largely driven by volume.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected to continue due to service mix, payer mix, and operating leverage.
items.quote: EBITDA margin that we see in Q4 is on account of better service mix and a payer mix and operating leverage due to a strong revenue growth. We expect that to continue going forward.

items.statement: Maintenance capex guided at Rs 65-70 crores.
items.quote: As far as the maintenance CAPEX is concerned, we have always guided, and our maintenance CAPEX will be around 65 to 70 crores and 70 crores is the number which you saw for FY'24 as well.

items.statement: North Bangalore center total capex estimated at Rs 90 crores, spent over current and next financial year.
items.quote: North Bangalore, the total CAPEX is estimated is around 90 crores which largely would be spent in the current year and of course in the next financial year.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY25 expected between 35% to 39%.
items.quote: Somewhere between 35% to 39%.

items.statement: Adding 350 to 400 beds in existing hospitals over next four to five years, mostly completed in three years.
items.quote: In total, across our current hospitals, we are looking at adding about 350 to 400 beds in our existing hospitals in the next four to five years. Most of that will get completed in the next three years.

items.statement: Two new hospitals in Bangalore with total 125 beds to be operational in next 12 to 15 months.
items.quote: We are currently in the process of establishing two hospitals with total 125 beds in North Bangalore and Whitefield area , slated to be operational in the next 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: South Mumbai expected to break even in middle of the year.
items.quote: South Mumbai has reduced the losses and is expected to start breaking even sometime in the middle of the year.

items.statement: Kolkata center started contributing positive EBITDA and will continue to grow.
items.quote: Kolkata has started contributing positive EBITDA. It will continue to grow going forward.

items.statement: Rising incidence of cancer expected in coming decade due to population and lifestyle.
items.quote: Given the population of India and more recognition of cancer and lifestyle disease, there is definitely going to be a rising incidence of cancer in the coming decade.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 75% year-on-year in FY24 and will be important growth driver.
items.quote: Our digital revenue has grown 75% year-on-year in FY'24 and will continue to be an important driver of growth in future.

items.statement: Doctor attrition low at less than 5%, not expected to be an issue.
items.quote: our top doctors’ attrition is very low, less than 5%. So, we have been very proud and even today because of the way we empower the doctors, we are involved in academics and research. Our attrition has not been a major issue and we don't expect it to be an issue at all.

items.statement: Planning to introduce MR LINAC Radiation Therapy in Bangalore.
items.quote: We plan to introduce MR LINAC Radiation Therapy in Bangalore, which would be a notable addition to the vastly superior radiation treatment offering at a HCGwhich will help us revolutionize radiation therapy in the state.

items.statement: Institutional Research Committee established to fund investigator-initiated trials.
items.quote: We have established an Institutional Research Committee to fund investigator-initiated trials, which is one-of-a-kind in the Indian private health sector.

items.statement: Mortality rate now under 1%.
items.quote: We're happy to report that our mortality rate as we measure while we are one of the few measuring it has now come under 1% over the years , the feat we are immensely proud of and definitely meeting or beating the global standards.

items.statement: Management aims to consistently deliver growth and performance, with multi-year contracts for next year higher than current revenue.
items.quote: The contracts in the next year are much higher than, the current numbers that we have done.

items.statement: Management does not see margins declining due to favorable exchange rates, productivity, reusable components, and larger multi-year contracts.
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, we do not believe that our margins will at all go down because everything is in favor the exchange rates are in favor, the productivity is in favor, reusable components and tools are in favor.

items.statement: Robust pipeline of signed businesses and multi-year contracts position the company for continued success.
items.quote: With a robust pipeline of signed businesses, we are well equipped to continue our trajectory of success in the upcoming year.

items.statement: Multi-year contracts signed for next year exceed current year revenue, providing revenue visibility.
items.quote: What we continuously and consistently try and achieve is that we have more signed contracts in hand for the next year before we end the current financial year.

items.statement: Capex is not a large portion of growth; investment focuses on talent, subsidiaries, market expansion, and potential acquisitions.
items.quote: Capex does not remain a very large portion of where the growth is done but investment does happen in creating subsidiaries, reaching out to new mark ets, reaching out to creating acquisitions or investments into scale-up startups

items.statement: Team grew from 250 to 400 engineers; targeting 40-60% year-on-year team growth, potentially doubling in 12 months.
items.quote: We do believe that on a year-on-year basis, we do add between 40%, to 60% of our team size. So, we are fairly geared at this point of time to grow from 400 to more than double in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Cybersecurity practice is a focus area with SOCs being set up in India and Netherlands for real-time monitoring.
items.quote: Shortly, we'll be setting up a Securities Oper ations Center, a SOC, in both India and the Netherlands. This is where a fa ir amount of investment will also

items.statement: 95% revenue from overseas (Nordics, Benelux, Germany, UK), 5% domestic; no single customer >20% of revenue.
items.quote: Almost 95% of our revenue comes from overseas customers and around 4%-5% comes from domestic customers.

items.statement: Shift to local entity in Netherlands enables higher billing rates and larger multi-year deals.
items.quote: This strategic shift from an outsourcing Company to a local entity in a local market, delivering local relationships and local culture, has significantly boosted our revenue and growth and enabled us to close larger multi-year deals.

items.statement: Active treasury desk hedges FX flows for at least 3 years.
items.quote: We at least make sure that we are fairly covered for at least 3 years. And we have a very active treasury desk towards making sure that we maintain our FX flows.

items.statement: Key risks include geopolitical instability, customer acquisition, technology changes; mitigated by diversification, FX hedging, and customer concentration limits.
items.quote: Somewhere war happens or somewhere political instability happens or the law changes in certain countries or your customers' businesses get acquired overnight and you lose control on your relationship.

items.statement: R&D spend estimated at 4-4.5% of revenue (INR4-5 crores in FY24), expensed not capitalized.
items.quote: Around INR4 crores to INR5 crores, yes.

items.statement: Priority is reinvestment for growth; dividend decision rests with board, but management recommends staying highly invested in growth.
items.quote: I would recommend to my board of directors to remain highly invested into growth and make sure that our shareholders remain as our top priority and we give them maximum growth along with the organization's growth.

items.statement: Competes with firms like Sogeti, TEOTO in Nordics/Benelux; differentiation via consulting depth, onsite presence, non-English market expertise.
items.quote: We compete with, let's say, Sogeti from France or we compete with TEOTO and every kind of players in the Nordics or we compete with a few names in the Benelux ecosystem.

items.statement: Stable Indian government supports global respect for Indian tech companies.
items.quote: Hopefully, if our results happen the way they are of our country, we get stable government. That means a lot to us on a global scale because Indian tech Company is hugely respected and appreciated on a global scale.

items.statement: Potential acquisitions or investments in scale-up startups are part of immediate strategies.
items.quote: investment does happen in creating subsidiaries, reaching out to new mark ets, reaching out to creating acquisitions or investments into scale-up startups and so on and so forth which do remain as some of the immediate strategies

items.quote: Margin will be more or less same because we're not taking any price hikes. We want to increase the volume.

items.quote: What we are thinking maybe in this -- I mean, the lower segment, we may a little bit cut down the prices and bring back the volume so that the overall sales of the company increases.

items.statement: Management targets defending consolidated EBITDA margins near 27% and PAT margins near 20% achieved in Q4 FY24, though acknowledges it will be tough.
items.quote: In terms of Margins, yes, we will try to defend them or protect them to as close to these levels as possible.

items.quote: The INR915 crore order of Bangladesh came in April. So we have not added that to the order book. But now that's also a finite order and a contract agreement has also been signed.

items.statement: Consultancy revenue (consolidated) reached all-time high of INR 1,300 crore in FY24, up 10% year-on-year in project consultancy.

items.statement: Bangladesh coach order (200 coaches, 8 types) to start prototype production in a month; revenue realization targeted by Q3-Q4 FY25. Locomotive order (10 units) longer cycle, revenue may slip to early FY26.
items.quote: We recently on 20th May signed the formal contract agreement also. So now the final designs and approvals are underway and we will start production of the prototype and manufacturing very soon in a month or so.

items.statement: Turnkey order book of INR 2,500 crore executable over roughly 2.5-3 years; fresh turnkey orders limited to ~INR 500 crore in FY24.

items.statement: Turnkey margins range 3-4%; consultancy margins ~45% in Q4 but under pressure from competitive bidding in both project consultancy and QA.
items.quote: Turnkey business by nature have a margin ranging from 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Management claims RITES is the only Indian company with full-spectrum infrastructure consultancy across 13 verticals (airports, ports, highways, metros, rail, buildings, etc.) under one roof.

items.statement: Leasing business seeing growing client base across private and public sectors (power, cement, ports, steel); competition increasing but management targets higher revenue and EBITDA.
items.quote: Number of new clients, both in the private and public sector have been approaching us. And we are moving in the right direction in expanding our client base in the leasing business.

items.statement: REMC (subsidiary) signed first PPA for 900 MW round-the-clock tender, second LOA for 700 MW issued; solar plant at Bhilai inaugurated; revenue up 30%+, PAT up 37%+, dividend ~INR 80 crore (51% to RITES).

items.statement: Shift from nomination to competitive bidding across consultancy and export orders compressing margins; management focuses on cost optimization and faster execution to protect profitability.
items.quote: The change, which happened about 2.5 years back in terms of nomination vis-a-vis competitive mode. That is the major change, which has been there for about 2, 2.5 years.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; business model emphasizes low capex, no construction risk, and bottom-line focus.
items.quote: One, we are a debt-free company. Two, we are a low capex company. Our capex will always be in the range of INR100-odd crore, INR130 crore to INR140 crore, as you see from the trend. Three, we are not going to be a construction company.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue projected at Rs. 2,000 crore in FY25, approximately 2x growth from FY24.
items.quote: In FY '25, on a consolidated basis, Gensol is projected to achieve the milestone of Rs. 2,000 crore revenue, approximately 2x growth from what we did in FY '24.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins expected to remain at 25%-26%.
items.quote: So, I think on the bottom line, we have said that our consolidated EBITDA margins are about 25%-26% We see that we should continue to do the similar kind of numbers.

items.statement: EV manufacturing revenue expected between Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 crores in FY25.
items.quote: And in terms of revenue, we are expecting that we will have a revenue of between Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 crores from EV manufacturing in FY '25.

items.statement: Scorpius Trackers revenue expected to double between FY24 and FY25.
items.quote: The Scorpius Tracker, the revenue from there is expected to actually double between FY '24 and FY '25.

items.statement: Solar order book stands at Rs. 1,448 crores as of FY24 end.
items.quote: Our solar order book stands at Rs. 1,448 crores as on FY '24 end with a big pipeline that far surpasses the number.

items.statement: Scorpius Trackers order book approximately Rs. 100 crores out of total Rs. 1,700 crores.
items.quote: I would not have the exact number, but I can today tell you that approximately out of the Rs. 1,700 crore order books, Scorpius would have about a Rs. 100 crore-ish order book.

items.statement: EV manufacturing plant requires additional CAPEX of Rs. 75-100 crores.
items.quote: think on the EV manufacturing side, it will need between Rs. 75 and 100 crores more and if the EV leasing book will continue to grow by 100% year-on-year

items.statement: India to have over 300 GW solar power by FY30, ensuring no dearth of orders.
items.quote: I think we are seeing that India is going to have some 300 plus gigawatt of solar power by FY '30, which means that there is going to be no dearth of orders for solar, no dearth of orders for battery energy storage systems.

items.statement: EV leasing and solar businesses each expected to contribute half of EBITDA next year.
items.quote: Half of the EBITDA next year will come from the EV leasing business and half of the EBITDA will come from the solar business.

items.statement: Promoter pledges for IREDA and PFC to remain for 2-3 years; some pledges may reduce in six months.

I think that you could see the pledge coming down in about six months' time.

items.statement: Rs. 900 crores fund raise to open in early June; money expected from June.

items.statement: EV leasing book is pristine with no payment delays.

items.quote: Well, the MNC Aerospace is the sector margins are not inferior. To begin with, we look at margins of 20% to 22% but it would improve as we streamline the operations, as we ramp up.

items.statement: Targets order inflow of INR2000-3000 crores in next quarter and INR5000-6000 crores for FY25.
items.quote: The company is targeting an order inflow of INR2000-3000 crores during the next quarter s and however the total order inflow for FY24 is targeting around INR5000-6000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected to be flat, similar to last year's figure.
items.quote: So with all that, I think really if we go -- that's the last year figure that will be the greatest thing what we can do in this. We will try our best in this.

items.statement: Guidance for EBITDA margin between 15%-16% for FY25.
items.quote: but our guidance is between 15%-16% definitely we could be able to deliver.

items.statement: Expects capex of INR100-120 crores for FY25.
items.quote: but we are expecting somewhere around INR100 crores to INR120 crores will be there actually.

items.statement: Plans to infuse INR350 crores equity in FY25, INR90 crores in FY26, and INR64 crores in FY27 for HAM projects.
items.value: INR350 crores, INR90 crores, INR64 crores
items.quote: The additional equity requirement for INR504 crores to be infused as INR350 crores, INR90 crores and INR64 crores for FY25, '26 and '27 respectively.

items.statement: Total order book as of March 31, 2024 is INR5305 crores, excluding INR1200 crores from two HAM projects without appointed date.
items.quote: Now, coming to the order book position, as of March 31, 2024, the company has a total order book position of INR5305 crores.

items.statement: Plans to cut margins by 3% to 4% to win jobs due to market aggression.
items.quote: So, unless if you cut down little bit margins like 2%, 3%, 4% definitely it may not be possible for you to win the job at all, we have a taken some calls by which we were successful in that Mysuru and Ongolu bids and going forward we would like to cut down margins by 3% to 4% I think.

items.statement: Pending receivables from Telangana government amount to INR800 crores, with INR600 crores certified.
items.quote: As of now, the receivables from the Telangana government amount to roughly INR800 crores which include portion awaiting certification.

items.statement: Expects INR70 crores from Vivad Se Vishwas in first half of FY25.
items.quote: are expecting around INR70 crores out of that. So right now, one is there which we are expecting in this year and others is anyway we have gone to the court actually

items.statement: Optimistic about new project awarding after elections and new government.
items.quote: We are optimistic for new project awarding activities after the results are out and the new government takes chair.

items.statement: Exploring new sectors like irrigation, metro, tunnelling, railway, mining, solar for de-risking.
items.quote: We continue to explore new geographical and undertake unconventional projects like irrigation, metro, t unnelling, railway, mining, solar, etc.

items.statement: Provision for impairment and doubtful advances for KNR Muzaffarpur Barauni Tollway due to insufficient toll collection.
items.value: INR55 crores, INR32 crores, INR10 crores
items.quote: During Q4 FY24, the company has mad e a provision towards impairment of equity of INR55 crores and towards doubtful advance of INR32 crores and towards doubtful trade receivables of INR10 crores for one of its subsidiary companies i.e., KNR Muzaffarpur Barauni Tollway Private Limited as the toll collection of the project is not sufficient to recover the cost of the maintenance and the debt obligat

items.statement: Received claim amount of INR135 crores principal and INR109 crores interest in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: During the year Q4 FY24, the company received a claim amount of INR135 crores towards principal and INR109 crores towards interest, which were shown in the revenue and other income respectively.

items.statement: HAM projects fiscal progress as of March 31, 2024: Magadi-Somwarpet 83%, Oddanchatram-Madathukulam 99%, Ramanattukara-Valanchery 73%, Valanchery-Kappirikkad 75%, Chittor-Thatchur 51%.

items.statement: Invested INR488 crores out of INR992 crores equity for eight HAM assets as of March 31, 2024.
items.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the company has already invested INR488 crores out of INR992 crores revised equity requirement for the eight existing HAM assets.

items.statement: Appointed date received for Marripudi to Somvarappadu project on February 10, 2024; awaiting for two Karnataka HAM projects.
items.quote: The company received 10th February 2024 as the appointed date for the 6-laning of Marripudi to Somvarappadu, which is a part of Bengaluru-Vijayawada Economic Corridor. This project is the Greenfield Highway awarded by the NH AI on HAM model under Bharat Mala Pariyojana Phase-1 in the state of Andhra Pradesh. We are still awaiting the appointed date for 2 HAM project in the state of Karnataka namel

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue target of at least Rs 1,200 crore and EBITDA margin of 5-10%
items.quote: if you look at the consolidated numbers, for this year we could generate around 3% positive EBITDA. And we expect that we would cross at least 1200 crore in 2024-25. And, and would try to have consolidated EBITDA of not 3%, at least between 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Minimum IRR hurdle of 25% for new capex projects, targeting over 30%
items.quote: We have minimum IRR that we are looking at is 25% for the new project for the CAPEX, but our target is to have more than 30% IRR on any new projects.

items.statement: No significant capex needed to improve existing dyes and intermediates business; focus on product mix changes within current assets
items.quote: I don't think it will require more CAPEX for it. A little bit of investment, few here and there, it's fine but it would not require any significant CAPEX to improve the existing business, it was more of our own abil ity to change within the existing investment that we have in this plant

items.statement: Overall capacity utilisation ~50%; intermediates 36%, dyes <20%, basic chemicals ~60%
items.quote: capacity utilization on intermediate side is 36%, dyes side is less than 20% because we have large capacities and basic chemicals is about 60% and overall average if you look at all facilities together out of 68,725 tonne we have produced 34,388 tonne so which is about 50% of the production capacity.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA turned positive ~3% in FY24; Q4 FY24 consolidated EBITDA profit Rs 5 crore vs loss prior quarters
items.quote: for this year we could generate around 3% positive EBITDA. And we expect that we would cross at least 1200 crore in 2024-25. And, and would try to have consolidated EBITDA of not 3%, at least between 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA deficit restricted due to better material margins in commodities market; hopes margins continue to strengthen
items.quote: During quarter four 2024 company was able to restrict EBITDA deficit as compared to previous three quarters mainly on account of better material margins in commodities market. Hopefully the material margins continue to strengthen in coming quarters

items.statement: Expects demand in international market to pick up, enabling manufacturers to sell at better prices and earn profits
items.quote: Hopefully the material margins continue to strengthen in coming quarters and demand in international market picks up and also manufacturers are able to sell their products at better prices, enabling manufacturers to earn profits.

items.statement: Lonsen Kiri Q4 revenue Rs 88 crore and EBITDA Rs 18 crore (40% stake), up from Rs 64 crore and Rs 11 crore in Q4 FY23
items.quote: The revenue and EBITDA of Lonsen Kiri for quarter four 2024 for 40% stake of Kiri included in this financials amounted to Rs.88 crore and Rs.18 crore respectively, which were Rs.64 crores and Rs.11 crores for quarter four 2023.

items.statement: Singapore International Commercial Court judgment May 20, 2024: Kiri entitled to Rs 603.8 million priority from en bloc sale of DyStar; long-stop date Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: According to the order Kiri is entitled to receive Rs.603.8 million as the priority from the en block sale of entire shareholding of DyStar. The remaining balance from the proceeds of sale of DyStar with go to Senda. Moreover, the court has ruled that en block sale of DyStar will proceed without any reserve price, and the long-stop date is set for December 31st, 2025.

items.statement: Promoters actively arranging funds to increase stake; process ongoing for over a year
items.quote: promoters are highly inclined to increase their stake, and it all depends on the arrangement that the promoters are able to do to increase the stake, the intention is very positive. And we h ave been working on for quite a long for more than a year

items.statement: Active thoughts on buyback once funds received if market not recognizing value
items.quote: Active thoughts on that, s o once the fun d comes and market is not recognizing value, and that is the option absolutely

items.statement: Capital gains tax on DyStar proceeds estimated at 10% without indexation
items.quote: Based on the advice we have as we would not be taking into account the indexing. We will be paying 10% capital gain tax.

items.statement: Majority of DyStar proceeds to fund new growth projects outside dyes/intermediates (renewable energy, green hydrogen, EV, petrochemical derivatives); targeting >25-30% IRR
items.quote: majority of the funds would be used for the future growth and for the projects, and also a number of initiatives which the management has been thinking. So, majority of the funds would be utilized for the future, for the growth and for taking Kiri to the new levels.

items.statement: Litigation expenses to continue until sale proceeds received, though lower than before; Senda may appeal within 30 days (by ~June 20), appeal could take ~9 months but will not stop sale process
items.quote: we would continue to incur the litigation expenses, till the funds come to our account. And what has been happening now is , we have been actively engaged through our lawyers with the receiver s o, receiver is trying to sell the company and wherever the involvement of shareholders, Kiri, Senda and DyStar as a company, we need to be continuously involved in helping them in the process

items.statement: If DyStar not sold by Dec 31, 2025 long-stop date, court may order liquidation; but management sees enough buyer interest to avoid this
items.quote: if let us say in the worst case scenario, till December 2025, the company's not sold by any kind of reason, then it needs to be liquidated as per the courts directions, but I don't think that is going to happen, because there is enough interest, practically speaking, the buyers are preparing to bid and there are multiple options.

items.statement: DyStar cash balance ~$508 million at Dec 2023 year-end; estimated at least $550 million by March 2024
items.quote: As on year end which was the December end for DyStar financial year, it was around 508 million. And by end of March, I don't have balance sheet item, but looking at the profitability and the cash generation, I would say the cash in the company would be at least 550 million may be more than that.

items.statement: DyStar valuation range 6-10x EBITDA (~$150 million baseline); recent comparable Huntsman acquisition at ~7.8x EBITDA
items.quote: if you look at the cash free debt free basis, and if you look at the consistency of EBITDA of DyStar, based on the past established performance is around 150 million. So, depending on how the buyers recognize it, the valuation may vary from seven times EBITDA to six times EBITDA to even eight, 10 times EBITDA.

items.statement: Multiple strategic and financial buyers interested in DyStar; no reserve price in en bloc sale; receiver (Deloitte) controls process, shareholders cannot impose conditions
items.quote: based on my information there are multiple buyers looking at DyStar and interested in DyStar some are strategic buyers, and there are many funds also, some of the large funds, what I have learned are also looking at the buying DyStar. So, there is enough interest in the market and there are many prospective buyers at the moment who are interested to be for the company.

items.statement: Kiri to receive crystallized Rs 603.8 million regardless of DyStar sale price; balance goes to Senda
items.quote: Yes, we will get 603.8 million that's what we are going to get. So, if the company is being sold at 700 million, or it is being sold at 2 billion, whatever is the balance amount will go to Senda, Kiri will get only 603.8 million, irrespective of what price DyStar is sold. Our number is decided, it's a crystallized number.

items.statement: Kiri plans to appeal court decision on interest component; Senda has 30 days from May 20 to appeal enforcement order
items.quote: We have a legal advice to strongly file an appeal for the interest part which haven't got so, interest part is an important part and we have a very strong reasoning our belief is strong. So, we will file appeal for the interest.

items.statement: Promoters keen to increase stake from current 26.72%; process depends on fund arrangement
items.quote: promoters are highly inclined to increase their stake, and it all depends on the arrangement that the promoters are able to do to increase the stake, the intention is very positive.

items.statement: Focus on changing product mix within existing dyes/intermediates capacity to improve profitability; adding new products, restarting idle buildings
items.quote: we could change products within the category of intermediates and dyes, and also some related chemistry. And that could be our efforts to even at 1000, 1500 level, we come back to the decent profitability by changing our product mix, definitely that is possible, we are trying to endeavor to do it

items.statement: No operational disruption or customer pushback at DyStar post receiver appointment; operations normal
items.quote: there is no disturbance in operations at all. We don't see any impact on the day-to-day operations of DyStar. And we also don't see any impact at least we are knowing offer or we have been informed about on the customers running away from DyStar, haven't seen that nothing like that, it has been normal as it was before.

items.statement: DyStar revenue stagnant for 15 years ($850M-$1.1B range); peers Archroma, Huntsman, Clariant also stagnant; shareholder dispute hindered growth capex
items.quote: For the last five years, as you have rightly said the company's revenue has been ranging from 850 million to 1.1 billion and not only last five years, before we acquired DyStar in 2010, if I remember correctly, 2008 revenue was also $1 billion. So, in the last 15 years, the company's revenue has not been grown or increased much but it has remained range bound.

items.statement: DyStar EBITDA margin ~15% consistently over last 5 years; baseline EBITDA ~$150 million
items.quote: Last five years EBITDA is about 15% in DyStar. So, what DyStar has gained from is the restructuring, which was done post-acquisition by Kiri and Lonsen and that has turned the company into a good profitable path

items.statement: Consolidated cash erosion stopped; Q4 FY24 EBITDA neutral excluding legal costs
items.quote: if you take out the legal cost by the way, in the last quarter we are EBITDA neutral. So, at least the cash has stopped now eroding.

items.statement: Rail EBITDA per TEU guidance for FY25 is INR9,500, with annual increments and costs factored in.
items.quote: So we attended 9,500 for this financial year. So I think that is a good range, it will fluctuate a little bit up and down depending on quarter imbalance and volume mix, but this is a good range to be here.

items.statement: CFS EBITDA per TEU target for rest of year is INR1,500.
items.quote: But like Manoj said INR1,500 is what we are targeting for the rest of the year.

items.statement: General maintenance capex for next year is about INR20 crores.
items.quote: And with general maintenance capex would be about INR20 crores for the next year.

items.statement: Jaipur terminal to be operational in FY26.
items.quote: So it will be operational in FY '26, and we will be taking a call very soon on whether to go for CFS or the straightway buy some more land and go for the ICD.

items.statement: Expect double stacking to return to standard 40% within next 2 quarters.
items.quote: So it was pretty stable between, say, 40% - 42% this quarter that is declined as much mainly on account of the Red Sea crisis that happened. There was a irregularity of volume. We had to run some empty trains, one directional trains. So there was higher underpinned cost resulting into lower double stacking. Like for example, suddenly, there was a discharge of a few thousand containers at Mundra po

items.statement: Expect double stacking in Q1 to be better than Q4.
items.quote: So in Q1, probably we expect double stacking to be better than Q4. Even though imbalance, maybe not what it was earlier, 60:40, it will be slightly better than that.

items.statement: Looking at double-digit growth in rail business.
items.quote: We're still looking at double-digit growth. So we have to see, but we have seen a volume uptick and expect that trend to continue going forward into next quarter, Q2 should be better than Q1 and even the pipeline ahead of that is also strong.

items.statement: Expect to buy land for new terminal within this financial year.
items.quote: So we expect that, within this year, we will buy the land. But of course, it takes a while to make it operational over the last two years from the date acquisition of land.

items.statement: Lucknow warehouse to be functional in July; Kolkata in September.
items.quote: Lucknow will be up and ready for use in July, and Kolkata will be in September.

items.statement: Krishnapatnam expansion to complete this year; Bhubaneswar in FY26.
items.quote: Krishnapatnam, yes. Bhubaneswar, no, it will go into FY '26.

items.statement: Effective tax rate to increase to 5-6% next year, then full tax rate in FY27.
items.quote: Right now, our effective tax rate is about 2%. Next year, one location is going away, so it might go up to 5% - 6%. And then '27 is when the full tax rate, then we'll start becoming, but w e'll use the MAT credit for 4 years after that

items.statement: MAT credit to be used by FY32.
items.quote: I mean, basically, we'll be using the MAT credit that we generate in FY '27 and '28 by FY '32 is our projection.

items.statement: Expect Faridabad terminal to be double stacked in next 3-4 months.
items.quote: And in the last quarter, the double stacking dipped by around 5%. So even though the -- yes, from 40% to 35%. So it is the main reason for the profitability of the revenue going down. So whenever the volumes pick up, our double stacking will go up, and it is also pertinent to mention that Faridabad terminal will be double stacked soon. Some works by the railways going on, and we expect that to hap

items.statement: Expect double stacking to go closer to 45% to 50% once JNPT and Faridabad are added.
items.quote: Yes. So once it also goes way to JNPT and Faridabad also add we want to go closer to 45% to 50%, which in the past we've done about 43% and 44% are the highest. So we are more than capable of doing that, but it all depends on the volume mix and overall import export imbalance.

items.statement: Expect slight improvement in export mix going forward.
items.quote: Going forward, we don't really have a clear trend shipping lines also a re committing to what the mix will be like, but maybe a slight improvement will happen more in favour, exports

items.statement: Expect to see something happen on new ICD within this financial year.
items.quote: So we are actively pursuing this, and you should probably see something happen within this financial year. But it is a work in progress.

items.statement: Targeting mid-teens annualized growth for domestic biscuits in FY25.
items.quote: Yes, FY '24, that's what I'm coming to -- that was also mid-teens growth in FY '24 also. And FY '25 also, we are targeting that on an annualized basis for the full year, we should be able to achieve a mid-teens kind of growth.

items.statement: Aiming for mid-to-high teens annualized growth at company level.
items.quote: So we have been consistently saying that we want to maintain at a company level mid -to-high teens kind of growth, right? And that's what we have achieved this year also. So that's what we are striving for to achieve on a consistent basis on an annualized basis, mid-to-high teens kind of growth.

items.statement: Capex for FY24 and FY25 around INR550-570 crores.
items.quote: So as of now, around INR550 crore, INR560 crores is the capex between the last financial year and this financial year. Last financial year, what we have capex which we have spent and the balance would happen in this financial year.

items.statement: Margins may remain around same level with slight moderation in coming quarter.
items.quote: So yes. It may remain around the same level, right, at this point of time. But yes, the higher contribution of export, we don't expect to continue at the same pace. So there could be some moderation on account of that.

items.statement: Expect demand to recover from Q2 FY25 due to good monsoons and controlled inflation.
items.quote: We all know the good monsoons are projected for this year and the inflation is also coming in control. So we are also very confident that starting quarter 2 of this financial year, we should see the demand coming back and definitely post Diwali, it should be a good run.

items.statement: Competitive intensity led to consumer offers and price drops; company took action in Q3 and Q4.
items.quote: In terms of competitive index also starting, I think the quarter 3 of last financial year, there has been more competition from all the companies, especially the leader in the category has rolled out a lot of consumer offers kind of dropping the consumer price of the product. And we have also taken a respective action in quarter 3, quarter 4 in terms of being competitive in the market.

items.statement: Premiumization reached 37% in Q4, up 20%.
items.quote: And our premiumization percentage even starting from a part of this year, to quarter 4, we have reached 37%. So there is a 20% jump in the premiumization percent.

items.statement: Red Sea issue may take 1-2 quarters to resolve, impacting working capital.
items.quote: But the Red Sea impact is something which can take another 1 or 2 quarters to come down because this is a force majeure kind of situation for us or for anybody. So hopefully, it should also kind of come down over the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Capex funded two-thirds by debt, one-third by own resources.
items.value: two third debt, one third own
items.quote: There will be more debt. So the whole idea is to keep it in the range of one third- two third kind of a scenario. The two third will come through borrowings and one third will be coming from our own resources.

items.statement: Project Impact 1.0 cost transformation benefits to start reflecting from Q4 FY25.
items.quote: So that program has just started and it's more on a study and scoping stage. So in terms of benefits to start coming in from this program, it would start reflecting in some manner in quarter 4 of this financial year and then in the subsequent quarters of the next financial year.

items.statement: Dubai subsidiary to start dispatching containers and billing from coming quarter.
items.quote: Yes. Hi, So basically, the Dubai subsidiary has -- we are going to start dispatching our containers and billing it through the Dubai route from the coming quarter. And this time, the subsidiary will be fully active.

items.statement: Bakebest bun and bread lines to come up by end of Q4 FY25, sales after that.
items.quote: Bakebest -- I'm Anoop Bector here. It is an investment which we are doing in putting up a state-of-art bun line and bread line, right? and that investments are happening right now and they will -- only the lines will come up in the end of this quarter this year, '24-'25. So you will only see sales after that.

items.statement: Cremica brand to be present in Dubai Lulu from Q3 or Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Also, this year, we will start being present in Dubai, Lulu with our own brand and that should be happening from Q3 or Q4. The negotiations are currently ongoing and we will be bearing the listing cost and investing in the market.

items.statement: Employee cost to remain elevated due to new plants and leadership hiring.
items.quote: Yes. So because if you look at other expenses, so other expenses, I'll tell you on an annualized basis, if you add other expenses and employee expenses, then for the both financial year, it is 31.7%. So a bit of a reclassification and definitely employee expense has gone up for the reasons I told you too.

items.statement: Cremica acquisition to complete in coming quarter, timelines being worked out.
items.quote: So we have acquired that. So this is a transaction, which should happen in the coming quarter or sometime -- the time lines are being worked out. So it is more about the bakery operations.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected between INR270 crores and INR300 crores.
items.quote: Let's keep a range of between INR270 crores to INR300 crores as a top line, sir.

items.statement: Net profit margin expected between 20% and 23%.
items.quote: That has always been consistent in the history between 20% to 23%, sir.

items.statement: Minimum PAT of INR60 crores expected for FY25.
items.quote: It should be a minimum of INR60 crores, sir.

items.statement: Additional capex of INR100 to INR120 crores planned if order book reaches INR1100 crores.
items.quote: We will have to do an additional capex of INR100 to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Total capex of INR160 crores planned for cutter suction dredgers and allied crafts.
items.quote: That is why we will have to do a total capex of INR160 crores this year for the additional orders on cutter suction dredger and the allied crafts.

items.statement: Order book expected to reach INR1100 crores with additional INR400 crores.
items.quote: We intend to add another INR400 crores very soon. That will take our order book to INR1,100 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to continue around 30%.
items.quote: However, we remain optimistic about our revenue outlook and expect to see improved performance in the coming years, with continued EBITDA margins of around 30%.

items.statement: Bahrain EBIT margins expected to lower from 60% due to vessel upgrades.
items.quote: It will lower down going forward because we will be doing some upgradations to the vessel. So there will be some expenditure to it.

items.statement: Sand prices in Bahrain are market-driven, with fixed prices for first 6 months, then free to increase.
items.quote: Yes it is not a fixed price contract. It is market driven. So this is not with the government of Bahrain. This is with private entities and we had fixed the price for the first 6 months. We are free to increase the price as driven by the market after the initial 6 months.

items.statement: Bahrain sand market prices currently between 3.75 to 4.25 Bahraini dinars per cubic ton.
items.value: 3.75 to 4.25 Bahraini dinars per cubic ton
items.quote: presently the sand market is anywhere in Bahrain between $2.5 per ton to $2.75 per ton which translates to 3.75, oh sorry BD, I meant BD not dollars, Bahraini dinars. 3.75 Bahraini dinars to 4.25 Bahraini dinars per cubic ton.

items.statement: 60% of sand mined is under fixed sale contracts for next five years, 40% for open market.
items.quote: So 60% of our sand that we mine has been agreed into a sale for the next five years. So we already have our fixed contract wherein we can vary the price as per the market but it is going to be picked up by our clients. 40% we have kept it for the open market.

items.statement: Fleet to consist of 24 vessels, with plans to expand to 40 or more crafts.
items.quote: With these contract wins, our fleet will soon consist of 24 vessels, which remarks our commitment to expand our fleet to 40 or more crafts in the next few years.

items.statement: Risk factors include equipment efficiency and understanding site material.
items.quote: See, the risk factors in contracts are limited to two we consider is identification of a proper equipment to the highest efficiency and to have a good understanding of the type of material that we will encounter in the contract.

items.statement: Promoters intend to buy back shares next week.
items.quote: No actually presently we have decided that we intend to buy back our share on the valuation in which it is available. So you will see next week the promoters actually buying back some of the equity.

items.statement: Company to list on BSE and NSE main boards within 60 to 90 days.
items.quote: Within definitely within the next 60 to 90 days.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20% for FY25
items.quote: we were expecting a 15% to 20% growth on the top line in fiscal FY25 as well as fiscal FY26

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance deferred by 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Right now, EBITDA margin guidance will be difficult. It will take another one or two more quarters to give concrete EBITDA margin guidance.

items.statement: Export demand recovery expected in current quarter with good order position
items.quote: During current quarter, we have seen signs of reversal. We registered full year EBITDA of Rs.102 crores with 15% EBITDA margin as compared to 24% EBITDA margin achieved in FY23.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin at 15% vs 24% in FY23 due to lower price realization
items.quote: We registered full year EBITDA of Rs.102 crores with 15% EBITDA margin as compared to 24% EBITDA margin achieved in FY23.

items.statement: Prices stopped declining but rising slowly; raw material costs stable
items.quote: On the pricing front, the price has stopped declining, but they are rising very slow. And the raw material costs, they have also become stable.

items.statement: Order book around Rs.100 crores
items.quote: Around Rs.100 crores order book in

items.statement: Capex of Rs.110 crores planned for FY25 (Rs.50 crores IPL, Rs.60 crores Shalvis)
items.quote: Capex of Rs.50 crores for IPL and Rs.60 crores for Shalvis Specialties is planned for FY25.

items.statement: Installed capacity increased to 24,200 metric tons for technical and intermediates
items.quote: Furthermore, we have increased our present installed capacity of technical and intermediates to 24,200 metric tons.

items.statement: Land acquired adjacent to Sandila plant for future expansion
items.quote: In addition to this capacity expansion, we have taken a significant step towards facilitating our expansion efforts by acquiring a land adjacent to our Sandila plant.

items.statement: Key product prices (Prosulfocarb, Captan, Folpet) fell 10-12% in FY24
items.quote: Sir, prices for all these products, they have fallen a bit maybe around 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Three herbicide technicals received EU technical equivalence; registrations in UK, US, Canada
items.quote: During this period, 3 of our advanced herbicide technical products have been granted technical equivalence certification by the European Union. Apart from this, we have also received registrations in U.K., Canada and U.S..

items.statement: Planning 3 more product registrations in Australia and Europe; 12+ products in CIB pipeline
items.quote: And this year we are planning to register again three more products in Australian market and European market and our registration request for the local CIB is for more than 12 products.

items.statement: Signed 3-year contract with Japanese company for intermediate supply
items.quote: We entered in a 3-year contract with a prominent Japanese company to supply an intermediate.

items.statement: Export revenue declined 44% to Rs.270 crores in FY24; Europe and Australia major geographies

items.quote: And in case of renovation capex, it will be about around Rs. 45-50 crore per annum plus the Flurys will be about Rs. 100-120 crore capex over the period.

items.statement: Park Pune 200 rooms at cost of Rs. 200 crore spread over three years; Vizag 100 rooms at Rs. 100 crore.

items.statement: Sale of apartments to add roughly Rs. 100 crore to cash flows every year for next three years.
items.quote: The sale of apartments should add roughly about Rs.100 crore to our cash flows every year for the next three years.

items.statement: Foresee persistent demand-supply imbalance, positioning for double-digit growth; hospitality super-cycle to last over a decade.
items.quote: We foresee a persistent demand-supply imbalance in the industry, especially in the key growth markets, which positions us favourably for anticipated double-digit growth. items.statement: Plan to add 383 keys on asset-light side next year, including specific hotels.
items.quote: We plan to add about 38 3 keys on the asset-light side of the model next year. FY26 includes about 43 keys in Calcutta, an additional hotel in Indore, 118 keys, Lucknow 100 keys, Alibag 50 keys and Patna 42 keys.

items.statement: Expect to remain net cash positive throughout development cycle using cash accruals and apartment sale proceeds.
items.quote: Our cash accruals rising out of operations and sale proceeds of apartments will keep us net cash positive throughout the development cycle and this is a significant part of our strategy.

items.statement: Guided 35-40% revenue growth in FY25 with 20% organic growth and at least INR1,000 crores from acquisitions
items.quote: We are very confident of delivering 35% to 40% revenue growth in FY '25 driven by organic growth of 20% against an expected IPM growth of 8% to 10% and at least INR1,000 crores of distributed acquisitions.

items.statement: Guided 100 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY25 over FY24
items.quote: This revenue expansion driving operating leverage, apart from our procurement efficiencies and product mix, can help us to deliver 100 basis point improvement in EBITDA margins in FY '25.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin improved 91 bps to 2.9% driven by gross margin expansion and operating leverage
items.quote: Operating margin for FY '24 is at INR2.9%, which is an improvement of 91 basis points compared to last year. This margin expansion is primarily due to higher gross margins and operating leverage.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin improved 49 bps to 2.8% on gross margin improvement
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 2.8% which improved by 49 basis points. The improvement in operating profitability can be attributed to better gross margins.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 84 bps to 9% in FY24 from procurement efficiencies and service fee income
items.quote: Gross profit margin stood at 9% for the year, an improvement of 84 basis points from last year. This enhancement in gross margin can be attributed to procurement efficiencies which have allowed us to manage costs more effectively and increase service fee income from our third-party marketing business.

items.statement: Acquisition outlay estimated at INR250-300 crores enterprise value for INR1,000 crores revenue
items.quote: So, typically we have guided that based on historical averages if we look at typically our enterprise value is like one-fourth of the revenue. So you can expect INR250 crores to INR300 crores enterprise value for a thousand crore of revenue in that ballpark range.

items.statement: Network expanded to 79 warehouses across 39 cities serving 86,300 pharmacies and 3,500 hospitals; three new acquisitions will add Ahmedabad and Bijapur taking presence to 41 cities
items.quote: The newly acquired entities will add Ahmedabad and Bijapur to our opera tional network. This acquisition will increase our total presence to 41 cities across
