items.quote: Our product mix is driven by those products which inherently give more margin, for example, consumable or medical devices which carry a gross margin which are 1.5x to 2x of pharma gross margin, right. So, when I speak of product mix, it's not only private label, it includes moving the product mix towards higher gross margin products which are let's say non-pharma category.

items.statement: Targeting 200,000-250,000 retail pharmacy reach in next 2-3 years from current 86,300
items.quote: Once you have to -- our next 2-3 years, if we reach 200,000-250,000 retail reach that will be a substantial reach within the country. After which your new geography additions could be very limited.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used to reduce working capital debt leading to interest cost optimization
items.quote: That is what you can see in the reduction in the debt for us. So, that has resulted in the interest cost optimization as well for that one and a half month.

items.statement: Scale enables higher gross margins from manufacturers through data and ability to deliver higher growth
items.quote: Primarily two things, one is data and the second is the ability to give them higher growth.

items.statement: Revenue grew 19% in FY24 vs IPM growth of 7.6%; Q4 grew 17% vs IPM 6%
items.quote: Further, FY '24 has been an eventful year for us with total operating revenue of INR39,223 million which is an increase of 19% over last year against a pharmaceutical industry growth rate of 7.6% and accompanied by an expansion in margins which led us to turn back positive for the year.

items.statement: Normalized ROCE improved from 6.1% to 10.2%; normalized ROE improved to 5.8% from negative
items.quote: During FY '24, we have witnessed a strong improvement in our return profile of the company with a normalized ROCE improving from 6.1% to 10.2%, whereas our normalized return on equity improved to 6% (to be read as 5.8%) from a negative last year.

items.statement: Sales plus delivery headcount ~1,000; will increase with growth
items.quote: So, we have around 1000 people, which is sales plus delivery, some people double up as sales as well as delivery, right? So, together we have around 1000 people in the company who is doing the job of sales plus delivery, which is booking the order, collecting the money and sometime delivering the product also.

items.quote: For example in Bangalore our market share will be between 15% to 20%. In Vizag our market share will be in double digits. In Cochin our market share will be in double digits. In Goa our market share will be in double digits.

items.statement: Two active third-party marketing contracts with Roche and Abbott; working on more
items.quote: So, we have two contracts like that, which is currently in operation. One is, of course, the Roche one and another is with Abbott. Those two are continuing while we are working on with other similar propositions with other companies, but others have not been concluded yet.

items.statement: Operating expenses 6% of revenue: 4% fixed unit-level (mainly manpower), 1% variable (sales commission, delivery), 1% corporate
items.quote: Out of this 5%, 1% is corporate. So, 4% is fixed at the unit level. 1% is variable and 1% is corporate cost. That is how you should read it. And this 4% predominantly will have manpower cost.

items.statement: Acquisition execution risk mitigated by deep pipeline with multiple targets per micro-market; Plan B/C available if deals fall through
items.quote: So we have a very robust pipeline as Prabhat mentioned that means in every single micro market that we are currently looking at acquiring we are talking to multiple partners in the micro market. So even if one transaction or one particular deal doesn't happen, we have alternate plan B, plan C available in the same micro market to actually go ahead and then conclude on those transactions.

items.statement: Maharashtra expansion planned in Pune, Nashik, Aurangabad, Jalgaon beyond current Mumbai presence
items.quote: So in Maharashtra, for example, we would want more centers to be open, we are exploring in Pune, in Nasik, in Aurangabad, in Jalgaon various other micro-markets.

items.statement: IPO completed February 2024 raising INR951 crores; INR158 crores deployed in working capital and debt reduction
items.quote: With the successful completion of our IPO in February 2024, we have strengthened our balance sheet giving us the financial flexibility to pursue these strategic initiatives.

items.statement: Engineering business growth expected at least last year's, with subdued projection of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Engineering margins expected to return to FY23 level of 9.1% in FY25.
items.quote: We do expect to improve on this significantly. On a consol basis, we saw for the full year roughly 7.7% margin. And for FY '22-'23, this number was around 9.1%. And we do expect that we will at least come back to that level.

items.statement: Engineering margin drag from unforeseen cost increases expected to continue for 1-2 quarters, then improve.
items.quote: Overall, the rest of the project margins remain healthy. This one contract where we have witnessed unforeseen price increases, we expect the drag would continue for maybe 1 to 2 quarters. And thereafter things should improve significantly.

items.statement: Engineering order book at end of March 2024 stood at Rs. 3,546 crores.
items.quote: At the end of the financial year, March 2024, the total order book for Engineering division stood at Rs. 3,546 crores.

This is roughly around Rs. 120 crores. The other one, is from UAE and that value is roughly in the range of Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: Domestic enquiry bank robust; finalization of large opportunities expected to accelerate in next few months.
items.quote: The domestic enquiry bank is robust, and we are hopeful that the finalization of some of the large value opportunities would accelerate in the next few months.

items.statement: Chemical segment volumes expected to continue improving over coming year; margins to maintain current levels if global environment and raw material prices stable.
items.quote: Overall, we do see that the volumes in the business would continue to improve over the coming year. items.statement: Sequential pickup in international chemical volumes anticipated to continue over coming quarters.
items.quote: There has been a sequential pickup in the volumes from the international market and we anticipate this to continue over the coming quarters also.

items.statement: Middle East situation impacted costs and increased shipping times.
items.quote: But we are seeing a bit of an impact over the last maybe few months due to the situation in the Middle East, which has impacted costs to some extent, and also the shipping times have gone up.

items.statement: UP contract execution delayed due to elections; Q1 FY25 expected to see continuing pressure.

items.statement: UP contract expected to be executed by end of this financial year, awaiting resumption after elections.
items.quote: We are expecting by the end of this financial year that contract should be executed, and we await the resumption of pace after the election process has been completed.

items.statement: Mapril revenue impact for full year around Rs. 92 crores; margins lower than standalone chemical segment.
items.quote: On an overall basis for the full year, the revenue impact of Mapril is in the region of around Rs. 92 crores.

items.statement: Consumer business investments to continue; significant volume growth expected, but no timeline for positive bottom line.
items.quote: The investments in ramping up this volume to a much higher level will continue. We do hope that we would be able to start seeing a positive bottom line soon. items.statement: Working capital levels expected to remain in line with FY23 and FY24 levels going forward.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect that the working capital level to be largely in line with what we have been shown at FY '23 March and also what we are showing now at FY '24.

items.statement: Receivables expected to normalize around midyear.
items.quote: The normalized level, for example, on the receivable side is what you should see around midyear because the end of the year receivables are always at its peak.

items.statement: Engineering segment expected to grow 15% to 20%.
items.quote: And given that we are carrying a very healthy order growth, 15% to 20% growth, we will certainly hope to achieve, if not more.

items.statement: Consumer segment expected to maintain similar growth momentum.
items.quote: You would have seen that we have delivered roughly around 31% growth for the current year. And we do expect that we would maintain momentum in a similar range of growth.

items.statement: Chemical segment margins expected at similar levels if stable environment.
items.quote: As far as the Chemical segment is concerned, we should be seeing margins at similar levels as of date, provided that we continue to witness stable prices and the overall dynamics on the geopolitical side do not alter significantly.

items.statement: Chemical segment margins sustainable if stable environment.
items.quote: If we are going to see a stable environment in the future also, the margin levels are sustainable.

items.statement: Total capex for current year around Rs. 115 crores.
items.quote: The total Capex, for the current year is in the region of, Rs. 115 crores.

items.statement: Roha capex for year around Rs. 50 crores, cumulative Rs. 70 crores.
items.quote: Roha, I can share that for the year, the capex is around Rs. 50 crores. And cumulatively, we have spent around Rs. 70 crores.

items.statement: Overall Roha capex just under Rs. 400 crores.
items.quote: Yes. We have indicated earlier also the overall Capex for the Roha is just under Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Roha capex this year around Rs. 250 crores to Rs. 300 crores.
items.quote: We can't be very definitive about that as of today, but it should be around that number of Rs. 250 crores to Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Roha commercialization expected in FY '25-'26.
items.quote: We have mentioned in the earlier con call that we are expecting the commercialization in FY '25-'26 of this Roha facility.

items.statement: Roha facility to be fully utilized over next 3 to 4 years.
items.quote: We expect to fully utilize that facility over the next 3 to 4 years once the commercial production commences.

items.statement: Roha project financing: 20% internal accruals, 80% debt.
items.quote: No, as regards financing of the Roha project, 20% of that will be from internal accruals and balance will be debt.

items.statement: International order book as of March '24 end around 27%.
items.quote: International order book as of March '24 end is around 27%.

items.statement: Market size in India expected Rs. 20,000-25,000 crores per year excluding municipal.
items.value: Rs. 20,000 crores to Rs. 25,000 crores per year
items.quote: So if we exclude the municipal segment and also the purely similar construction-oriented jobs coming from the government, we would expect the market size in India to be in the range of around Rs. 20,000 crores to Rs. 25,000 crores per year.

items.statement: Unforeseen cost increase in significant contract impacted Engineering margins.
items.quote: There was one significant contract where we saw an unforeseen cost increase, and we had to, therefore, take that extra cost provision in our books. That has led to an adverse impact on the margins reported by the Engineering division.

items.statement: Working capital normalized level expected 70 to 75 days.
items.quote: So the normalized level, if I understood your question correctly, should be in the region of around 70 to 75 days.

items.statement: Customer advances Rs. 180 crores, unearned revenue Rs. 224 crores as of March end.
items.quote: The customer advance as of March end was around Rs. 180 crores and the unearned revenue was around Rs. 224 crores.

items.statement: Aims 25-30% annual AUM increase, targeting over INR500 crores by FY25 and INR600 crores by FY26.
items.quote: Way forward, we aim to achieve a 25% to 30% annual increase in A UM, with targets surpassing INR500 crores by financial year 2025 and we aim to reach INR600 crores loan book by FY '26.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% growth in P&L and income in the coming year.
items.quote: We are seeing around 20% to 25% growth in the coming year as well, both on the P&L and the income.

items.statement: Total revenue expected around INR80-85 crores conservatively.
items.quote: To be honest, INR100 crores looks tough, but total revenue should be around INR80 crores-INR85 crores at a conservative approach.

items.statement: Plans fresh disbursement of around INR200 crores this year, adding INR120 crores AUM.
items.quote: AUM, yes, definitely we are targeting to add, to disburse around INR200 crores of fresh disbursement this year. And with the rundown every month that we have of principal via collections and closures, we should be adding around INR120-odd crores of fresh AUM to the existing.

items.statement: Aims to reach 75 branches by end of FY25.
items.quote: By the end of financial year '25, we aspire to establish a total of 75 branches, enhancing our market presence and accessibility.

items.statement: Plans to open 4-5 branches in Maharashtra next quarter or Q3.
items.quote: Yes, we will be opening spoke loc ations around the branches that we have already opened and we will be entering Maharashtra very soon. So, we plan to open 4 to 5 branches in Maharashtra by in next quarter if the team joins us on time. Otherwise, in Q3.

items.statement: Plans to tie up with large lenders for micro-housing products this year.
items.quote: We also plan to tie up with a couple of large lenders, large NBFCs or small fina nce banks, for micro-housing products to be added in this year.

items.statement: Cost of borrowings expected 25 basis points lower in FY25.
items.quote: While we have added new lenders this year, majority of the borrowings that have been added in the previous financial year are from very large NBFCs or scheduled banks and small finance banks, which further gives us a broader base to borrow and the cost of borrowings should be around 25 basis points lower in the current financial year now in FY25.

items.statement: NIMs stable at 10.5-11%, expected to continue with slight improvement from vehicle loans.
items.quote: NIMs are around 10.5 t o 11% which have been stable and marginally improved. We see the same kind of NIMs going forward as well. Little bit improvement could be seen if we are able to add a good amount of two -wheeler loan, three -wheeler loan, vehicle loan and electric vehicles portfolio.

items.statement: Interest rates range 16.5-24%, average yield 19.5%.
items.quote: So, our interest rat e starts from 16 .5%, but typical yield on our portfolio is close to about 19.5%. We are also going up to 23 %, 24%. It's all profile based. So, the interest rate range is 16.5%-23%, 24%, but average yield is 19.5%.

items.statement: Foresees higher employee attrition in older geographies as a risk.
items.quote: One of the risks that we foresee is higher attrition in our employees, which is in the older geographies, not in the new geographies. The team has been stable for around 15 to 18 months with us in MP and now Gujarat.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.6%, net NPA 0.36%, expects reduction by 25-30 bps by year-end.
items.quote: And we have about 2.6% NPA, gross NPA that we have reported this year with a very comfortable provisional coverage on that. And net NPA is 0.36%. So we have done a very conservative approach there and we do n't see further slippages there. In fact, with the addition in the AUM, this number should come down by 25 to 30 basis points by end of this year.

items.statement: Plans to introduce electric vehicles and two-wheelers in vehicle loan segment.
items.quote: Furthermore, our commitment to innovation extends to introducing a new product portfolio, including electric vehicles and two -wheelers in the vehicle loan segment, to better serve our customers and drive continuous success in the evolving market landscape.

items.statement: Rights issue deferred; may consider later after AUM reaches INR500 crores.
items.quote: So we have given intimation for the rights issue, but later we deferred this agenda. The proposal was placed for the Board of Directors, but the management along with the Independent Directors of the company were in the opinion to defer the proposal of issuance of rights issue at a later date and for consideration at an appropriate time.

items.statement: Considering issuance of NCDs soon.
items.quote: Apart from that, we are also thinking of issuance of NCDs very soon. But as of now, it's completely through banks and NBFCs via the mode of term loans or small working capital limits from a couple of banks.

items.statement: Branch setup cost INR2-3 lakhs per branch, breakeven in 5-6 months.
items.quote: So, each of our branch within 6 months, 5-6 months is very given on its own. The basic infra that our branches are designed by are couple of lakhs is more than enough to get a branch ready.

items.statement: Expects to reach 100 crore capital commitment by first half of FY25.
items.quote: We are confident that by the first half of 2025, we will reach 1 00 crore capital commitment from our various partners. We have already made significant progress towards this, with almost 65 to 70 crores as of today.

items.statement: NCD of 15 crores fully committed, expected to be allocated within 30 days.
items.quote: Regarding the fundraise, I am sure some of you saw our announcement on the Bombay Stock Exchange about raising an NCD worth about 15 crores. We have been blown away by the response from subscribers.

items.statement: Expects significantly better ROEs this year versus last year.
items.quote: Obviously, compared to last year, I'm expecting this year for us to have significantly better ROEs, largely because when I compare it to last year versus this year, obviously this year we're expecting our capital to be significantly well deployed.

items.statement: ROI charged to partners typically 16.5% to 18%.
items.quote: So the capital commitment, you know, ROI that we basically typically charge could be anywhere between 16.5% to 18%. That's typically the range of ROI that a polo charges.

items.statement: NCDs raised so far below 12-13%.
items.quote: But I think today, as of now, in terms of NCDs, at least when we've raised, right? It's all been below 12-13%, right?

items.statement: Q4 90+ DPD was 2.8%, 90% from discontinued partners; expects lower going forward.
items.quote: I think in terms of NPAs, right? As you disclosed in the presentation, Q4 90 -plus DPD numbers were about 2.8%. But as we spoke about before, right? Over there also, 90% of those DPDs are actually coming from discontinued partners.

items.statement: Expects significant growth over next couple of quarters.
items.quote: We feel that moment is here, and we expect significant growth over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Majority of capital allocation now towards digital NBFCs.
items.quote: We went from primarily working with largely LSPs to, when you look at our capital allocation right now, almost the majority of our allocation being towards digital NBFCs.

items.statement: Sweet spot for loans: ticket size under a couple lakhs, duration 3-12 months.
items.value: less than a couple of lakhs; 3 to 12-month
items.quote: So we like to do loans which are probably less than a couple of lakhs in terms of ticket size, and we also like to keep the duration usually in the 3 to 12 -month range.

items.statement: Employee count may increase from 30 to 35, no significant change.
items.quote: Maybe we'll go from 30 to 35 people, but I don't foresee a significant change in terms of employees.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity currently below 0.5, headroom to go 2-3x.
items.quote: So today, very honestly, you know, our debt is insignificant, right? Like we are not even at 0.5 debt-to-equity.

items.statement: Capital commitment is total capital drawn, earning interest for 12 months.
items.quote: Yes, when I say 100 crores of capital commitment, I mean 100 crores of capital drawn. The loan book, however, can be slightly lower because the money keeps churning.

items.statement: Management targets average EBITDA margin of INR7 per liter for bulk alcohol business (ENA and ethanol combined) over the cycle
items.quote: Going forward, we believe that the bulk business, which is a combination of ENA and ethanol, our EBITDA margins in this business will be at around INR7 a liter.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 bulk alcohol EBITDA margin collapsed to near zero due to FCI rice supply discontinuation and open market rice price spike
items.quote: Frankly, there were no spreads. That's why you saw the kind of performance that you see.

items.statement: Management expects bulk alcohol margins to recover to average INR7 per liter by end of FY25 as maize crop arrives and rice prices soften
items.quote: In fact, I believe that -- by the end of this year, we will be back to our average level of margins that we have seen in the last few years, which is around INR7 per liter.

items.statement: Ethanol production shifting from rice to maize; currently over 2/3 of ethanol output expected from maize in FY25 versus negligible in FY24
items.quote: In this financial year, for ethanol, we expect over 2/3 of our ethanol production to come from maize?

items.statement: Total installed capacity now 300 million liters per year after regulatory approvals for Jharkhand and West Bengal 60 KLPD expansions
items.quote: After certain pending regulatory approvals were complete in Q4, our total installed capacity pending regulatory approvals for Jharkhand and West Bengal expansion that is, our total installed capacity now stands at 300 million liters per year.

items.statement: Bengal and Jharkhand 60 KLPD plants to add INR215-230 crores incremental revenue in FY25; UP bottling plant commissioned in April for own brands
items.quote: Bengal and Jharkhand, 60 KLPD will give you an additional revenue of anything between INR215 crores to INR230 crores.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment volume grew 170% YoY in Q4 FY24 to 0.13 million cases; full year volume 0.38 million cases, up 84% YoY
items.quote: the quarter gone by, we witnessed a sales volume of 0.13 million cases with a growth of 170%. For the full year, also the performance has been robust. Our full year volumes stood at 0.38 million cases with a growth of 84% year -on-year

items.statement: Regular & Others segment volume grew 8% YoY in Q4 FY24 to 3.43 million cases; full year volume 14.16 million cases, profitability INR1,404 million up 22% YoY
items.quote: For the full year, this number of volume stands at 14.16 million and profitability at INR1,404 million with 22% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Launching Mountain Oak and SNOSKI Vodka in Prestige & Above; RTD brand Not Out launched in Delhi; expanding distribution from 6 to 8 states in FY25
items.quote: We are also going to be expanding our distribution presence, which currently stands at 6 states to another 2 states during the coming quarters.

items.statement: Joint venture with ANSA McAL for Carib Beer distribution and contract manufacturing in India; launch expected Q1 FY26; no brewery investment until 1-2 million cases scale
items.quote: We plan to contract manufacture the beer in India to start with, and we expect launch in Q1 of FY'26.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR241 crores at end of FY24 from INR194 crores in FY23 due to new units and geographies
items.quote: Our net debt of cash -- net of cash and cash equivalents at the end of FY'25 stands at INR241 crores, a slight increase versus FY'23, which stood at INR194 crores.

items.statement: Income tax demand of INR40.93 crores received; INR30.41 crores deposited in protest and appeal filed; management believes no provision needed
items.quote: Subsequent to the year-end, the company has received assessment orders of income tax. The amount of tax demand is INR40.93 crores out of which INR5.3 crores was deposited in Q3. For the balance amount, the company has deposited INR25.11 crores in protest and has gone for appeal.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 bulk alcohol production 64.8 million liters; sales 48.7 million liters; full year power and fuel cost INR245 crores
items.quote: The production in Q4 has been 64.8 million liters. Our power and fuel cost for the entire year has been INR245 crores.

items.statement: FY25 AUM target ₹780 crore; FY26 AUM target to cross ₹1,000 crore
items.quote: Talking about business projection s, for the financial year 2025, the target AUM is ₹780 crores, and for FY26, the target AUM will cross ₹1,000 crores

items.statement: FY25 equity raise target ₹50-100 crore
items.quote: In FY25, we target to raise equity funds between ₹50 crores and ₹100 crores.

items.statement: FY25 branch target 90 branches; FY26 target to cross 100 branches
items.quote: The targeted branch count for FY25 is 90 branches, and for FY26, we aim to cross 100 branches.

items.statement: FY25 average monthly disbursement target ₹30-35 crore; annual disbursement around ₹400 crore; AUM ₹700-780 crore
items.quote: Our previous year target was for average monthly disbursement of ₹ 25 crores. For this year, if we take an average of 25% for the branches, so our average monthly target will be between ₹30 crores to ₹35 crores. And our disbursement will be around ₹400 crores hence our loan book will increase around ₹200 crores. And the AUM will be between ₹700 crores to ₹780 crores.

items.statement: Plan to open 15 new branches in Q2 FY25 in south and Maharashtra; 10-15 branches in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We plan to open 15 new branches in Q2 in the south and Maharashtra regions and 10-15 branches in Q3.

items.statement: New branches in Maharashtra (two clusters of six each), Karnataka (six), Tamil Nadu (five), Telangana (three), Andhra Pradesh (three to four)
items.quote: These new branches include two clusters in Maharashtra, each comprising six branches, along with six branches in Karnataka, five in Tamil Nadu, three in Telangana, a nd three to four in Andhra Pradesh

items.statement: New branches typically take 4-6 months to reach break-even
items.quote: It typically takes 4-6 months to achieve break-even in these new branches.

items.statement: Net interest margin on gross loan book 11.29%; spread maintained at 11%
items.quote: The company has maintained a healthy spread of 11%. The net interest margin on the gross loan book stands at 11.29%.

items.statement: Average borrowing cost 11.13% in FY24 vs 10.82% in FY23 due to repo rate increases
items.quote: Due to the increase in the repo rate, our average borrowing cost is 11.13%, compared to 10.82% in the previous year.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.29% (down from 2.50%); Net NPA 0.69% (up from 0.51%)
items.quote: The gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio is 2.29%, down from 2.50% in the previous year, while the net NPA ratio is 0.69%, up from 0.51% last year.

items.statement: Total outstanding borrowing ₹491 crore (up from ₹357 crore); mix 49% banks, 39% FIs, 12% NHB
items.quote: The company's total outstanding borrowing is ₹491 crores which was ₹357 crores last year. with 49% from banks, 39% from financial institutions, and 12% from the National Housing Bank.

items.statement: CEO Archis Jain spends 20-22 days/month in field; team of 650-700 employees
items.quote: Our team consists of approximately 650 to 700 highly skilled individuals who are dedicated to our cause.

items.statement: Fintech model not applicable in housing finance due to need for property docs, valuation, legal reports; fewer HFCs in rural areas due to fieldwork
items.quote: In rural areas, there are relatively fewer housing finance companies due to the extensive fieldwork required. Additionally, the fintech model is not applicable in housing finance companies. Fintech typically operates in unsecured loans where property documents, valuation, legal reports, and technical aspects are not required.

items.statement: Conservative 50% LTV maintained to mitigate property depreciation risk; no increase planned despite rising property prices
items.quote: Maintaining a conservative LTV margin is crucial for enhancing collection efficiency. Exceeding the appropriate LTV ratio, such as r eaching 80% to 85%, poses risks, as property values can depreciate significantly if defaults occur

items.statement: Good monsoon does not increase prepayments; instead boosts business activity and financing demand
items.quote: Good monsoon conditions do not directly lead to increased prepayments. Instead, business activity tends to surge during favorable monsoon periods. As business activity rises, individuals may require additional financing.

items.statement: Bank transfer (BT) rate 8-10% of loan book; balanced inflow/outflow
items.quote: The bank transfer, commonly referred to as BT, typically ranges from 8% to 10%. The amount transferred out from our finance company is generally reciprocated by an equivalent sum from the recipient finance company.

items.statement: ALM position comfortable; liquid funds ₹82 crore including ₹17 crore undrawn
items.quote: The company's liquidity position remains strong, with liquid funds of ₹82 crores, including ₹17 crores of undrawn funds. Our asset-liability management (ALM) position is also comfortable.

items.statement: Favorable monsoon stimulates rural income and housing demand; but no certainty factored into guidance
items.quote: Sir, during a favorable monsoon season, development is stimulated across the entire country. Monsoon plays a pivotal role in India's economy due to its significant contribution to agriculture. With increased agricultural productivity, there is a correspond ing rise in income levels, prompting people to invest in housing, expand businesses, and foster overall development

items.statement: Fixed-rate loan book; repo rate increases cause temporary NIM pressure; rate cuts would improve profits
items.quote: Sir, our client base primarily opts for fixed-rate loans. If the repo rate rises, we might experience a slight profit decline for the fiscal year. However, if the repo rate subsequently decreases, our profits will likely increase.

items.statement: Recruited 10-12 branch managers for new branches; hired industry-experienced teams to minimize training time
items.quote: Business plans have been formulated, and teams have been recruited for these locations, including the appointment of 10 to 12 branch managers.

items.statement: Management expects non-engine/non-auto components to reach 25% of revenue in about a year, later than the earlier FY25 target.
items.quote: Yes, I don't think it would be possible in this current financial year, but perhaps a year later would be possible.

items.statement: Standalone business growth not expected to be double-digit immediately; significant new contracts to start production in next 12-24 months.
items.quote: I don't think double digits would be possible immediately in the coming quarters. But I think there will be a point where we have 3 or 4 new contracts that will come into SOP, or basically start supplies all in a very short period of time in the next 12 months to 24 months.

items.statement: EMOSS Europe growth will be muted over coming quarters due to recessionary environment.
items.quote: The growth at EMOSS would be muted over the coming quarters and should be taken into account considering the general economy in Europe.

items.statement: Retrofit EV business in India targets 20-25% gross margin and 10-15% operating margin at scale of 4,000-5,000 vehicles per year.
items.quote: At a big picture kind of long term goal if you ask me and we're talking about around a 20%, 25% gross margin and about a 15% operating margin 10% to 15% operating margin is what we hope for.

items.statement: OEM EV manufacturing in India is 2-3 years away, using retrofit powertrain data.
items.quote: It is still another two to three years away I would say.

items.statement: Domestic market expected to grow 8-10% YoY over next 3-4 years, helping offset export mix.
items.quote: The domestic market is expected to grow significantly over the next 3 years to 4 years, I would say, 8%, 9%, 10% year-on-year.

items.statement: EMOSS India has good traction with 15-20 large fleet customers owning over 10,000 LCVs combined.
items.quote: Just between them, they own or operate more than 10,000 vehicles just in the LCV category.

items.statement: EMOSS India signing commercial agreements with large waste collection, biomedical waste, and pan-India logistics providers.
items.quote: EMOSS India is in the process of signing commercial agreements with several key customers, including one of India's largest service provider company for the use in waste collection application, one of India's largest biomedical waste management company and an EV-only pan-India logistics provider.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 17%, PAT margin 11%; domestic sales exceeded exports (53% vs 47%) lowering realizations.
items.quote: Total income for Q4 decreased by 0.2% year-on-year to INR176 crores. EBITDA margin was 17% and PAT margin was 11%.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin ~10%, PAT margin ~1.2%.
items.quote: Coming to the consolidated business, total consol income decreased by about 8% to INR261 crores. EBITDA margin was about 10% and PAT margin was about 1.2%.

items.statement: New foundry and machine shop awards ensure full capacity utilization for next 4-5 years; new assembled camshaft plant in Solapur based on strong order book.
items.quote: In the last year, PCL has been awarded new business in the foundry as well as the machine shop that will ensure complete utilization of our capacities at least for the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: MEMCO secured additional business from key customers in fuel injection and critical instrumentation.
items.quote: MEMCO has already secured additional business from its key customers in the fuel injection business as well as critical instrumentation business.

items.statement: MFT Germany awarded new HVAC customer business for high-volume components starting production this calendar year.
items.quote: At MFT also, we have a new customer, which is in the HVAC space and has awarded us business for certain high-volume components that we will be starting production this year, this calendar year.

items.statement: PCL India ramped up non-engine brake component volumes; shipping commercially for last 2-3 months with higher volumes expected.
items.quote: We have ramped up the volume. Customer is already -- I mean, we're already shipping commercially to this customer for the last 2-3 months and we should see higher volumes in the coming year.

items.statement: Setting up new assembled camshaft plant in Solapur; adding new machining lines for new contracts starting production in 12-24 months.
items.quote: setting up a new assembled camshaft plant at a new location in Solapur, and these new investments are made on the basis of a strong order book for new assembled camshaft businesses that has been secured along with an addition of past camshaft business

items.statement: Retrofit satellite conversion workshops may open this financial year based on critical volume; currently outsourcing to partners.
items.quote: Yes, there could be a requirement to open a few centers in this financial year.

items.statement: PCL India cast 6.98M camshafts in FY24 vs 5.8M in FY23; machined 2.98M vs 3.1M.
items.quote: We cast 6.98 million camshafts in FY '24 as compared to 5.8 million in FY '23. And out of this number, the company machined 2.98 million camshafts in FY '24 compared to 3.1 million last year.

items.statement: Retrofit conversion time reduced to 8-10 hours per vehicle in India via process standardization and supply chain simplification.
items.quote: We are able to convert 1 vehicle or the retrofitting, we can use 8-10 hours.

items.statement: PCL India diversifying into non-engine brake components; MEMCO into instrumentation; MFT into HVAC components.
items.quote: At PCL, we manufacture brake components, so it's still automotive, but it's not engine-dependent, let's put it like that. We have ramped up the volume. Customer is already -- I mean, we're already shipping commercially to this customer for the last 2-3 months and we should see higher volumes in the coming year. Similarly, at MEMCO, we have an instrumentation customer, which we are growing with com

items.statement: EMOSS developing new modular powertrain platform for off-highway niche applications (waste trucks, sweepers, cranes) to launch in ~2 years.
items.quote: We're developing a platform which will be extremely modular, extremely flexible. We will be working with some of the largest suppliers in the world that will allow us to be extremely competitive on cost and provide some very unique solutions in the European kind of off-highway vehicle application which should start kicking in the next 2 years or so I would say.

items.statement: PCL serves 50+ global customers across 14 plants in 3 countries; 15+ products beyond automotive.
items.quote: The company now has 14 plants in three countries, serving over 50 marquee global customers and manufacturing over 15 different products catering to various industries, which are not restricted to the automotive industry only.

items.statement: EMOSS India deployed 25+ trial vehicles with 15+ key customers in logistics, e-commerce, waste management.
items.quote: We have already successfully deployed over 25 vehicles with 15-plus key customers in logistics, e-commerce, waste management, etcetera.

items.statement: EMOSS competitors are niche powertrain integrators of similar size in Europe/US and OEMs doing own truck electrification.
items.quote: They're all in the similar size as what we operate in, whether they're in Europe or the US. And mainly in these 2 geographies in a similar size that we operate in at this point of time, I would say. But they are again, niche powertrain manufacturers or integrators like us. And then the obvious competitors are the OEMs that do electrification of trucks themselves.

items.statement: Government discussions ongoing for financial incentives on LCV retrofitment; policy not yet declared; business model based on non-subsidized economics.
items.quote: Yes, I think there is discussion within the government and they're involved in certain forums regarding the financial incentives for retrofitment. However, it's not yet clear and the new policy, which is yet to be implemented by the government has to be declared.

items.statement: Retrofit business working capital needs can be met via debt at PCL level; no equity raise planned currently.
items.quote: Yes, I think, at this point, it can be done at PCL level quite comfortably with raising -- I mean, working capital can be bought in terms of debt, right? It doesn't need to have equity capital at this point.

items.statement: European subsidiaries operate as standalone P&L entities; no cash support from PCL India parent.
items.quote: None of the subsidiaries are taking any financial benefits from PCL from the stand-alone company. The companies operate on their own as stand-alone companies and are completely P&L at that level, which they take care of. So there is no cash that is being shelled out from the parent company to the subsidiaries.

items.statement: EMOSS Europe faces headwinds: recession, public spending slowdown, EV subsidy pushback, lackluster growth forecast.
items.quote: EMOSS is facing significant headwinds in Europe. This is due to the overall recessionary trends, a slowdown in public spending, pushback on EV subsidies and a general lackluster growth forecast.

items.statement: Retrofit scale-up dependent on customer demand; supply chain for battery packs/BMS could be bottleneck.
items.quote: The bottleneck can more be the supply chain and availability of components, battery packs, BMS, things like that.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% top line increase for FY25.
items.quote: For the financial year 2024-'25, we would like to guide with a target of 20 to 25 percentage increase in the top line.

items.statement: Expects to sustain EBITDA at previously guided level.
items.quote: We expect to sustain the EBITDA at the level which we have previously guided.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin guidance of 17-19%.
items.quote: But going forward, the blended level, you can expect around the 17% - 19%.

items.statement: Ship repair EBITDA margin guidance of 22-23%.
items.quote: Ship repair, we would like to say 22 to 23 percentage.

items.statement: Additional depreciation from new capex to be INR125-150 crores.
items.quote: Both capacities put together is around INR2,800 crores. So the additional depreciation will be around INR125 crores to INR150 crores, not exact.

items.statement: New dry dock and ISRF to be fully commissioned by August 2024.
items.quote: We are planning to fully commission that project by August '24.

items.statement: Current unexecuted order book approximately INR22,000 crores.
items.quote: As we look towards the future, I'm pleased to inform you that our current order book position is healthy, with approximately INR22,000 crores of unexecuted orders, including the ship repair orders, which typically amounts to a little bit of higher level than earlier times at about INR1,200 crores at this given point of time.

items.statement: Ship repair order book at INR1,250 crores.
items.quote: The ship repair component of order book is about INR1,250 crores, which normally, if you have been following us earlier, we always used to guide about the order book of INR600 crores, INR700 crores.

items.statement: Expects 8-10 green tug orders over next year.
items.quote: We are expecting at least 8 to 10 vessels being ordered over the next year or so by the major ports through private entities and of course we expect to be very much actively parked in those process.

items.statement: Confident of growth for next 5-6 years.
items.quote: So we don't want to talk about peak revenue as a company. We want to continually grow both top line with a steady-state margin levels.

items.statement: PAT to be tempered due to higher depreciation from new projects.
items.quote: Our PAT level will have to be tempered due to the higher depreciation cost from the commissioning of the ISRF and the new dry dock project.

items.statement: Fixed asset turnover expected around 2 for new facilities.
items.quote: It will be around, I don't have the exact numbers right now. It will be around 2, once the operation in both new facilities get stabilised.

items.statement: IAC-2 execution timeline 8-10 years if similar to Vikrant.
items.quote: But whatever we have said on record earlier, if next carrier, when it comes, is largely based on the same or similar platform as what was Vikrant, then we have said we are somewhere around 8 to 10-ish years.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue growth target 10-12%
items.quote: So FY '25 on a consolidated basis, at a minimum, we should be seeing a 10% kind of growth in the revenue, 10% to 12%.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin target 18-20% including France losses
items.quote: And at an EBITDA level, as I mentioned earlier, close to about 18% to 20% is our target.

items.statement: FY25 operating cash flow target INR400-500 crores
items.quote: On a cash flow basis, we should be -- with most of the capex program being done, we do expect that we should generate free cash flow from financial year '25, and the cash profit should be close to about INR500 crores as far as our cash flow from operations is concerned, INR400 crores, INR500 crores.

items.statement: Net debt expected to reduce over next 2-3 years as free cash flow generates
items.quote: Yes. So as far as the net debt is concerned, we don't expect a significant increase from here on. On the contrary, as the free cash flow keeps on getting generated, the net debt over the next 2, 3 years should keep on reducing.

items.statement: PAT expected to turn positive from FY26
items.quote: I think as far as the profit after tax is concerned, that should come positive from FY '26.

items.statement: Development orders in excess of $140 million as of March 2024
items.quote: So since the development orders have been increasing and we have also mentioned in the presentation that currently we are sitting on development orders in excess of 140 million.

items.statement: Total customer advances INR634 crores as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: So the total is -- so the total comes to about INR634 crores.

items.statement: Major capex program completed; no significant capex expected going forward
items.quote: So now that all of those things have been completed and most of the assets have been operationalized, we don't expect any major capex to be incurred.

items.statement: France EBITDA loss to narrow from INR100 crores in FY24 to INR35-40 crores in FY25
items.quote: So FY'25, it would be close to about 4 million to 5 million. So that would be close to about INR35-odd crores to INR40-odd crores, which in the last financial -- or financial year '24 stood at about INR100 crores.

items.statement: France facility breakeven expected at $18-19 million revenue in FY26
items.quote: The breakeven point will be close to about 18 million to 19 million. And that is what we are targeting to achieve over the next year.

items.statement: CRAMS revenue growth guidance 14-15% for FY25-26 including France and India CRAMS
items.quote: So yes, 15% -- 14% to 15% kind of growth in the CRAMS revenue should very much be doable.

items.statement: India CRAMS revenue target INR350 crores in FY25, INR400 crores in FY26, INR450-500 crores thereafter
items.quote: I think as far as the India CRAMS is concerned; we should be closer to about INR350 crores for the full financial year of '25. And so, yes, I mean, we can easily move to INR500 crores, but that would take about 2 years' time. FY '26 is when we can expect we will be closer to INR400 crores as far as the India CRAMS is concerned, and then it could go to INR450 crores to INR500 crores in the year aft

items.statement: Swiss entity expected 8-10% revenue growth; UK entity 40-50% growth in FY25 on low base
items.quote: And also now U.K. also coming back on track. We do expect that the U.K. entity -- just in financial year '25, we do expect a 40% to 50% kind of growth because the base was lower in the last financial year. So overall, if you take a combination of all of this, and right now, this CRAMS as also includes the French entity. So France, from what it is doing right now with close to about $14 million of

items.statement: Bavla site USFDA audit completed; all sites approved except formulation plant
items.quote: USFDA was a general audit. The last inspect of it was in 2018, this was a general audit. So the auditor, as I mentioned before, came. It was not an announced -- it was an announced audit. It was regarding all the Italian sites and the auditor going to show all the products in running condition and we clearly mentioned that it is a general audit. So all the site is now approved.

items.statement: Regulatory clearances for Bavla enabling new orders from existing and new customers
items.quote: We're seeing an increase in the orders from the existing customers where the commercial supply are being supplied out or will be supplied out of Bavla. So that is number one. Number two, we have already seen new customers coming to the Bavla side.

items.statement: ADC project validation batches running; revenue ramp from FY26 to FY31 with peak around FY30-31
items.quote: We are already doing revenues out of that project because we are running, as I mentioned, the validation campaign related to the Phase III of the current application. And based on that, there will be further applications using that material. Ramp-up of the volumes from '26 to '31 and beyond with a maturity around '30, '31 with certainly a peak demand by the need of the sales.

items.statement: Non-current liabilities jump due to customer prepayments rising from INR138 crores to INR418 crores
items.quote: So that is largely on account of the prepayments that we have received from our customers. So the prepayment which was at about INR138 crores in -- as on 31st of March '23 that increased to about INR418 crores as on 31st of March '24.

items.statement: No major capex planned; free cash flow generation to reduce net debt over 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes, because right now, we don't have any major capex program. Most of the capex you see over the last 3 years, the debt has increased largely because of the capex that we have done in France, plus the co-investment projects in Switzerland, plus addition of certain lab and the capex that we have to do in Bavla and Naroda.

items.statement: Insurance and supplier claims filed for France facility delays; amount uncertain
items.quote: So that is exactly what we have pursued. So we are already filing a claim against the supplier as well as we are filing a claim to the insurance company. But right now, we don't have anything concrete.

items.statement: FX translation loss driven by 12-13% CHF depreciation vs INR; only partial USD hedging
items.quote: The major movement that we have seen in the Swiss franc to the INR where the depreciation is to the tune almost 12%-13%. Yes. From a sales perspective, we would hedge a portion of the U.S. dollar to Swiss franc, but not the entire portion because from a cash perspective, it really doesn't impact this conclusion.

items.statement: Q1-Q2 FY25 expected better than Q4 FY24; H2 FY25 much higher growth
items.quote: If we have to break it up quarter-wise, it is not ideal for our kind of business, but Q1, Q2 should be good quarters than what we have seen in Q4 FY '25 but we will see the second half of the year posting on much, much higher growth than what we've seen in the first half.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow at least 15% annually for next 3 years
items.quote: What I can say is for Lemon Tree certainly, we will see at least a 15% increase in revenue every year for the next 3 years.

items.statement: Rate growth in FY25 should not be less than FY24
items.quote: Well, I would say that rate growth this year should not be less than last year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 will be much better than Q1 FY24 for owned company
items.quote: As far as for the owned company goes, I think Q1 will certainly be much better than Q1 last year.

items.statement: Operational inventory target of 120+ hotels with over 11,000 rooms by end of FY25
items.quote: We expect our operational inventory to be about 120 + hotels with over 11,000 rooms by end of FY25.

items.statement: Pipeline addition of 2,000-3,000 rooms in FY25; openings of 1,200-2,000 rooms
items.quote: I do not think this is guidance when I say that we are very confident that we have 2,000-3,000 more rooms on our pipeline this year. And our endeavour is very simple, I can say it will be between from 1,200 - 2,000.

items.statement: Debt reduction to start in FY25; net debt zero within 4 years at latest
items.quote: So, debt reduction will start from this year. And there are 2 views, as I have said earlier. We are very confident that our debt will be 0 within the next 4 years, we will be net debt 0

items.statement: Renovation spend of Rs. 100 crore each in FY25 and FY26; ~65% opex, ~35% capex
items.quote: But bottom line is that this year, I have said this earlier, we will spend Rs. 100 crores on renovation and next year too. And at the end of it, by October CY25, the entire company will be new hotels.

items.statement: Keys portfolio target EBITDA of Rs. 60 crore per year minimum by October 2025
items.quote: Our target EBITDA for Keys would be Rs. 60 crore a year, minimum. And I think we will be getting there certainly by next October.

items.statement: Renovation impact on EBITDA margin was ~1.4% in Q4 FY24 (2% of revenue vs 0.6% prior year)
items.quote: It's about a 1.4% impact on overall EBITDA.

items.statement: Industry ARR hikes expected at 5-12% going forward; Lemon Tree brands to see staged increases through October 2025
items.quote: Otherwise, typically, the hikes you will see will be depending on the market and depending on the quality of hotel, it could be anywhere from 5% to 12%.

items.statement: Keys ARR target Rs. 4,500; Red Fox target north of Rs. 5,000; Lemon Tree/Premier target north of Rs. 7,000 by October 2025
items.quote: Once Keys is renovated, its average rate will move to Rs. 4,500, which was what roughly Red Fox's rate is. So, within the next 2 rate cycles, that is by October next year, you will see Keys gradually moving up to Rs. 4,500. Red Fox in my opinion, will move to north of Rs. 5,000 and Lemon Tree and Lemon Tree Premier and all, each of them will be north of Rs. 7,000.

items.statement: Structural demand upcycle imminent; India at GDP per capita inflection similar to China 2006/Indonesia 2007
items.quote: My forward view is, now I think the whole industry will wait for the upcycle, which is imminent in my opinion. At which point, you will see further significant hikes.

items.statement: No demand spillover from Q1 to Q2 FY25; June showing significant pickup after May softness
items.quote: I do not see any demand spilling over from Q1 to Q2. I think that there was a slowdown in demand in May partly due to weather, partly due to elections, and that is galloping back actually in June.

items.statement: IT hiring slowdown impacting Bangalore/Hyderabad occupancy; recovery expected from Q3 FY25
items.quote: We have been giving early indications that IT hiring should start in Q3 onwards. I guess we are quite dependent on that. That's a very large segment for us.

items.statement: Signed 12 management/franchise contracts adding 667 rooms in Q4 FY24; operationalized 4 hotels adding 176 rooms
items.quote: During Q4, we signed 12 new management and franchise contracts which will add 667 new rooms to our pipeline and operationalized 4 hotels added 176 rooms.

items.statement: Management fees up 48% YoY to Rs. 41.2 crore in Q4 FY24; full year Rs. 134.3 crore up 30%
items.quote: Total management fees for Lemon Tree in Q4 were up 48% Y-o-Y at Rs. 41.2 crore compared to Rs. 27.8 crore in Q4 FY23. The total management fee for the full year stood at Rs. 134.3 crore, which is up 30% over FY23.

items.statement: Operational inventory at 104 hotels, 9,863 rooms as of March 31, 2024; crossed 10,000 rooms as of call date
items.quote: As of 31st March 2024, the inventory for the group stands at 104 hotels operational, with 9,863 rooms, and our pipeline comprises an additional ~4,000 rooms. In fact, as of today, we are pleased to announce that our operational inventory has crossed 10,000 rooms.

items.statement: ~12-15% of Hyderabad inventory shut for renovation at any time; 100 rooms shut in Bangalore Whitefield
items.quote: About 12%-15% of Hyderabad will be shut at any given time.

items.statement: Debt increased Rs. 143.3 crore (8%) in FY24 due to Aurika Mumbai Skycity borrowing; peak debt reached
items.quote: The debt for the company increased by Rs. 143.3 crore or about 8% from Rs. 1,745.7 crore in FY23, which was owing to borrowing against Aurika, Mumbai Skycity.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels holds ~75% of total debt; potential Fleur listing could accelerate deleveraging
items.quote: We are very confident that our debt will be 0 within the next 4 years, we will be net debt 0 but should we list Fleur before that, which is something we're thinking about then obviously we will be debt free much earlier because Fleur has roughly 75% of the total debt of the company

items.statement: Q4 FY24 Gross ARR Rs. 6,605 (+13.4% YoY), Occupancy 72% (-163 bps YoY), RevPAR Rs. 4,754 (+10.9% YoY)
items.quote: Q4 FY24 recorded a Gross ARR of Rs. 6,605, which increased by 13.4% Y-o-Y and 4.3% Q-o-Q. Occupancy for the quarter stood at 72%, which decreased by 163 bps Y-o-Y and increased by 605 bps Q-o-Q. This translated into a RevPAR of Rs. 4,754, which increased by 10.9% Y-o-Y and 13.9% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai Q4 FY24: ~66% occupancy, ARR ~Rs. 9,000 (includes crew rooms); April strong, May flat, June pickup
items.quote: Fourth quarter, we did, I think, about 66%. Let me just pull out the figures for the Aurika, yes, we did about 66%. ARRs were about Rs. 9,000.

items.statement: Keys Pimpri Pune case study: >50% renovation drove ARR to Rs. 4,577 (+Rs. 800 vs Q4 FY23)
items.quote: Please refer to Slide 40 in the annexures which showcases a case study on how renovation of the Key s Pimpri, Pune, which is the first Keys hotel to be more than 50% renovated, translated into an ARR of Rs. 4,577, which was an increase of Rs. 800 over Q4 FY23.

items.statement: Supply additions largely in Tier-2/3/4 cities via asset-light model; 80% of capital deployed in top 6 metros where demand-supply favorable
items.quote: Now what supply additions are happening in India, second point, is that a lot of it is in Tier-2, Tier-3, Tier-4 cities, where, interestingly, we are only in 64 cities and we want to go to 150 cities in India where there are going to be airports, they are not already there, and where there is at least a population of 0.5 million.

items.statement: Cash profit increased 24% YoY to Rs. 293.8 crore in FY24
items.quote: The cash profit for the company increased 24% Y-o-Y from Rs. 237.1 crore in FY23 to Rs. 293.8 crore in FY24.

items.statement: Airline crew share at ~13% in Q4 (200-250 rooms); target to reduce to historic 8-10% as corporate/retail/MICE demand builds
items.quote: We had about 200 -250 crew rooms in the Q4. If I just take it over the base of, say 6,000 rooms, it is about 4%, which is most of the height that you see in the airline. But going forward, once we have built demand from the other segments, we will automatically reduce airline business and back to historic level of 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Total order book INR627.89 crores with INR345 crores unexecuted as of 31 March 2024
items.quote: As of 31st March 2024, the company's total order book stands at INR627.89 crores with INR345 crores of unexecuted orders, reflecting a strong pipeline and a promising future.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book INR350 crores to be executed over 2.5 to 3 years
items.quote: Out of that, INR350 crores is unexecuted. So the INR350 crores unexecuted order book is to be executed in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Revenue and profit growth estimated at 10% to 20% for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: Yes, there would be -- it would be in the range of 10% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline INR1,000 to INR1,200 crores for current year with 20-30% success rate expected to double order book
items.quote: So the order book that we are submitting right now is INR1,000 crores. So the bidding happening for this year is INR1,000 to INR1,200 crores. So even if we consider -- so while talking about terms of order book, in terms of order book, if I say INR1,200 crores is being bidded and even if we assume a success rate of 20% to 30%, we would definitely be able to double this order book.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 18% for FY24, up 540 bps YoY, considered sustainable with potential improvement from larger ticket projects
items.quote: The EBITDA was INR14.75 crores, up by 43% year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 18%, an improvement of 540 basis points.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to grow further due to larger domestic projects INR20-50 crores and international orders with better margins
items.quote: Yes. That is why, in fact, we are hoping for this to grow more because we are adding in a lot of clients this time. We are not just in international but in domestic market also we are now targeting a large ticket size projects wherein right now, we were getting orders of INR5 crores, INR10 crores, INR15 crores, we will now be getting orders of INR20 crores and above -- INR20 crores to INR50 crores

items.statement: Working capital cycle 45-60 days for NHAI, 90-120 days for MoRTH
items.quote: Yes. So NHAI/MoRTH it is in the range of -- at NHAI it is 45 to 60 days. And for MoRTH, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, it is 90 to 120 days.

items.statement: U.K. subsidiary Dhruv International Private Limited established; office establishment in U.K. expected this year
items.quote: So whenever -- right now, we have opened a subsidiary in U.K. by the name of Dhruv International Private Limited. Definitely, there will be an office establishment in U.K. this year.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue flat due to election-related order delays; normal revenue would have been INR90-95 crores
items.quote: INR90 crores to INR95 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 profitability impacted by mobilization expenses for new projects and ECL provision of approx INR1.8 crores
items.quote: It will be approx. INR1.8 crores.

items.statement: International expansion targeting African countries (Tanzania, Zambia, Uganda, Mozambique, Kenya), Gulf (Saudi Arabia, Dubai), Southeast Asia via U.K. subsidiary; shortlisted for ADB projects in Manipur, Mozambique, Ghana
items.quote: We also plan to venture into African countries, including Tanzania, Zambia, Uganda, Mozambique and Kenya, as well as Gulf countries like Saudi Arabia and Dubai. Dhruv has now positioned itself for substantial global expansion.

items.statement: Three international projects pending work orders: Tanzania ~INR50 crores, Mozambique, Ghana; Dhaka project shortlisted above INR20 crores, financial proposal pending
items.quote: Yes. So there are three projects that we are due to receive our work order. One is the Tanzania, it is around INR50 crores assignment. There is one project in Mozambique and one project in Ghana.

items.statement: Employees added continuously via in-house recruitment; consent taken during bidding; key professionals pre-identified for international projects
items.quote: So when it comes to recruitment, first, we have to take their consent while bidding. So during submission of bids itself, we have to take the consent and as and when the project is awarded, the employees are taken on the roles.

items.statement: FY24 total income INR82.41 crores, up 0.13% YoY; EBITDA INR14.75 crores, up 43% YoY; PAT INR5.89 crores, up 22.77% YoY
items.quote: For the full fiscal year 2024, the company achieved a total income of INR82.41 crores, a slight year-on-year growth of 0.13%. The EBITDA was INR14.75 crores, up by 43% year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 18%, an improvement of 540 basis points. The PAT reached INR5.89 crores, a year-on-year growth of 22.77% with a PAT margin of 7.14%, an increase of 132 basis points.

items.statement: Election cycles cause order delays every 5 years; international diversification aims to mitigate this dependency
items.quote: This -- as I said that this mainly happened due to the elections that were due at the central government level. And this is a trend that is there every 5 years. Hence, now with international orders coming up, we will be able to mitigate this sector. There is no dependency on the central government elections.

items.statement: Expects 40-50% year-on-year growth for next couple of years.
items.quote: So growth, we are looking to continue the current growth trend of 40% to 50% year-on-year for the next couple of years. I mean, 40% on a conservative level, we are hoping to grow for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin of 8.5-9.5% for current financial year.
items.quote: And, as far as EBITDA is concerned, we are expecting EBITDA to be in the range of 8.5% to 9%, 9.5% for the current financial year.

items.statement: Plans to increase ODU capacity by 20% in coming year due to demand.
items.quote: We are also looking at increasing our capacity by about 20% in ODU in the coming year, because of increased demand.

items.statement: Expects 50-70% capacity utilisation in commercial refrigeration next year.
items.quote: And we hope that by next year, we will reach a capacity utilisation of 50% to 70% of the capacity that we're creating this year.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin of 2-3% depending on depreciation method.
items.quote: So PAT between 2% and 3%, we are contemplating if depreciation if you want to go into a straight line depreciation calculation, then PAT will go towards 3%, maybe slightly higher. But if we continue WDV, then about 2%.

items.statement: Plans to start Chennai unit for AC components in current financial year.
items.quote: This year, we also plan to start a unit in Chennai for making components for air conditioners, because some of our customers are wanting us to make certain parts locally for them in Chennai. So our unit in Chennai is also planned in the current financial year.

items.statement: May enter washing machine segment towards end of year or next year.
items.period: end of this year or next year
items.quote: We are also exploring washing machine as a segment. So we might enter washing machine also either towards the end of this year or maybe next year, but it is not confirmed as of yet.

items.statement: Expects June quarter to be better than last year.
items.quote: So, April and May normally is good every year. And this year, June is also looking to be really good, which is not normally the case because June onwards, the sales start declining. But this year, we are expecting a good June. So overall, the June quarter is expected to go better than last year.

items.statement: Expects ODU to pressure EBITDA, but other verticals to balance.
items.quote: So EBITDA with ODU is lower than IDU, because the value addition in the overall product is lower. So ODU is expected to put pressure on EBITDA, but I think the other verticals like commercial ref we'll probably balance it out slightly.

items.statement: Pricing with customers reset quarterly based on LME average.
items.quote: So we have a quarterly pricing structure with our customers. So, the pricing gets quarterly reset based on the average of last three months. So effectively, it nullifies over a period of two quarters.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to be lower or similar this year despite growth.
items.quote: So with the recent fundraise that we did, we believe this year, the interest cost will be slightly lower than last year even after the growth coming in. So it will be similar or a lower number, irrespective of the growth.

items.statement: Plans to use QIP proceeds for working capital and capex.
items.quote: So, working capital and CapEx primarily.

items.statement: Expects 2-3% of sales from exports this year.
items.quote: And I think this year our export number is, we are expecting at least 2%, 3% of our sales to come from export. And if that happens, we'll continue to build on it in the coming years.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15-20% YoY for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Our vision endeavor will be continuing this trajectory of growth 15% to 20% Y-on-Y that should be our endeavor and the guidance for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of around 3%+ in 1-2 years
items.quote: Range we should be hovering around 3 plus percent in year or two to come.

items.statement: Rs 1000 crore revenue target remains on horizon, halfway there currently
items.quote: The Rs. 1000 crore mark still stays on the horizon. And if you say how close , we are halfway there.

items.statement: FY26 aspirational target for Rs 1000 crore revenue
items.quote: FY26 would be my dream target , but our endeavor is there.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 4.36%, up 43 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 4.36%, an improvement of 43 bps compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Full year FY24 net profit margin 2.53%
items.quote: Net profit for the margin stood at 2.53%.

items.statement: Segment margins: Networking 5-7%, UC 7-9%, Security double-digit
items.quote: The margins in the networking patch, what we call it, is a round hovering around 5 % to 7%. In the UC patch, it is approximately 7% to 8% or 9% and in the security patch, it is double digit.

items.statement: Margins improving via scale, efficiency, services attachment, and product mix optimization
items.quote: as the scale increases and we continue to bring efficiency into our operations and thirdly, the product mix of adding services to the products which we are getting and more and more solutions offering as we grow, we see that the margins improv ing to a better level than this

items.statement: Strong demand for Samsung, NETSCOUT, Netgear, D-Link, Arbor products and software/services in FY24
items.quote: due to strong demand in our products like Samsung, NETSCOUT, Netgear, D-Link, Arbor and other software and services.

items.statement: Interactive panel revenue expected Rs 30-50 crore in FY25 vs Rs 8-12 crore in FY24
items.quote: we see that contributing to a decent maybe Rs. 30 to Rs. 50 crores this year interactive panel into our kitty.

items.statement: Enterprise security fastest growing segment, now ~25% of revenue
items.quote: enterprise security business, which is the latest addition and as the time goes, it has a more and more demand has risen to approximately 25% of our kitty.

items.statement: Order book not relevant; quoted funnel ~Rs 40-50 crore converting in month/quarter
items.quote: It is approx imately around Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50 crores which we are already quoted, and the order should be coming through maybe in this month or the quarter next, so order book is not very relevant to our business.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Networking 45-50%, UC 25-30%, Enterprise Security ~25%
items.quote: networking. So networkin g still remains a huge chunk of our business, which is approximately 45%-50% of our business, the unified communication patch also contributes around 25 %-30% of our business and the enterprise security business

items.statement: Hardware 80%, Software/Services 20% of FY24 revenue
items.quote: FY24, hardware is 80%, 20% comes from the software services.

items.statement: Top 15 customers contribute 40-50% of revenue; key accounts include Tata Communications, Hitachi, NSE/BSE via SI partners
items.quote: our top 15 of them will be contributing around 40%-50% of our business.

items.statement: Samsung contributes 15-20% of UC revenue; Netgear 45-50% of Networking; NETSCOUT/Arbor 60% of Security
items.quote: Samsung would be around 15% to 20% contributing out of that. So that answers. In the networking patch , Netgear which we are exclusive distributors for Northeast and West of India contributes around 50% of our patch , 45%-50% in that patch. The third enterprise security, NETSCOUT and Arbor are visibility solutions and DDoS security solutions is 60% of that patch which we offer.

items.statement: No direct listed peer with same 3-domain mix; differentiated by solution/services vs pure distribution
items.quote: We are working into three domains, so there is no apple-to-apple company which is available exactly in these domains.

items.statement: Expanded operations to South India this year; overseas expansion under study
items.quote: This year, we have just moved to the southern India, which we are not present. So we just set up our operations in Southern India, the team is in place.

items.statement: Open to raising funds via bank debt or preferential issue as business demands to fuel growth
items.quote: if need be, as the business demands, we are open to raising more funds from bank or maybe via preference or whatever the board feels right, we may raise.

items.statement: Promoters not diluting stake; warrants conversion will restore promoter holding
items.quote: promoters are not in the mode of diluting the stake. We have done a preferential thing, but parallelly, there has been warrants which are convertible, which has been issued which will be up on conversion of warrants will be again back to what we were

items.statement: ~70 employees across sales, engineering, technical support, finance, admin; no in-house software development
items.quote: We are approximately 70 plus team and it is mixture of everything. It is not only sales, sales support guys, the engineer, the technician and obviously the finance and the admin team.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue Rs 154.59 crore, up 60.74% YoY
items.quote: have reported Rs. 154.59 crores of revenue during Q4 of FY 24, a 60.74% Y-on-Y rise

items.statement: FY24 revenue Rs 459.63 crore, up 27.81% YoY
items.quote: we have reported Rs. 459.63 crores revenue in FY24, a 27.81% year -on-year rise

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA Rs 6.74 crore, up 78.16% YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the fourth quarter stands at Rs. 6.74 crores, increasing 78.16% Y-on-Y

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA Rs 20.04 crore, up 57.53% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the full year is Rs. 20.04 crores, an increase of 57.53% Y-on-Y

items.statement: FY24 net profit Rs 11.61 crore vs Rs 7.08 crore in FY23
items.quote: Our net profits during the full year is Rs. 11.61 crore against profit of Rs. 7.08 crore in FY23.

items.statement: Security segment quarterly spike due to Diwali deferrals; may not repeat every quarter
items.quote: some orders which were supposed to be executed in OND because of that Diwali patch, they got pushed into the JFM quarter and because of that JFM quarter, you see a big spike. This kind of numbers would may not be the same

items.statement: Management expects to maintain historic revenue growth of 15% to 20%.
items.quote: Will grow accordingly on our regular previous year ’s growth and we don’t do bi dding very aggressively. We maintain it so that we can execute projects on time and give quality work, so we hope that we can maintain our historic increase of 15% to 20

items.statement: EBITDA margins will be sustained at around 13% to 14%.
items.quote: Gradually we have grown and we will sustain our margins at around 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Current order book stands at around Rs. 4,717 crores to be executed over 24 to 36 months.
items.quote: The current order book as on 31st March 2024 stands at around Rs. 4,717 crores across all the business segments to be executed over the next 24 months to 36 months.

items.statement: Aim to maintain order book to turnover ratio around 3 times.
items.quote: We aim to maintain order books to turnover ratio around 3 times.

items.statement: No immediate need for capex as adequate equipment is available.
items.quote: No, as of now we have proper equipment, so we hope that with this equipment itself new projects can be done and if any specific equipment is required then we can procure that.

items.statement: No plans for equity fund raising; growth will be managed through internal accruals and bank borrowings.
items.quote: As of now, company has no such plan for fund raising let us see with the existing growth which is going on, but right now management has no such plans.

items.statement: Government focus on infrastructure is good and bidding is continuous.
items.quote: And from the last few years, the governments focus has also been good on infrastructure segment.

items.statement: Diversifying across states; Rajasthan portion of order book reduced from 68% to 37%.
items.quote: Yes, sir. We are diversifying in other states also if we compare our last order book, in that our Rajasthan portion in that it came from 68% to 37% now and in other states its revenue has gone to higher side.

items.statement: Debtor days increased due to election period but will normalize going forward.
items.quote: Debtor days are according to the GST norms, but specifically last 6 months was election period, so due to that payments were slowed down, but going forward debtor days will be normalized.

items.statement: Debt equity ratio will be maintained under one.
items.quote: We will not aggressively take debt, but as you know that this is a working capital intensive business, so we are not going forward for aggressive debt funding and will maintain Debt equity ratio under one only.

items.statement: Historic bidding success ratio is around 17%.
items.quote: Last historic bidding success ratio is around 17%.

items.statement: Mobilization advances on balance sheet were around Rs. 61 crores.
items.quote: Generally we take mobilization advances where it is interest free. In last March 31 st balance sheet it is around Rs. 61 crores

items.statement: Finance cost will be in line with revenue growth.
items.quote: Will be in the same pattern because it is a working capital intensive business, has internal accruals and bank borrowings, so it has to be maintained, but is not going to aggressively increase.

items.statement: March quarter is seasonally strong due to government fund utilization.
items.quote: Already this is the pattern of tender March quarter which is a fourth quarter is always good.

items.statement: No significant impact from elections or summer on execution.
items.quote: During election period, our execution was going the same as it was befor e there was no major impact on it and if we talk about the summer season then we cover up by doing morning and night duty

items.statement: Focus on railways and roads for expansion.
items.quote: Our core competency is in water supply projects, but at the same time we are seeing expansion and opportunities in railways and roads also. We are bidding new tenders also.

items.statement: Management looks forward to maintaining current levels and increasing them, optimistic about continuing the growth trend.
items.quote: See, we are looking forward to maintain our current levels and also increase them. We are working forward towards it by introducing new line of inventories, new SKUs and catering to the customers.

items.statement: Planning showroom expansions in different demographic areas in Rajasthan and outside Rajasthan, deciding on small or high scale models.
items.quote: We are planning for a few expansions, a few showrooms in different demographic areas like in Rajasthan and also outside the Rajasthan. So we are planning for the different kind of models.

items.statement: No huge investments made yet in technology and new machinery, but planning to invest in the near future.
items.quote: As of now we have not made huge investments in the technology and the new machineries, but we are planning to do that and for the time being, we are focusing on improving our inventories to cater customers with various products which fulfils their demand, but we will be investing in the latest technologies as well.

items.quote: We have more than 3.5 lakh SAQs right now in our portfolio.

items.quote: We refresh our design every 3 months. We addition near about 20%-30% in our portfolio.

items.quote: Currently, our working capital cycle is 1.
