items.quote: And plus, our Vaishali Nagar showroom consists of 6,800 square feet. And its sales consists of around INR40 plus crores last year.

items.statement: Revenue boosted by increasing demand for marriage season and festivals like Diwali and Akshaya Tritiya.
items.quote: See the revenue part has been given a boost by the increasing demand for the marriage season and the festivals like Diwali and Akshaya Tritiya.

items.statement: Post IPO allotment and subscription, debt was reduced significantly, resulting in increased profits.
items.quote: Overall, also we have since post allotment of shares and successful subscription of IPO, we have reduced our debt significantly which has resulted in increased profits.

items.statement: Long-term goal is pan-India expansion, starting from Rajasthan or nearby, increasing showrooms year by year.
items.quote: Our long-term goals are basically expansion, expansion pan India. Just we start from Rajasthan or nearby where our main customer focus is portfolio is there. Then gradually we increase our showroom year by year that is our goal.

items.statement: Company is making different collections to promote via social media, websites and outdoor media.
items.quote: Yes we are making some different kind of collections and we are going to promote them via social media and websites and outdoor media also.

items.statement: Company has proper inventory management system to identify fast and weak selling products.
items.quote: Yes. We have proper inventory system. We call it IMS. So, from that inventory system, we just find out what product is selling fast and what product is selling weak.

items.statement: Company focuses mostly on trading, not manufacturing, and works with vendors to improve quality.
items.quote: Our company focuses mostly on the trading not on the manufacturing, but somehow we are trying to make our vendors to produce a good quality of product better than before and introducing new technologies and designs to make a new & good quality of products.

items.statement: Company has proper CRM system where every lead and review is followed up by CRM team.
items.quote: See, Priya, we have proper CRM System. So, every lead and every reviews are followed by our CRM team.

items.statement: Company sees incremental growth from social media marketing on Instagram and Facebook, and website engagement increasing.
items.quote: So, basically, we drive growth from social media. Like I said before, we do marketing on Instagram and Facebook. And we are seeing incremental growth from both the social media.

items.statement: Expects 5% to 7% annual inflationary growth for next 2 years.
items.quote: So for the next 2 years, there are a couple of things. Number one, whatever inflationary growth we keep getting, which is in the range of 5% to 7% per year that we are expecting.

items.statement: Chemical division to achieve 95% utilization from current 75%.
items.quote: We can achieve easily 95% from current level of 75%.

items.quote: And assuming 3 throughput as a reasonable, we can easily achieve around INR200 crores of revenue.

items.statement: India outbound travel spending surged 24% to $17 billion in FY24 with 8-11% projected air passenger growth
items.quote: Overseas travel spending has surged to US $17 billion in this last financial year, marking a notable 24% increase over the previous year. Projections indicate an anticipated growth in international air passenger traffic by 8% to 11%.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers outside India grew 20% driving 31% international GTV growth; enterprise buyers grew 8% driving 19% overall GTV growth
items.quote: Our monthly transacting buyers outside of India grew by around 20%, which led to a growth of 31% in GTV in our international business. At an enterprise level, our monthly transacting buyer base grew by 8%, which led to an overall increase in GTV by 19%.

items.statement: Air take rate steady state at 2.5%; air gross profit expected between 1.2-1.5%
items.quote: So, considering the current situation, we believe that 2.5% should be a steady state growth or the take rate number for air business and similarly, for the gross profit numbers, we expect to maintain it between 1.5% to 1.2%.

items.statement: Significant investment planned in technology and data teams; costs will increase going forward
items.quote: No. I think there is no cost optimization possible, Pratyush, and tech resources remain expensive. So, our significant investment will continue to go into building out the technology and data teams. From the perspective of how we should look at this going forward, we do intend to increase the number of people in the tech team. So, you will see some increase in costs on those heads going forward.

items.statement: 26,500 monthly transacting buyers total with 18,500 in India; international buyers grew 20% vs 8% enterprise growth due to India base effect
items.quote: In fact, in 2024, out of roughly 26,500 buyers, 18,500 are sitting in India. So, while that number has grown, that number is growing at a slow percentage because of the base effect. So, hence the enterprise growth number looks lesser.

items.statement: 85-90% of international business naturally hedged in USD/GBP/EUR; India hotel payments hedged via forwards; airline payments in INR
items.quote: In our international business, a majority of our business is naturally hedged because we are selling in so many countries and buying from so many countries from different suppliers. So let us say, for example, selling in USD and also collecting in USD and making payment to suppliers in USD. So, around 85%-90% of my business in currencies like USD, GBP and Europe in naturally hedged.

items.statement: Working capital remains negative; trade receivables and payables increased due to Jumbonline consolidation and hotel mix with longer booking window
items.quote: Notably, our working capital continues to remain negative. As of March end 2024, there has been a substantial increase in trade receivables and trade payables amount as compared to the past year. This has been primarily due to consolidation of financial numbers of our new acquisition Jumbonline as well as due to the increase in the overall mix of hotel business.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 1,550 Cr total with INR 400 Cr primary infusion for future growth goals
items.quote: The total size of the IPO was INR 1,550 Crore, with INR 400 Crore being the primary infusion of capital. This capital injection will enable us to fulfill our funding requirements to achieve our future goals.

items.statement: Completed 4 acquisitions in 5 years including Jumbonline for Southern European beach hotels; acquisition thesis focuses on adding buyer base or supply base globally
items.quote: Over the last 5 years, we have completed 4 acquisitions, enhancing our global reach and market position. Most recently, we had acquired Jumbonline, which is an aggregator of Southern European Beach Hotel supply. We will continue to look for more opportunities for inorganic growth.

items.statement: Jumbonline contributed INR 36 Cr revenue and INR 3.5 Cr PAT in FY24; material impact expected in coming year
items.quote: So, Swapnil, there was only INR 36 Crore of revenue that was contributed by Jumbo in the last FY numbers. So, we will see some material impact in the Jumbonline in the coming year, but it was not very material for last year. In terms of PAT, the contribution was about INR 3.5 Crore from the Jumbonline business.

items.quote: So, the SG&A cost is at around 2.5%. items.statement: Travel volatility from macroeconomic and political events is fundamental risk; global diversification provides some hedge

So the chances of something going wrong in some part of the world is always there, though it also adds a hedge for us because we are not overly concentrated in a certain market

items.statement: Existing order book sufficient to absorb full Dahej output; new large multinational clients at advanced approval stages
items.quote: even currently we have an order book which a llows us, if we can make as per the requirement already that we have the existing order book, we can achieve full, we can ship out all the production that we will be able to get even after the Dahej facility is maxed out

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin improved 500 bps to 18.8%; manufacturing EBITDA now dominates as trading exits
items.quote: The margins stood at 18.8% in FY24 as compared to 13.8% in FY23, thus improving by 500 basis points.

items.statement: Blended realization per kg expected to rise above $10/kg over 3-5 years; average selling price per kg to improve >10%
items.quote: The realizations per kilo would jump above $10 per kilo comfortably over three to five years period.

items.statement: New high-value products developed over 4-5 years to contribute ~15% of volume and >30% of revenue
items.quote: Around, we see it at around 15%, it can go higher also. But I would safely say around 15% of our total volume.

items.statement: Domestic manufacturing revenue tripled to INR22.59 crores in FY24; remarkable growth expected in next 12 months
items.quote: for the f inancial year '22-'23 where our domestic revenue from manufacturing stood at INR8.18 crores, I'm happy to inform you that for the year 2023 -'24, that revenue has almost tripled to INR22.59 crores

items.statement: Roha expansion pending environmental clearance; no other challenges envisaged
items.quote: Environmental approval is pending. Yes.

items.statement: Dahej greenfield expansion of INR70 crores completed and funded via internal accruals; capacity doubled to 675 tons/month
items.quote: The to tal investment for this was INR70 crores, which was all funded through internal accruals

items.statement: Trading business estimated at zero for FY25; all volumes now manufacturing-only
items.quote: See, we are estimating the trading business to be zero only as far as FY'24, FY'25 is concerned.

items.statement: R&D expense at 4-5% of sales; proprietary processes developed in-house
items.quote: Our R&D expense would come to around 4% -5% of our sales.

items.statement: PAT declined due to steel price volatility; steel prices fell from Rs 80/kg in March 2023 to Rs 57/kg in March 2024, reducing revenue despite higher tonnage.
items.quote: Due to volatility in prices of Steel. In March, 2023 prices of steel were around Rs.80/- whereas in March, 2024 prices of steel showed a decline to Rs. 57/-, due to such downward trend for the whole financial year the revenue of the company has declined inspite of increase in production capacity/tonnage.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue and tonnage: Q1 Rs 28 Cr/787t, Q2 Rs 26 Cr/501t, Q3 Rs 25 Cr/980t, Q4 Rs 24 Cr/1100t.
items.quote: In Q1: Revenue was 28 Crs., tonnage was 787 ton. In Q2: Revenue was 26 Crs., tonnage was 501 ton. In Q3: Revenue was 25 Crs., tonnage was 980 ton. In Q4: Revenue was 24 Crs., tonnage was 1100 ton.

items.statement: Management targets operating profit margin to increase by 1% in the current fiscal year.
items.quote: The management will try that the Operating Profit Margin increases from 1% this year.

items.statement: PEB order book covers next 2.5-3 months; plant booked for execution till October 2024.
items.quote: For Pre-Engineering Buildings we have order book for next 2.5-3 months and for execution the plant is booked till October,2024.

items.statement: Unit II current capacity 800 tonnes/month; target 2000 tonnes/month in 3-4 years after installing more machines and hiring staff.
items.quote: In Unit I, the production capacity of 300 tonnes for Roofing Sheets and approx 100 tonnes of Pre-Engineering Buildings, whereas, in Unit II, the production capacity as on date is 800 tonnes per month and in future the same can be increased to 2000 tonnes.

items.statement: Future capex will be funded from internal accruals, not from shareholders.
items.quote: There may be capital expenditure in coming future, but the same will be from our own accurals and not from the side of shareholders.

items.statement: After full phase completion and machine installation, turnover can reach Rs 200-250 Cr in future.
items.quote: Therefore, in Unit II after completion of all the phases and instalment of more machines, the turnover can reach to Rs. 200-250 Crs. in future.

items.statement: Revenue is directly proportional to steel prices.
items.quote: Yes, steel prices are directly proportional to the revenue.

items.statement: Built accommodation for ~80 labourers, started canteen services, and forming MOUs with ITIs and skill centres for fitters, welders, grinders.
items.quote: Sir, to solve this issue we have taken following measures: 1. The accommodation facilities for approx. 80 labours has been arranged by constructing 16-18 houses. 2. Canteen Services has been started, so that labours do not starve for food. 3. We have approached many Industrial Training Institutes and Skill Development Centres to form strong team of fitter, welder, grinder men as per our requiremen

items.statement: Total debt repaid in FY24 was around Rs 2.13 Cr.
items.quote: Total debt repaid in FY 23-24 was around Rs.2,12,66,000/-

items.statement: FY24 PAT margin 3.36%, operating profit margin before tax 6.29%, operating profit Rs 6.66 Cr.
items.quote: PAT margin in FY 23-24 3.36% Operating Profit Margin before Tax in FY 23- 24 6.29% Operating profit in value was Rs. 6,65,86,000/-

items.statement: Unit I (36,000 sq ft) rented out at ~Rs 3.15 lakh/month; Unit II expanded to 300,000 sq ft in phases.
items.quote: Unit I is non -operative and it will be given on monthly -rent for Rs. 3.15 Lakhs approx..

items.statement: Suven entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling 51% stake in Sapala Organics, a Hyderabad-based CDMO specializing in oligonucleotide drugs and nucleic acid building blocks.
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that Suven has entered into a Definitive Agreement for the Acquisition of a Controlling Stake in Sapala Organics.

items.statement: Initial consideration is Rs 2,295 million for 51% stake on a fully diluted basis; 100% acquisition expected at 13x-15x EBITDA multiple over the next three years, financed through cash reserves.
items.quote: Subject to the customary adjustments for net cash and working capital, the initial consideration is Rs. 2,295 million for an acquisition of 51% stake on a fully diluted basis. We expect the 100% acquisition to be valued at 13x to 15x times EBITDA multiple, contingent on the financial performance, primarily EBITDA, over the next three years.

items.statement: Transaction expected to be EPS-accretive from the first year of acquisition and will not affect the current merger scheme with Cohance.
items.quote: The transaction is expected to be EPS-accretive from the first year of acquisition and we do not expect this acquisition to affect the current merger scheme with Cohance.

items.statement: Sapala's business expected to match or exceed the market growth rate of 20%+ CAGR in the mid-to-long term due to a smaller base.
items.quote: In a mid-term-to-long-term. It will match or exceed the current market growth. That's the internal view that we have, because the base is lower and smaller.

items.statement: Sapala FY24 revenues over Rs 670 million with adjusted EBITDA margins at 45%+; adjusted revenue growing at 18% CAGR over the last three years.
items.quote: In FY'24 Sapala's revenues were over Rs. 670 million and the adjusted EBITDA margins being at 45%-plus. As shared in the investor deck, the adjusted revenue has been growing at a CAGR of 18% for the last three years.

items.statement: Plans to create a GMP manufacturing facility at one of Suven's expanded platform sites to support future growth as molecules progress from preclinical to commercial stages.
items.quote: And one of the important elements as a part of the deal is, we end up supporting the growth of the organization by creating a GMP manufacturing facility. Hence, we don't have any capacity constraint right now, and as it is a predominantly R&D, we have enough capacities; however, in view of the future growth, we have plans to create a GMP manufacturing site in one of our expanded platform sites.

items.statement: Current operations are predominantly R&D-led with kilolitre-scale capacity for basic amidites; no capacity constraints currently, but GMP facilities planned for future clinical and commercial scale-up.
items.quote: This is predominantly R&D-led activity and today, the basic amidites or some of the compounds that we do manufacturing are in kilolitres capacity. Otherwise, from a capacity standpoint, it is predominantly on R&D side of it; however, when the molecule grows into the clinical phase from preclinical into commercial, what we need is GMP facilities.

items.statement: Sapala has a diversified innovator customer base across US (40%), Europe (30%), and Japan (20%), including big biopharma and oligo-focused CDMO players; top five customers contribute less than 50% of revenue.
items.quote: Today, Sapala has innovator customer base across US, Europe and Japan. Broad geography, average sale split, the last few years between US, Europe and Japan is around 40, 30 and 20, which also means is a good mix of big biofirms, which includes oligo-focused CDMO players and that's how the current business mix is around the companies.

items.statement: Customer addition is happening regularly, along with addition of molecules for existing customers and product progress; Suven's existing relationships with top innovator companies expected to accelerate this.
items.quote: Yes. Addition of the customers is happening, on top of it addition of molecules for the same line of customers is also happening. Finally, product progress is actually seen and Sapala is along with the product progress as well.

items.statement: Sapala specializes in locked and bridged nucleic acids, tricyclo DNA, and GalNAC compounds, positioning it as one of few global players capable of delivering such specialized oligonucleotide solutions.
items.quote: Sapala capabilities in locked and bridged nucleic acid, Tricyclo DNA, GalNAC positions it as one of the few players globally capable of delivering such specialized solution, which the market is looking for.

items.statement: Competitive landscape is unique with no directly comparable peers; some companies are closely related but not exactly comparable due to Sapala's unique combination of competencies under one roof.
items.quote: As you understand, there is a very unique combination of having bridged nucleotides and galvanic compounds and tricyclic compounds. So, it's very hard to decide; however, there are some companies who are closely related, but not exactly comparable.

items.statement: Synergies from combining Sapala's R&D depth with Suven's customer access and manufacturing capabilities expected to materialize within two to four years, depending on clinical success of pipeline.
items.quote: But, as you understand, our success is depending on the clinical success of a pipeline, which means anywhere visible case studies can be built with synergies at least within two to four years' timeframe is what we see so which comes back to the same time period or which can be a little early also.

items.statement: Dr. P. Yella Reddy, Sapala's promoter and CEO with 20+ years experience in Japan, will continue as CEO for the next few years and serve as strategic advisor for Japan market entry across Suven and Cohance platforms.
items.quote: We plan to operate this business collaboratively with the current promoter, working as the CEO of Sapala Organics for the next few years as well as the strategic advisor for Japan region before we fully acquire 100% of Sapala.

items.statement: Acquisition structured with initial 51% stake purchase, balance 49% to be acquired over three to four years at 13x-15x EBITDA multiple based on future financial performance, ensuring alignment of interests.
items.quote: We're expecting to acquire 100% in a period of three to four years which again would be valued at 13 to 15 EBITDA multiple in the next three to four years.

items.statement: Gross written premium crossed INR 9,000 crores in FY24 with market share of 3.1% on GWP basis
items.quote: we have completed and crossed INR 9,000 crores of premium income in the last whole year. Overall market share on GWP basis is about 3.1.

items.statement: Net earned premium doubled from FY22 to FY24 reaching INR 7,000 crores
items.quote: if you look at the next line, which is the premium retention ratio, the premium retention ratio has also been increasing each year. And in FY '24, this number was about 85.8%.

items.statement: Combined ratio for FY24 was 108.7%, about 1% higher than previous year due to large property and NAT CAT losses
items.quote: Our combined ratio in FY '24 was 108.7, which is about 1% higher than the previous year. Most of it is related to some large losses in property, which we had and some NAT CAT losses.

items.statement: Profit after tax for FY24 was INR 182 crores, Q4 FY24 profit was INR 53 crores (double Q4 FY23)
items.quote: Our profit for the year is about INR 182 crores. And for the quarter, it's INR53 crores, which is double to what we had in quarter 4 of '23.

items.statement: Premium retention ratio increased to 85.8% in FY24, among highest in industry
items.quote: And in FY '24, this number was about 85.8%, which I believe would be amongst the highest in the industry.

items.statement: Own damage mix increased from 16% to 22%, TP reduced from 46% to 39%, health travel increased from 13% to 19% in FY24
items.quote: you can actually see our own damage mix has increased from 16% to 22% in FY '24. TP has actually reduced from 46% to 39%. Health travel NP has increased from 13% to 19%.

items.statement: Outgrew industry in motor OD (42% vs 17%), fire (19% vs 7%), health; de-grew motor TP by 11% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: industry has grown in motor own damage by about 17% against our 42%. TP is about 10%, which is similar to ours. Fire, industry grew by 7%, we grew by 19%. And health, etcetera, also, we grew more than the industry.

items.statement: Took corrective action in motor TP due to third-party inflation and minimum wage increases; de-grew TP by 11% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: we as a company always plan continuously look at businesses where we feel it doesn't make sense economically for us to do business. And we would actually then get out of those segments if we don't find the margins to be attractive.

items.statement: Own damage loss ratio improved year by year: 74%, 69%, 66%; TP loss ratio viewed over 3-4 year period
items.quote: if you look at our own damage loss ratios has been coming down year by year, 74, 69, 66. TP loss ratio has been coming down. But in TP loss ratio, we always look at loss ratio over a period of three years or four years

items.statement: Health loss ratio increased due to growth in employer-employee health business and lower data quality initially
items.quote: The loss ratio still was at about 72% lower than, I would say, the industry health loss ratio. And this has increased last year due to the growth in the employer -employee health insurance business.

items.statement: Property and engineering NAT CAT losses of INR 70 crores impacted combined ratio by only 1% due to high net earned premium base
items.quote: We actually had an impact of about INR70 crores, which basically meant that in case of property and engineering, this had a very, very significant impact. But what is interesting is that because we have a very high net earn ed premium of almost INR7,000 crores, the impact on the overall loss ratio for the year is only 1%.

items.statement: API integrations doubled in two years; 51% of policies now issued through APIs
items.quote: you can also see in two years, we have almost doubled the number of APIs we have. And now 51% of our policies are issued through the APIs.

items.statement: Assets under management grew organically by INR 2,700-2,800 crores in FY24; raised INR 350 crores sub-debt for solvency
items.quote: if you look at from FY23 to FY24, we have roughly increased organically the AUM by about INR2,700, INR2,800 crores. And this year we had raised INR 350 crores of sub-debt to support the solvency.

items.statement: Investment income crossed INR 1,000 crores, more than doubled from FY22; investment yield improved to 7.3% (up ~100 bps)
items.quote: The investment income is decent. We crossed INR1,000 crores in investment income. So if you actually see FY22 to FY24, our investment income has actually more than doubled. And you can also see that the investment yield is also now about 7.3%, which is almost 100 basis points better than the previous year.

items.statement: Equity allocation kept low at 1.6% due to solvency sensitivity; will increase equity allocation post IPO capital infusion
items.quote: Our equity allocation has continued to be lower. It's only 1.6%. And when we look at our solvency of 161%, since solvency ratio was a bit lower, any unrealized losses in equity passed through the solvency or passed through the P&L.

items.statement: Solvency ratio was 1.61 as of March 2024; expected to exceed 200% by June 2024 post IPO capital infusion of INR 1,125 crores
items.quote: our sense is this will be more than 200%. What exactly that number would be that we will know only on 30th of June, but we expect the solvency ratio to go beyond 200% definitely.

items.statement: Raised INR 1,125 crores through IPO; net worth increased by one-third; leverage will decrease this year then resume growth
items.quote: leverage obviously will go down this year because we have raised capital of about INR 1125 crores or so. So, our net worth will suddenly increase by one third. So, the leverage will go down.

items.statement: Reserving triangles show adequate reserving across whole account, motor TP, and non-TP lines; no negative surprises philosophy
items.quote: I think for us in Digit our philosophy, for reserving is that we need to always be adequately reserved. I think having surprises on reserving, negative surprises, is something which shouldn't really happen.

items.statement: IFRS 17 audited reconciliation published; IFRS profitability from year 3; regulator not yet mandating IFRS reporting format
items.quote: as of now the regulator is not asking us or any company to publish IFRS results. And in what shape and manner would the IFRS get implemented in India or by the regulator is something which we'll have to wait and see.

items.statement: Retail health insurance ~INR 60 crores; group health dominates portfolio; health business under industry stress due to portability and waiting period dynamics
items.quote: most of our portfolio would be gro up. And retail health insurance would be a smaller number. If I remember offhand, this would be close to about INR60 crores or so for last year

items.statement: Support motor TP de-tariffing; industry priority is TP rate increase (no increase in 4 years); free pricing would shift competition from commission to price
items.quote: our view is that sooner or later, one should have de -tariffing simply because this is the only segment where there is no free pricing. Secondly, when the pricing is fixed, then people play on the commission, on the acquisition cost.

items.statement: Channel agnostic strategy; broker channel includes OEM, corporate, retail, aggregators - all with different loss ratios and acquisition costs
items.quote: we as a company are channel agnostic which basically means that we try and steer business through all possible distribution channels, looking at their own each channels, own loss ratio as well as acquisition cost.

items.statement: No target channel or product mix; market dynamics change rapidly (e.g., OEM channel fluctuates with auto sales cycles)
items.quote: there is no real channel mix which we steer towards to say in 2 years this is the channel mix which we want. Because I think again, based on our understanding of business market changes very fast.

items.statement: B2B strategy (fire, engineering, group health) combines relationships, underwriting expertise, reinsurance capacity, and claims settlement ability; earned right to win daily
items.quote: it actually becomes a mix of all of this. As far as I think right to etc etera goes, as you rightly said, we are a small player in this. But despite that, we did INR800 crores of property premium last year.

items.statement: No guidance on combined ratio trajectory; business driven by profitability not growth targets; will de-grow unprofitable segments
items.quote: we don't really -- we are not really in a position to give any guidance and nor we want to give guidance because we don't drive our business from that perspective.

items.statement: NAT CAT losses unpredictable; expect 1/3 to 1/2 of FY24 losses annually but not uniformly distributed; impact limited by growing premium base
items.quote: One would expect, I would say, half of these losses or one third of these losses to come every year. But the losses will never, ever be uniformly distributed.

items.statement: Motor TP de-growth in Q4 FY24 driven by commercial vehicles (90% TP premium); will re-enter when market corrects
items.quote: if we de-gr ew in motor third -party, you can be sure that the de -growth would have happened more because of commercial vehicles, because commercial vehicles have almost 90% of the premium coming in from third-party.

items.statement: Targeting 15% ROCE from FY27 at 80% capacity utilization
items.quote: we are targeting to achieve a ratio of almost 15%, and that we should start looking at from when we hit the capacity of, say, 80%, which we are targeting by, say, third year. So, one can safely assume that from '27, that is the return which we are looking at.

items.statement: INR 3,000 crores milestone payments for Krishnapatnam and Jodhpur completion
items.quote: out of which we will be releasing milestone payments of almost INR3,000 crores. This is the completion of Krishnapatnam as well as completion of the Marwar Jodhpur unit

items.statement: Operational capacity to reach 96 MTPA by end FY25 and 110 MTPA by FY26
items.quote: end of this year we should be hitting almost like operating capacity of say, 96 million tons and by FY26, I should be giving good news of 110 million tons.

items.statement: INR 300/ton cost efficiency upside from AFR, RE, cooler replacement and debottlenecking
items.quote: I would say about INR300 per ton cost efficiency is something very doable. And on the pricing side as you know Ambuja ACC are A category price players. So there is always a INR5 to INR10 upside on the pricing.

items.statement: Penna EBITDA/ton target INR 1,000-1,250 initially, reaching INR 1,500 with further optimization
items.quote: this number will go to INR1500, INR1000. See what we are doing at Ambuja, ACC level we are running on a cost on margin optimization program of INR550 which we had also announced in the last earnings call.

items.statement: Will apply Ambuja/ACC playbook: base brand, two premium brands, OPC and blended for B2B
items.quote: we have a very good playbook for our brands, for Ambuja and ACC. We have typically a base brand and we have two premium brands for each of the company which is the playbook we have for Pan India.

items.statement: South India demand growth expected with new AP regime; industry consolidation improving pricing discipline
items.quote: Mind you, there will be a substantial growth in large parts of the country, especially with the new regime in place in AP. I believe there should be a lot of development work. So some demand will happen there.

items.statement: Seller responsible for pending land acquisition for Jodhpur railway line and limestone; indemnification for past liabilities in place
items.quote: whatever is the pending parcels of land which will be required for the railway line and for the limestone reserves in due course, they are acquiring it. And that will be part of the overall enterprise value.

items.statement: Jodhpur 3 MTPA kiln and Krishnapatnam 2 MTPA grinding unit completion in 12 and 9 months respectively
items.quote: For Krishnapatnam, we are giving a timeline of say, nine months and Rajasthan, 12 months. Yes.

items.statement: 140 MTPA target by March 2028 on track; 20 MTPA under commissioning, 30 MTPA blueprint ready with land and mining
items.quote: we are well poised to hit our 140 million ton target, as we have been speaking in past.

items.statement: Acquisition includes 5 bulk cement terminals and 25,500 ton self-discharging cement carrier for coastal logistics
items.quote: On top of this cement capacity, we have five bulk cement terminals and one 25,500 tons self -discharging cement carrier, which will beautifully complement our coastal logistics strategy.

items.statement: INR 5-10/ton pricing upside as A-category player; INR 300/ton cost reduction from AFR, RE, group synergies
items.quote: on the pricing side as you know Ambuja ACC are A category price players. So there is always a INR5 to INR10 upside on the pricing. So if I put INR10 on pricing and INR300 on cost we are talking about INR500 EBITDA kick up from the current levels

items.statement: Entire INR 10,422 crore EV funded from internal cash; INR 10,000+ crore cash balance expected post-acquisition
items.quote: The entire acquisition will be funded through cash and cash equivalents. After all of this also, by end of this year, my estimate is that we will be holding almost INR10,000 plus crores of cash.

items.statement: South capacity utilization of leaders at 78%; Penna did 6.5-6.6 MTPA in 2022; ramp-up plan considered fair
items.quote: When I look at Penna, in 2022, Penna itself did about 6.5 million, 6.6 million. So that plus what we are doing, and we have taken a very considered ramp-up plan.

items.statement: Expects container shortage and high freight rates to continue for next 2-3 quarters, improving margins
items.quote: So, we are expecting that at least for the next 2-3 quarters, this is going to continue and I think as I mentioned that any increase in freight rates definitely also helps us improve our margins as well.

items.statement: Freight rate increases pass through to customers and improve margins due to cost-plus model
items.quote: I would say it will idea is that since we are in the cost-plus model, you know we will have to pass on this increase to our customer. So, I don't think it will have any negative impact, but definitely it will have a positive impact because any freight increase definitely also increases the overall margins as well.

items.statement: Business shifting from China to India and Vietnam will grow Indian international trade and benefit Tiger Logistics
items.quote: So, at the moment whatever is getting banned, it's getting transferred either to India or to Vietnam or to other countries. So definitely the Indian international business is going to grow and that benefit will definitely come on to us.

items.statement: Import volume mix growing from 15% currently, targeting higher share to reduce export dependence
items.quote: I think it is only increasing. We are looking at imports also contributing pretty well in the coming quarters. So that ratio is increasing. We don't want to be purely dependent on exports.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis continues with no vessels transiting; port congestion and container shortages persist due to China demand
items.quote: Few challenges I must talk to you about, of course, the Red Sea challenge continues to be there, which we cannot ignore that. Secondly, of course, the challenges in terms of the port congestion and container shortages have again hit us in India and that is primarily because of major business happening out of China.

items.statement: Shanghai-Chennai 40ft container rate surged from $800 in Feb-Mar 2024 to $4,500 currently
items.quote: I tell you in the in the month of February'24 and March'24, the 120 feet container from Shanghai to Chennai was around $800 and same container today is at $4,500, 40 feet container.

items.statement: Launched FreightJar 2.0 with global access, real-time rates, better customer experience; hiring for this vertical
items.quote: we were able to finalize the Version 2 of our logistics online platform Freight Jar which will definitely give us better access to more markets and better access to more customers & clients who are dealing in the international business.

items.statement: Won government contracts including 1-year HPCL petrochemical logistics and BHEL ODC/container shipments
items.quote: Development of the government projects business, it's doing well for us. We've got some good contracts this quarter as well.

items.statement: Overall volume grew ~17% QoQ despite lowest-ever freight rates reducing FY24 revenue to ₹24,026 lakhs from ₹43,335 lakhs
items.quote: though maybe I may have a 15% increase, 17% increase in the overall volume, but my billing has gone down because the freight itself has come down. So that is the reason for that.

items.statement: FreightJar platform operates at same 7-8% margin as core business
items.quote: The revenue model is purely what we are doing now. Since it is a sales product of Tiger Logistics, we are offering the same services through the online portal. So, the margin remains the same at 7%-8% whatever is there in our business.

items.statement: High freight rates causing some low-value product importers to hold shipments short-term
items.quote: It's not come till now but yeah, people are holding their imports because the rates have gone up so high. So, they feel that it is better to hold on, not immediately, but that impact does come in.

items.statement: Inorganic growth via LCL acquisition pending due to lack of aligned targets
items.quote: the only thing which is lacking is that we were looking at some kind of inorganic growth in terms of acquiring LCL company, which has not happened because you know we were not able to get the company which is aligned to our idea of growth.

items.statement: Robust order book exceeding INR 40 crores
items.quote: With a diverse product portfolio of over 25 SKUs and a robust order book of exceeding INR 40 crores, we serve B2B customers across defense, marine, offshore, oil and gas and other industries.

items.statement: H2 FY24 EBITDA margin 24.96%, PAT margin 14.85%
items.quote: The EBITDA was INR 10.83 crore with a Meson Valves India Ltd 3 18.06.2024 Result Conference Call robust EBITDA margin of 24.96%, reflecting operational efficiency. The notable profit after tax PAT of INR 6.44 crores with a PAT margin of 14.85% further underscores Meson's financial strength

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 23.61%, PAT margin 14.3%
items.quote: The EBITDA was INR 4.95 crore with a strong EBITDA margin of 23.61%, indicating continuous operational efficiency. The PAT was INR 9.05 crore with a PAT margin of 14.3%, underscoring Meson's financial robustness.

items.statement: Targeting sustainable 25-30% year-on-year growth
items.quote: So I think we will be able to achieve a very sustainable growth of 25%, 30% year-on-year. So that is also our target to be sustainable.

items.statement: Present CapEx around INR 15 crores as of May 2024; FY25 CapEx in planning
items.quote: Present we have around 15 CR CapEx. So we are planning yeah. Yeah. We are planning to have some more machineries, technological machine s and equipment in future so we can enhance our productivity also with the new technologies we will have increase in the ROCE

items.statement: Foundry integration and new CNC machines to increase throughput by 30-40%
items.quote: So, yeah. I can say if you just put it in numbers literally, it will be 30%, 40% increase.

items.statement: Foundry backward integration may add 3% to PAT margin once fully operational
items.quote: It is possible that the foundry will add to somewhere shares increase the margin, I think, by 3%. It is possible. Yes.

items.statement: 50-60% of revenues expected from defense sector
items.quote: 50-60% revenues will come only from defense.

items.statement: Huge surge in domestic shipbuilding and naval projects; capacity utilization was 100% for domestic demand
items.quote: Even in the coming future, we see a huge demand from the Indian local PSUs with the defense maritime, marine and as the things are progressing, we see that there is a huge surge in the local domestic shipbuilding projects, naval projects, where we have to also significantly gear up.

items.statement: H2O Dynamics water treatment venture receiving 20-25 inquiries, expecting conversion
items.quote: What I want to add that we just started, but the response from the industry is very much overwhelming, like we are getting we almost got 20, 25 inquiries right now. And most of the inquiries we are seeing that we can convert into the business.

items.statement: German filter technology for automatic cleaning; 80% Make in India, 20% parts from Germany
items.quote: Make in India. And some parts, say, around 20% parts will come from Germany, 80% of it will be made in India.

items.statement: Seasonality trend H1/H2 30-70% or 40-60% to continue for couple of years due to consolidation
